reads.title: Trump tells Zelenskyy to stop hitting Russian diesel; Nearly 80,000 displaced in Yemen; Trump rejects calls for AI guardrails
reads.subtitle: Drop Site Daily: September 14, 2026
reads.body:
- U.S. President Donald Trump speaks to reporters while aboard Air Force One while traveling back from Ireland to Joint Base Andrews, Maryland on September 13, 2026. Photo by Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images.Monday, September 14, 2026 – Ansarallah advances toward Marib, captures strategic Red Sea islands, and launches attacks at Saudi air base. World Health Organization: Nearly 3,000 casualties, over 77,000 displaced in Yemen in one week. Over 2,000 Yemenis flee to Djibouti as clashes intensify. Islamic Resistance in Iraq denies role in attack on Saudi pipeline. Iran denies interference in Yemen, involvement in attack on Saudi pipeline. Reuters: Saudi Arabia has just seven days’ worth of oil stored at Yanbu. Oil prices top $107 a barrel. U.S. officials meet with MBS, President Donald Trump claims talks with Ansarallah. One killed, four wounded in strike on Iranian vessel near Qeshm Island. Gulf-Iran meeting on Strait of Hormuz postponed at Saudi Arabia’s request, Iran says. Iran nuclear chief barred from atomic conference after Austria denies visa. Israeli attacks kill one Palestinian, wound more than a dozen across Gaza on Monday. Israeli soldiers and settlers continue to terrorize the occupied West Bank. Electricity generators failing at Gaza hospitals, Health Ministry says. Israeli forces raid Palestinian journalist home, beat son, order him to surrender. B’Tselem report documents Israel’s “eliminationist project” in the occupied West Bank. Thirty-seven Palestinian journalists currently in Israeli detention, more than half without charge or trial. Israel continues to attack southern Lebanon despite “ceasefire” framework. EPA plans to eliminate greenhouse gas limits on power plants. AI chiefs call for slowdown in AI developments. Afghan resident deported after conceding to being an “alien terrorist” in first-of-its-kind case. NSA undergoes historic restructuring under Director Joshua Rudd. Rapid Support Forces drones strike Sudan’s Ed Damazin amid fears of broader offensive. Scottish, Welsh, and Irish nationalist leaders declare right to self-determination at Cardiff summit. Trump calls for a unified Ireland. Syrians protest cost of energy, while Turkish Foreign Minister says Syria will play “vital role” in region’s energy. Sweden’s election too close to call as opposition edges ahead. 130 missing after passenger ship capsizes in Indonesia’s Java Sea. Poland, Ukraine accuse Russia of “escalation” after strike near Boris Johnson. Ukrainian drones strike two Russian oil refineries as Trump tells Kyiv to stop “causing shortage of diesel fuel.” Confirmed Ebola cases in DRC top 7,000. Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro faces corruption probe.
This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday – Friday

## Yemen

- Ansarallah advances toward Marib, captures strategic Red Sea islands: Ansarallah forces are advancing toward Saudi-backed government-held areas in Yemen, with fierce clashes reported on the outskirts of Marib, the government’s strategic oil- and gas-rich stronghold, according to Al Jazeera.

- The group is also advancing in Taiz, where government forces are relying heavily on Saudi airstrikes to prevent the city’s capture.

- Separately, Ansarallah captured the Greater and Lesser Hanish islands after hundreds of government-allied forces withdrew, AP reported. The islands lie about 160 kilometers north of Bab Al-Mandab in the southern Red Sea.

- The advances strengthen Ansarallah’s position around Bab Al-Mandab—a key route for Saudi oil shipments amid the war with Iran and blockades in the Strait of Hormuz.

- Ansarallah launches attacks at Saudi air base: Ansarallah launched dozens of ballistic missiles and drones at King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait in response to more than 300 Saudi airstrikes across Yemen over the past five days, military spokesperson Yahya Saree said Monday.

- Saree said the operation targeted fighter jet hangars, radars, runways, ammunition depots, and other military infrastructure, claiming “direct and precise” hits and significant damage.

- He warned that “any new aggression will be met with broader and more severe operations.”

- Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defense issued and lifted public warnings of potential danger in Khamis Mushait and nearby Abha three times early Monday.

- WHO: Nearly 3,000 casualties, over 77,000 displaced in Yemen in one week: At least 504 people were killed and 2,379 wounded across Yemen from September 6 to 12, according to the World Health Organization. As of September 12, at least 77,789 people had also been displaced across Taiz, Marib, al-Jawf, Lahj, Hodeidah, Abyan, and Shabwa.

- Nearly half the casualties occurred in Marib, strategic Saudi-backed government-held governorate east of Sana’a.

- Separately, Yemen’s Saudi-backed forces said more than 500 of their soldiers were killed and around 1,500 wounded in fighting with Ansarallah along the western coast from August 9 to September 10, while claiming more than 1,000 Ansarallah fighters were killed. The figures could not be independently verified.

- Over 2,000 Yemenis flee to Djibouti as clashes intensify: More than 2,000 Yemenis fleeing the fighting reached Djibouti, according to figures released Sunday by the International Organization for Migration (IOM). The number rose from around 1,400 arrivals reported a day earlier by Djibouti’s Economy and Finance Minister.

- Islamic Resistance in Iraq denies role in attack on Saudi pipeline: The Islamic Resistance in Iraq denied responsibility for a drone attack on Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline on Saturday, after the Iraqi government said the drones were launched from Iraqi territory.

- The group called responsibility for the attack “an honor we do not claim,” criticized the Iraqi government for responding before completing an investigation, and offered to join an official inquiry.

- Iraqi security forces located and seized a drone-launching platform allegedly used in the attack on the pipeline, according to the head of Iraq’s Security Media Cell. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi reshuffled military commanders in the country’s border regions following the attack, dismissing the Maysan operations commander and provincial police chief.

- Iraq also temporarily closed three border crossings with Iran—Shalamcheh, al-Shib, and Mandali—after discovering drone launch sites.

- No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.

- Iran denies interference in Yemen, involvement in attack on Saudi pipeline: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei denied that Tehran interferes in Yemeni decision-making, saying Ansarallah is “an independent Yemeni party that takes decisions based on what it considers to be its own interests and priorities.”

- Baghaei also rejected claims that Iran was involved in an attack on a Saudi oil pipeline from Iraqi territory, calling them “sheer lies” intended to deepen divisions among regional countries.

- Reuters: Saudi Arabia has just seven days’ worth of oil stored at Yanbu: Saudi Arabia has between five and seven days’ worth of oil stored in its Red Sea port city of Yanbu, three unnamed sources told Reuters on Sunday, adding that Riyadh also has a smaller amount of oil stored in Egypt.

- Saudi Arabia said it suspended its East-West pipeline after the attack as a “precautionary measure.”

- The shutdown of the pipeline, which allows exports to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, could threaten up to 4% of global oil supply.

- Oil prices top $107 a barrel: Oil prices rose more than 3% on Monday, with Brent crude futures gaining $3.21, or 3.1% percent, to reach $107.82 a barrel.

- U.S. officials meet with MBS, Trump claims talks with Ansarallah: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) met U.S. Central Command chief Admiral Brad Cooper and discussed the latest developments in the Gulf, Saudi state television reported on Monday.

- Trump, who spoke with MBS on Thursday and reportedly declined to intervene directly against Ansarallah, called MBS “a good friend of mine” when asked about their relationship on Saturday, and told reporters that “everything’s going to work out fine and dandy.”

- In the same remarks, he claimed that he had received a call from Ansarallah, who he said “don’t want to fight” the U.S., and that they were “letting most ships go through” the Bab Al-Mandab strait. “There’s one country they’re not too happy with,” he said, likely referring to Israel or Saudi Arabia, before promising to get the matter “straightened out.”

## Iran

- One killed, four wounded in strike on Iranian vessel near Qeshm Island: One person was killed and four others were wounded, including two Pakistani citizens, after an Iranian cargo vessel came under attack near Qeshm Island early Sunday.

- Iranian state broadcaster IRIB, citing Qeshm’s governor, said the vessel was attacked by the “U.S. terrorist enemy.”

- Separately, a fire broke out on a commercial vessel struck in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday evening, forcing its crew to abandon ship, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations monitoring outfit.

- Gulf-Iran meeting on Strait of Hormuz postponed at Saudi Arabia’s request, Iran says: A planned meeting between Iran and Gulf states on the future of the Strait of Hormuz was postponed after Saudi Arabia requested a delay, according to Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei, a claim Riyadh has yet to confirm.

- A regional official told AP that Saudi Arabia had proposed amendments over concerns the agreement could have lasting implications for other Gulf states.

- Baghaei called reported citing of the situation in Yemen a “flimsy pretext” and said an Iran-Oman agreement concerning the Strait had already been finalized. “Had this meeting taken place, it would have been a very suitable opportunity [to discuss the new policy].”

- Bahrain declined to participate in the meeting beforehand, arguing regional security “cannot be preserved through a policy of appeasement” and ruling out a collective meeting with Iran before their diplomatic ties were restored.

- Iran nuclear chief barred from atomic conference after Austria denies visa: Iranian nuclear chief Mohammad Eslami was unable to attend the International Atomic Energy Agency conference in Vienna after Austria denied him a visa. Iran’s Foreign Ministry said Austria claimed it acted under U.S. pressure.

- Baghaei also dismissed claims about activity at Mount Kolang (Pickaxe Mountain) near Natanz as U.S. “media and psychological warfare.”

- IAEA chief Rafael Grossi said there were “some indications” of activity at the site but acknowledged the agency had no “concrete information.”

- IRGC claims downing of U.S. MQ-1 drone over Strait of Hormuz: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said Monday its Aerospace Force intercepted and downed an advanced U.S. MQ-1 drone over the Strait of Hormuz, IRNA reported.

- South Korea, U.S. to discuss possible Korean military deployment to Strait of Hormuz: South Korea and the U.S. will hold senior-level defense talks this week to discuss a possible South Korean military deployment to the Strait of Hormuz, Yonhap reported. South Korea last week sent a team to the UAE to assess the security situation near the strait.

- Iran and UAE sign joint BRICS statement calling for restraint in war: Iran and the United Arab Emirates signed a joint BRICS statement calling for restraint in the war. Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian also met with Abu ⁠Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al ‌Nahyan on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in New Delhi—the highest level meeting between the two countries since the start of the war.

- “We express deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in Middle East/West Asia [and] call for exercising maximum restraint, as well as avoiding actions that could further aggravate the situation,” the joint BRICS declaration read.

- U.S. authorities claim Iran used Chinese satellite images in attack on Jordan base: Unnamed U.S. officials told the Wall Street Journal that they believe Iran obtained high-resolution satellite images from Chinese sources before Iran’s July attack on Jordan’s Muwaffaq Salti airbase that killed three American soldiers, calling it the “clearest” evidence yet of Chinese support for Tehran during the war.

- The unnamed officials declined to identify the specific Chinese entity involved and stopped short of directly accusing Beijing.

- Trump brushed aside the report, telling reporters on Sunday that, “they basically do what we do... when they say China spies on us, I say you’re right, and we spy on them too.”

- Asked whether he would raise the issue with Chinese President Xi Jinping at their planned September 24 meeting, Trump reiterated that he has “a good relationship” with Xi and that “he’s behaved reasonably well, and we behave reasonably well.”

- A spokesperson for China’s Foreign Ministry rejected the accusations as “groundless.”

- Iran seizes property from 240 people accused of ties to Israel: Iranian authorities seized property belonging to 240 people accused of affiliations with Israel and other hostile countries, according to Iran Wire. The judiciary accused them of carrying out “propaganda or practical actions against the country” that caused extensive infrastructure damage. Under an expanded espionage law passed last year, assisting the U.S., Israel, or other hostile states can carry the death penalty.

## Palestine

- Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, two Palestinians were killed and 25 injured in attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.

- The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,786 killed, with 174,771 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,372 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,659, while 831 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble.

- Israeli attacks kill one Palestinian, wound more than a dozen across Gaza: Israeli forces shot and killed a Palestinian in the Al-Mawasi area west of Rafah on Monday, according to WAFA.

- In Gaza City, an Israeli drone struck a tent sheltering displaced Palestinians, wounding more than 10 people, several seriously.

- In central Gaza, an Israeli drone struck a group of Palestinians near the Egyptian Committee headquarters in Al-Zawayda, leaving several wounded, some seriously.

- Another Israeli drone strike west of Khan Younis wounded several Palestinians, including one seriously.

- Israel continues to kill in Gaza throughout the weekend:

- Sunday: An Israeli strike targeted a vehicle in Gaza City’s Tel Al-Hawa neighborhood, killing two Palestinians and wounding 13, according to the Palestinian Red Crescent. Drop Site contributor Abdel Qader Sabbah spoke to witnesses at the scene of the attack; one Palestinian man at the site held up household items in the car and asked, “Are these rockets? Are these guns?” Sabbah’s dispatch is available here.

- Saturday: Israeli warplanes injured 13 Palestinians, including children, in two strikes near Khan Younis on Saturday, according to WAFA. Separately on Saturday, a pregnant woman and her unborn baby died from wounds sustained three days earlier from Israeli gunfire south of Khan Younis. Drop Site’s Mohamed Ahmed spoke to the victim’s family. “We sit in fear. We sleep in fear. We walk in fear. Everything is fear,” her mother-in-law told him. His video report is available here.

- Israeli soldiers and settlers continue to terrorize the occupied West Bank:

- Ramallah: Israeli settlers with three bulldozers began carving a road through olive-planted land west of Ni’lin on Monday for a new settlement outpost, WAFA reported.

- Hebron: Israeli forces shot and wounded a Palestinian after pursuing his vehicle in Beit Ula, then deliberately set the vehicle on fire.

- Tulkarm: Israeli special forces opened fire at the vehicle of Mohammed Shahada, 46, secretary of Fatah in Tulkarm refugee camp, before detaining him. On Sunday, medics received a 27-year-old Palestinian who had been shot in the foot by Israeli forces.

- Bethlehem: Israeli forces detained two children, aged 14 and 15, during a raid on Bethlehem on Sunday, WAFA reported. Separately, Israeli forces opened fire in the Kremzan area of Beit Jala, wounding two Palestinian workers en route to their workplace in Jerusalem.

- Jenin: Israeli forces shot and wounded two Palestinian farmers in the village of Fuqqu’a, according to Al Jazeera. Israeli soldiers reportedly opened fire after settlers let livestock loose on the Palestinian farmers’ property and a group of Palestinians tried to stop them.

- Salfit: Israeli settlers beat two Palestinian men on agricultural land in Salfit on Sunday, severely injuring them.

- Tubas: Israeli forces detained five members of the Bani Odeh family from Tammun, south of Tubas, early Sunday, according to the Prisoners’ Society in Tubas. The family members were detained as a means of pressuring another son to turn himself in to Israeli authorities, the Society reported.

- East Jerusalem: Israeli forces opened fire in the Silwan neighborhood in East Jerusalem on Saturday, moderately injuring a Palestinian man near the Al-Aqsa mosque.

- Electricity generators failing at Gaza hospitals, Health Ministry says: Several electricity generators at hospitals in the Gaza Strip are no longer working due to shortages of spare parts and fuel, the Strip’s Health Ministry told Al Jazeera, noting the small quantities of fuel that Israel allows into Gaza were sufficient only for emergency needs. Read Mohanad El-Hemrwawi’s report for Drop Site on the collapse of Gaza’s strained network of generators here.

- Israeli forces raid Palestinian journalist home, beat son, order him to surrender: Israeli forces raided the Jenin home of prominent Palestinian journalist Ali Al-Samoudi, beat his son Majd, and gave Al-Samoudi one hour to turn himself in. He was not home at the time.

- The raid comes months after Al-Samoudi was released in April 2026 after a year in Israeli detention without charge. He emerged having lost half his body weight—from 120 kg to 60.

- When Israeli forces arrested him, they broke down his door and beat him and his wife. He was held for 80 hours handcuffed and blindfolded and severely beaten on his way to Megiddo prison.

- Al-Samoudi was also shot while reporting alongside Al Jazeera journalist Shireen Abu Akleh during an Israeli raid on Jenin refugee camp in May 2022. Abu Akleh was killed by Israeli forces during that raid.

- B’Tselem report documents Israel’s “eliminationist project” in the occupied West Bank: The Israeli human rights organization B’Tselem released a lengthy new report entitled “The Elimination Project” on Monday, detailing Israel’s “systematic effort to dismantle Palestinian collective existence in the West Bank.”

- The report says this effort has accelerated since the current government took office in December 2022 and especially since October 7, 2023, identifying five interconnected mechanisms used by Israeli forces in the territory: violence and intimidation, movement restrictions, economic strangulation, social and political destruction, and ethnic cleansing and territorial takeover.

- Israel has established 200 new checkpoints since October 7, 2023, the report finds, seized about 18% of Palestinian land in the occupied West Bank through settlements and illegal outposts, and depopulated 64 Palestinian shepherding communities.

- B’Tselem’s full report is available here.

- 37 Palestinian journalists currently in Israeli detention, more than half without charge or trial: The Palestinian Prisoner’s Society (PPS) reported on Sunday that 37 Palestinian journalists arrested since October 2023 remain in Israeli detention, more than half of them—19—held without charge or trial under administrative detention.

- Among them is Drop Site contributor Mohamed Awad, detained by the Israeli military from his home in Beitunia, near Ramallah, on August 12 and ordered to be held for four months without charge.

- The group also noted the case of female journalist Bushra al-Taweel, who was recently transferred to solitary confinement in Ramleh Prison, amid escalating repressive measures against female Palestinian prisoners.

- Palestinian prisoners’ rights group reports deteriorating health conditions at Ofer, Janot prisons: The Commission of Detainees and Ex-Detainees Affairs reported Sunday a deterioration in the health and humanitarian conditions at Israel’s Ofer and Janot prisons.

- The group highlighted the case of 60-year-old Maher Naasan from Al-Mughayyir village, who was detained on July 6 and, according to testimonies from released prisoners, was severely beaten, had cigarettes extinguished on his body, and was held for hours under the sun.

- Palestinian prisoners at Ofer described outbreaks of scabies, insufficient cleaning supplies and clothing, cell raids, confiscation of belongings, and deliberate prevention of communal prayers by prison authorities.

- In Janot prison, the commission noted the case of Osama Fatahallah Al-Shenni, detained since 2024, who suffers from a herniated disc and has been denied painkillers despite severe pain, and has lost 35 kilograms since his detention.

- Trump defends Witkoff, Kushner work in Gaza, says Hamas ready to disarm: Speaking to reporters aboard Air Force One, Trump lauded the success of his Middle East envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, saying, “look at the fact that we got all of the hostages back.”

- He also claimed that “there’s not a lot of fighting in Gaza,” and that Hamas “is now willing to give up their weapons.”

- Israel has killed more than 1,370 Palestinians since the so-called ceasefire and has continued to push further into Gaza, occupying more of the Strip’s land.

- Trump made similar comments during his visit to Ireland on Saturday, saying that his administration had “put out the fire in Gaza” and calling their world “quite amazing.”

- Israeli minister vows to revoke citizenship of filmmakers behind Gaza documentary: Israeli Culture Minister Miki Zohar said on Sunday that he would move “immediately” to revoke the citizenship of filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor after their documentary “NAZA,” about “Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza,” won the Special Jury Prize at the Venice Film Festival.

- Zohar called the film “vile” and accused the pair of “treason against the state” in a post on X.

- Netanyahu to visit U.S. from September 23-25: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is scheduled to visit New York City for the United Nations General Assembly, arriving in the U.S. on Wednesday, September 23 and leaving on Friday, September 25th, his office told the Times of Israel. He is expected to speak before the body on the 24th. Netanyahu has an outstanding arrest warrant issued against him by the International Criminal Court for war crimes and crimes against humanity for Israel’s war on Gaza.

## Lebanon

- Israel continues to attack southern Lebanon despite “ceasefire” framework:

- Monday: Israeli forces opened heavy machine-gun fire toward the outskirts of Chaqra and Baraachit in the Bint Jbeil district, intimidating residents who had attempted to return to their homes, Lebanon’s National News Agency reported.

- Sunday: Israeli warplanes carried out two strikes on Mansouri in the Tyre district, struck the outskirts of Haris in the Bint Jbeil district, and targeted an area between Mayfadoun and Zawtar Al-Sharqiya in the Nabatieh district.

- Lebanese President visits Nabatieh as talks with Israel postponed: Joseph Aoun, President of Lebanon, visited Nabatieh city on Saturday, surrounded by soldiers providing a military escort. Nearly 30 people have been killed in the southern Lebanese city since early September.

- The visit follows reports by Axios’s Barak Ravid that talks between Lebanon and Israel scheduled to take place in Rome next week have been postponed to October.

## U.S. News

- EPA plans to eliminate greenhouse gas limits on power plants: The Trump administration plans to announce Monday that the U.S. will no longer regulate greenhouse gas emissions from power plants, according to the New York Times.

- EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin is expected to announce the change during a G20 energy ministers meeting in Houston, arguing that greenhouse gases from power plants do not endanger human health or the environment and therefore fall outside the agency’s authority under the Clean Air Act—a legal position that, if upheld by courts, could prevent future administrations from restoring such regulations.

- The Biden-era rule it replaces had been projected to generate $120 billion in public health benefits by 2047, including preventing up to 1,200 premature deaths and 360,000 asthma attacks annually by 2035.

- Social Security COLA projected at 3.6% for 2027: Government inflation data released Friday points to a 3.6% Social Security cost-of-living adjustment for next year, according to an AARP forecast, which would mark the largest increase since 2023’s 3.2% (this year’s COLA was 2.8%).

- The official COLA, determined by averaging July, August, and September figures from the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers, will be announced October 14. The adjustment will apply starting in January to benefits for 75.7 million Americans.

- Trump discusses interest rates ahead of Fed meeting: President Donald Trump reiterated Sunday in Ireland that the U.S. should have the lowest interest rates in the world “regardless of their formulas,” even as data released Friday showed consumer prices rose more than expected in August, pushing traders to price in an 86% chance of a Federal Reserve rate hike this month and two increases by year’s end.

- When asked whether he expected the central bank to raise rates at its upcoming meeting, Trump said “I don’t know,” while suggesting Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s hands may be tied by what Trump has called a “very political” board of governors.

- Trump also restated an earlier threat to cut off trade with countries the U.S. has a trade deficit with if the Fed doesn’t lower rates, telling reporters “yeah, I’m going to do that with some nations” and that it “will take place over a period of time,” though it remains unclear how such a move would influence Fed policy.

- AI chiefs call for slowdown in AI developments: The chief executive of artificial intelligence company Anthropic, Dario Amodei, published a 3,800-word open letter on Saturday calling for a slowdown in the development of A.I., with increased guardrails and oversight. The letter prompted the heads of other leading A.I. companies, including  OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, and the chair of Google DeepMind Demis Hassabis, to speak out in agreement.

- In his letter, Amodei pointed to the hack of Hugging Face by hundreds of autonomous AI agents: “Given the accelerating rate of AI capability development, it’s my worry that in 6–12 months such a swarm could be capable of taking over the entire internet with a persistent botnet (potentially causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage), and that the scale of damage would continue to increase from there if AI becomes more powerful without the necessary guardrails,” he wrote.

- President Donald Trump on Monday posted on Truth Social: “The only control or “guardrails” that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades! The Trump Administration has stopped AI ‘people’ from doing bad, or potentially bad, ‘things,’ like Dario (Anthropic!), who is now pretending to be a ‘perfect little angel’ - and we will continue to do so!” He continued: “There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China. WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS! We are leadi

reads.title: DE HENRY FORD À RFK JR. : LA LIGNE N'A JAMAIS ÉTÉ ROMPUE
reads.subtitle: Ce que l'aveu d'un Secrétaire d'État américain révèle sur un siècle de mécanique occidentale Marco | Independent Analyst *14 septembre 2026
reads.body:
## Introduction : ce qui a changé
Pendant trois ans, l’Occident a nié une évidence. L’Ukraine n’est pas un pays qui se défend. C’est un proxy. Un intermédiaire. Un instrument.
Nous l’avons écrit. Nous l’avons documenté. Nous l’avons répété. Et nous avons été qualifiés de « pro-russes », de « complotistes », de « désinformateurs » — précisément par les structures que nous documentions.
Le 13 septembre 2026, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Secrétaire à la Santé et aux Services Humains des États-Unis, l’a dit à voix haute chez Tucker Carlson :

> « Cela n’a rien à voir avec la démocratie. L’Ukraine est un proxy. 113 milliards de dollars. »
Et il a ajouté ce que nous savions depuis 2022 : l’accord d’Istanbul a été saboté. Par Boris Johnson. Avec l’aval de Washington.
Ce n’est pas une révélation. C’est une confirmation.
Mais la vraie question n’est pas « pourquoi maintenant ? ». La vraie question est : pourquoi a-t-il fallu attendre un Secrétaire en exercice pour entendre ce que les documents disaient depuis 80 ans ?
Parce que la ligne n’a jamais été rompue. Elle va de Henry Ford à RFK Jr.
Voici la ligne.

## I. Henry Ford — le premier maillon
En 1938, Henry Ford reçoit la Grand-Croix de l’Ordre de l’Aigle allemand — la plus haute distinction que le régime nazi accorde à un étranger. La même année, il accepte une décoration similaire de Mussolini.
Ford n’était pas un observateur passif. Ses filiales allemandes (Ford-Werke) ont produit des véhicules militaires pour la Wehrmacht pendant toute la guerre. Des travailleurs forcés y ont été employés. Le régime nazi a reçu, via Ford, un soutien industriel direct.
Après-guerre : rien. Aucune poursuite. Aucun procès. Aucune conséquence. Ford est mort en 1947, couvert d’honneurs, célébré comme un génie américain.
Ce n’est pas un détail. C’est le premier maillon d’un mécanisme : l’industrie occidentale finance, arme, et sert des régimes autoritaires — puis efface la trace.

## II. JP Morgan, Prescott Bush — la finance et le scandale effacé
➡️ Le plan Dawes (1924) et le plan Young (1929) — orchestration de la finance anglo-américaine (JP Morgan, notamment) pour restructurer la dette allemande et financer l’industrialisation du pays. Le régime qui en bénéficiera est celui qui, dix ans plus tard, déclenchera la guerre.
➡️ Prescott Bush (père de George H.W. Bush, grand-père de George W. Bush) — directeur de la Union Banking Corporation, saisie en 1942 sous le Trading with the Enemy Act pour liens financiers avec le régime nazi. Les actifs ont été confisqués. Le nom Bush, lui, est devenu une dynastie présidentielle.
Le scandale s’efface. Le nom reste.

## III. Operation Paperclip — les nazis récompensés
Entre 1945 et 1959, plus de 1 600 scientifiques, ingénieurs et techniciens nazis sont intégrés dans l’appareil militaro-industriel américain.

- Wernher von Braun — ancien officier SS, concepteur des V-2, devient directeur du programme spatial américain.

- Hubertus Strughold — médecin nazi impliqué dans des expériences sur des détenus de Dachau, devient « père de la médecine spatiale » américaine.
Pas jugés. Pas poursuivis. Récompensés.
Le mécanisme : ce qui servait l’Empire ne se jugeait pas. Ce qui servait l’Empire se récupérait.

## IV. Operation Gladio — les attentats false flag
En 1948, l’OTAN met en place des réseaux stay-behind dans toute l’Europe de l’Ouest : l’Operation Gladio.
Objectif officiel : résistance en cas d’invasion soviétique.
Objectif réel : contrôle politique. Les réseaux Gladio ont été impliqués dans des attentats attribués à la gauche ou à l’extrême-gauche, pour déstabiliser les partis communistes et justifier un durcissement sécuritaire.

- Attentat de la gare de Bologne (2 août 1980) — 85 morts, 200 blessés. Attribué initialement aux Brigades Rouges, puis aux néo-fascistes, avec des liens documentés aux services secrets et à Gladio.

- Strage di Peteano (1972), Strage di Piazza Fontana (1969) — même schéma.
Le président italien Francesco Cossiga a publiquement reconnu l’existence de Gladio en 1990. Le Parlement italien a ouvert une enquête. Les conclusions sont publiques.
La ligne se poursuit.

## V. Operation Mockingbird — les médias comme instrument
Dans les années 1950-1970, la CIA a infiltré, financé et orienté des dizaines de médias occidentaux : Operation Mockingbird.
Journalistes payés, rédacteurs en chef recrutés, agences de presse noyautées. L’objectif : façonner la perception publique de la guerre froide, du tiers-monde, des mouvements de libération.
L’enquête du Church Committee (1975) a partiellement révélé le programme. Carl Bernstein, du Washington Post, a publié en 1977 une enquête intitulée « The CIA and the Media », documentant plus de 400 journalistes en relation avec la CIA.
Le programme n’a jamais été officiellement arrêté. Il a été rebaptisé.

## VI. Integrity Initiative — l’héritier direct
En 2015, l’Institute for Statecraft, organisation écossaise affiliée à la NATO Public Diplomacy Division et au programme « Prevent » du ministère de l’Intérieur britannique, lance l’Integrity Initiative.
Objectif déclaré : « réponse occidentale coordonnée à la désinformation russe ».
Objectif réel : opération d’influence multinationale.

## Financements documentés
SourceMontantUK Foreign & Commonwealth Office (via CSSF)~£2 millionsUS State Department£250 000NATO HQ Public Diplomacy£168 000Facebook£100 000

## Structure
Clusters actifs en Espagne, France, Allemagne, Italie, Grèce, Pays-Bas, Lituanie, Norvège, Serbie, Monténégro. Plans d’expansion vers les États-Unis, le Canada, et la région MENA.

## Tactiques documentées

- Opération Moncloa (Espagne, 2018) — campagne de discrédit contre Pedro Baños pour bloquer sa nomination à la sécurité nationale.

- Ciblage de Jeremy Corbyn — argent public utilisé pour contrer le Labour Party.

- Opération Iris (Skripal) — surveillance des réseaux sociaux, ciblage d’influenceurs en Italie.

- Anne Applebaum — membre du « UK Inner Core ».

## Issue
L’Institute for Statecraft a été fermé par le régulateur caritatif écossais. Le Foreign Office n’a jamais nié l’authenticité des leaks.
Comme l’a résumé le professeur David Miller (Université de Bristol) :

> « C’est une initiative qui prétend lutter contre la désinformation et qui semble elle-même pratiquer la désinformation ! »

## VII. Ukraine 2022 — le dernier chapitre (jusqu’ici)
Mars-avril 2022. Négociations d’Istanbul.
Un accord de paix était sur la table. Selon plusieurs sources (dont Naftali Bennett, ancien Premier ministre israélien, médiateur à l’époque), un cadre était proche d’être signé :

- Ukraine neutre

- Garanties de sécurité internationales

- Retrait russe progressif

- Intégrité territoriale ukrainienne préservée
Boris Johnson arrive à Kiev. Mission : tuer l’accord.
Ce qui suit est documenté :

- $113 milliards engagés par les États-Unis

- Objectif 1 : changement de régime à Moscou

- Objectif 2 : épuisement de l’armée russe

- Objectif 3 : maintien d’un conflit contrôlé, pas d’une victoire ukrainienne
L’Ukraine, elle, n’a jamais été l’objectif. Elle a été le moyen.
Et RFK Jr., en septembre 2026, le dit publiquement.

## VIII. Le mécanisme Göring — pourquoi ça fonctionne
Le 18 avril 1946, dans sa cellule de Nuremberg, Hermann Göring explique à Gustave Gilbert (psychologue américain) comment fonctionne le consentement de masse :

> « Naturellement, le peuple ne veut pas la guerre. Mais les dirigeants peuvent toujours l’imposer. Il suffit de dire aux gens qu’ils sont attaqués, de dénoncer les pacifistes comme traîtres, et de dénoncer toute opposition comme un danger pour la nation. Cela fonctionne dans tous les pays. »
Le mécanisme :

- Menacer d’une attaque externe

- Dénoncer les pacifistes comme traîtres

- Obtenir la conformité
Ce n’est pas de l’histoire. C’est de la mécanique. Et elle est documentée.
Pendant trois ans, quiconque demandait la paix en Ukraine était qualifié de « pro-russe ». Quiconque documentait les accords sabotés était « désinformateur ». Quiconque remarquait que Gladio existait était « complotiste ».
Le mécanisme fonctionne. Il fonctionne encore.

## IX. Ce qui a changé
Trois facteurs expliquent pourquoi RFK Jr. peut dire aujourd’hui ce qui était indicible il y a trois ans :

- Internet — les leaks, les documents, les archives sont accessibles. Le DPG-1992, le memorandum Baker-Gorbachev, les Integrity Initiative leaks de 2018 : tout est là.

- Un Secrétaire en exercice — ce n’est plus un blogueur, un analyste indépendant, ou un ancien fonctionnaire. C’est un membre du cabinet américain.

- Le calendrier politique — les midterms de novembre 2026 approchent. La guerre en Ukraine est impopulaire. L’aveu sert aussi des intérêts politiques.
Mais peu importe pourquoi il parle. Ce qui compte, c’est ce qui est dit.

## X. La ligne, résumée
PériodeMécanismeConséquence1930sHenry Ford, JP Morgan, Prescott BushSoutien industriel au régime nazi1945-1959Operation Paperclip1 600 nazis intégrés, récompensés1948-1990Operation GladioAttentats false flag, contrôle politique1950s-1970sOperation MockingbirdInfiltration des médias occidentaux2015-2018Integrity InitiativeOpération d’influence multinationale2022-2026UkraineProxy assumé, accord saboté, $113 mds
Ce n’est pas une théorie. C’est un modèle.

## Conclusion : pourquoi la ligne compte
RFK Jr. n’a pas inventé la vérité. Il l’a rendue publique.
Ce que nous avons documenté pendant trois ans n’était pas une opinion. C’était une archive. Ce qui a changé, ce n’est pas la réalité. C’est la visibilité.
La question n’est plus « est-ce vrai ? ». La question est : pourquoi a-t-il fallu tant de temps ?
Parce que la ligne n’a jamais été rompue.
De Henry Ford à RFK Jr. — un siècle.
Et elle continue.

reads.title: Weekend Update #202: Zelensky Tweets The War
reads.subtitle: The War Is Getting More Brutal Now; Ukraine Showing Greater Adaptability In The Land War; Is Zelensky Fooling Himself About The USA?
reads.body:
Hello All,
Sometimes deciding how to frame these weekend updates can be a challenge. There are usually a number of important issues that need discussing each week, and choosing the ones to highlight and the balance of time to spend on each (I want to keep these updates to a somewhat reasonable length) is no easy matter. This week was shaping up to be one of those very tricky weeks, as there were a number of subjects that could each be given a great deal of attention—from the growing, intense, ranged attacks on each side, to the Ukrainians retaking a sizable chunk of land near Lyman, to the ongoing Ukrainian dilemma of what to do with the Trump administration.
And then I was reading through Zelensky’s tweets, and he highlighted all these issues in quick succession. Indeed, Zelensky (or more accurately his team) have been engaged in a relative tweet storm lately. Over the last three days, they have been pumping out messages at a pace that I have not seen before.  There has been lots on Zelensky’s visit to Canada, to air defense, ranged strike, the shipment of food through the Black Sea, etc.
And many of these tweets were extremely illuminating about Ukrainian concerns and how the Ukrainian government sees the war. I thought it made sense, therefore, to use Zelensky’s own framing of the issues—which were a combination of messages to his people, statements/pleas to Ukraine’s partners, and even signals to the Kremlin—to summarize the week. He did it better than I ever could.

-
- Zelensky Just Tweeted Out This Picture For A PurposeSo we have a weekend update brought to you by Volodymyr Zelensky.
Phillips’s Newsletter is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.

## The War Is Getting More Brutal Now
In last weekend’s update I mentioned how the ranged war is poised to get extremely brutal this Fall and Winter.
This was not to say that it was not already getting extremely brutal. As it was, this week has given us a taste of true brutality, brutality that will only get worse. For the Ukrainians, this has meant an almost continuous series of attacks (Kyiv seems to be being bombarded both day and night, these days). These regular Russian attacks are needless to say a main preoccupation of Zelensky’s.
Only a few hours ago he focussed on their effects on Odesa. This was aimed at both the Ukrainian people and Ukraine’s partners. If Russia is allowed to continue bombarding Ukraine in this way, without a response from those who support Ukraine, the Ukrainians are clearly threatening escalation.
And really it is a very difficult time for the Ukrainians. The Russians have not only the great advantage of being able to bombard Ukraine with ballistic missiles that the Ukrainians are struggling to intercept (thanks USA!), they have been able to scale up production of jet-powered Gerans which gives them a cheaper weapon that can be sent up in mass waves.
This specific Russian development was highlighted by Eric Schmidt, former Google CEO, in an op-ed in the Washington Post, which was entitled Ukraine’s way of fighting war can’t match what’s coming. Schmidt highlights how he believes Ukraine will struggle with Russian mass production of ranged attack systems, as the Ukrainians will find it very difficult to produce effective interception systems.
This is an extremely pressing issue. The jet powered Geran-3s individually could be a system with which Ukraine can cope. Again, Zelensky actually tweeted about them in the last few days.
 The Ukrainians have actually been working on interception systems for a while (when I was in Ukraine in January, Come Back Alive discussed these).  However, it is the numbers that you need to pay attention to. If the Russians can manufacture these in the mass that seems possible, and the Ukrainian interception system cannot, that means extreme brutality. These are the systems that can be sent against individual gas stations, office windows, etc.
I will write more about this in the piece on how the war ends from the Ukrainian perspective, the follow up to the Russian piece. My hope is that this is released at the end of this coming week.
Now Zelensky also referred to another Ukrainian response that could happen if their interception systems struggle, and this is also something I have tried to prepare you for. And that is the expansion of Ukraine’s own ranged campaign against Russian power generation and heating. If the Ukrainians have no consistent ability to defend themselves against Russian attacks, then responding in kind (which they can do) becomes a great option.
Zelensky made that threat extremely openly in this tweet from September 11. It was based on how Ukraine can respond to Russian ranged attack. Note the open threat—if Russia is going to “strike our energy system” this winter, “Russian will receive the same in return.”

-
- This looks like we are locked into a spiral of escalation. Both sides in this war are improving in their ability to strike at range, and both are struggling with air defense. Remember, as Zelensky also pointed out in the last few days, the Ukrainians are constantly extending the ranges of their attacks into Russia. They are hitting war industry targets thousands of kilometres from Ukraine.
This was just one example of Zelensky in the last two days talking about improving Ukrainian long-range strike. Here is another.
So both sides are set to kick the crap out of each other. The problem Ukraine faces is that Russia is less inhibited and has ballistic missiles Ukraine lacks entirely and new jet powered drones that pose a constant problem. Ukraine’s response, as Zelensky states, might have to be to escalate in kind.
Share

## Ukraine Showing Greater Adaptability In The Land War
Just a few hours ago, Zelensky, in another tweet about the ongoing Russian air attacks, mentioned that one of the reasons he believes they are doing this is that the Russians “cannot achieve success” in the land war.
Now this is almost certainly a reference to successful Ukrainian ground operations to push the Russians back from near the town of Lyman in the Donbas.
This operation is one that you will hear more about in the coming weeks. The Ukrainians have methodically been liberating territory near Lyman, some reports are up to 250 square miles of territory so far, but are keeping it extremely quiet for reasons of operational security (the Ukrainians have become very good at that—they only will announce successes once they feel a phase of campaign is over). That was what they did earlier this summer when they took back a chunk of land at the centre of the line—which I laid out in the weekend update from two weeks ago.
The Ukrainian advance near Lyman is notable because Putin had been assured by his own commanders that the town was basically in Russian hands already—and he had even boasted about it.  And I can assure you that there are excellent sources telling me that Putin has been given such wildly optimistic reports (from the Russian perspective) specifically about the Lyman area but also about the forward progress of the Russian Army throughout the land war.
I am personally waiting for Deep State to update their map (they wait until they feel they will not jeopardize Ukrainian operations before doing so) before saying exactly how much territory has been liberated. So far they have not made an adjustment—so for now they believe the operation is still continuing. However, there are some stories being written if you want to read more reports.
What is important about this operation is that it shows the Ukrainians have the ability to advance without taking mass casualties. They are doing, from what we can tell, exactly what General Havrylov said they would do in this interview with me from last December.
The Ukrainians operate with small numbers of well-trained and motivated forces, with close coordination with masses of drones and with excellent communications. It is about being as precise and accurate as possible—to move forward by knowing where a soldier must go and what he might encounter on the way. It is the opposite of the Russian strategy of wasting mass manpower on the assumption that a few soldiers might be lucky enough to make it a few yards ahead and seize territory.
Note, Russian casualties remain shockingly high. The daily losses yesterday were over 1500, which really is a stunning number. And British intelligence has just confirmed that they estimate that Russian military dead are now over half a million for the war.
So the adaptability balance in the land war continues to favor Ukraine. That shows at least one reason why Zelensky is now focussed on the Russian ranged war.
Share

## Is Zelensky Fooling Himself About The USA?
Zelensky’s desperation for more anti-air help, in particular Patriots, has been appearing regularly in his tweets over the last few days. This was most obvious in this tweet on September 12.

-
- There is a lot going on here. Zelensky is expressly saying that Ukraine is much more efficient in its use of anti air systems. The American standard of two anti-air missiles per incoming ballistic missile is something Ukraine could not afford. They would try a one for one exchange—and they would try to prioritize targets so that they were used on  Russian missiles that the Ukrainians conclude are particularly dangerous.
Zelensky’s plea for 100-120 interceptors (remember the US might have fired up to 60 the other night defending bases in Jordan), is, as he seems to understand, a tall (arguably impossible) ask from the Trump administration. There is no “political will” in the administration to provide such aid to Ukraine, no matter what Zelensky says. Zelensky has a hard time admitting that.
Zelensky also seems to have some hope that Trump would support strong sanctions on Russia, and rather hopefully mentioned the Graham bill as providing an opportunity for Trump to stand up to Putin.

-
- I do not know if these hopes are real from Zelensky—but he does continue to manifest them publicly. I really do hope that the Ukrainians are not basing their war plans on significant help from the USA.
Have a good rest of the weekend everyone.
Thanks for reading Phillips’s Newsletter! This post is public so feel free to share it.
Share

reads.title: Surprising Yemen
reads.subtitle: Who knew that the “Houthi” parts were so green and lush?
reads.body:
Zoom in on Google Earth, or search Google images, and you will be amazed by the extensive terrace farming across Western Yemen. All these hand-made rock walls, built to trap the rainfall on level terrace fields, took many generations to build. The people who live here feel a connection to the land and to the ancestors who constructed them is immeasurable. Not only are the "Houthis" (aka Ansar Allah) mountain people, they are farmers with a deep commitment to their land and their way of life.
Don’t get me wrong, terrace farming is driven by geology and rainfall patterns, and was developed from China to Peru over millennia. My point is that these terraces form a visible and vital connection between the living farmers who maintain and work them today, and the ancients who first built them. This makes their connection to these lands uniquely powerful.
Please see the photos and links that follow.

-
- This rich agricultural area is not just some tiny bit of Yemen, it’s a lot of land, and it’s where most of the population is concentrated. Just scroll around on Google Earth to the west and north of Sana’a, the capital of Yemen, and you will see what I mean. This is one screen capture. You will see hundreds of mountains covered with terrace farming like this one. Note the mosque and grocery store.

-
- Google has not gotten around to driving these roads with their camera cars to make street views.  It’s probably not the safest project among suspicious mountain folk who have been subjected to decades of a starvation blockade. But Saudi Arabia can’t blockade all these rich and fertile terraces, so the Yemenis can’t be completely starved into submission.
From Grok: "Mocha (Al-Mukha) was the historic Red Sea port that exported Yemeni Arabica coffee from the 15th–17th centuries, giving the beans their name. Traditional Mocha coffee has no added chocolate; its natural dark-chocolate notes come from the beans and dry processing. Modern café mochas add chocolate made from cacao, a crop native to the Americas."
[Ansar Allah recently captured / liberated the port city of Mocha]

-
- There is an outstanding article here, it’s where I found the above image.
The Ultimate Guide to Yemeni Coffee: Origins and Growing Regions
When you think of the Arabian Peninsula, you picture Lawrence of Arabia and sandy deserts. But there is some prime real estate, and it's mostly in western Yemen. And also the part of Saudi Arabia that the House of Saud annexed from Yemen in 1934, with British “help,” so there is a grudge match here going back a century. (Think of Britain, Ireland, and Northern Ireland, with cultural and religious overlays, but on the Arabian Peninsula.)

Monsoon rains sweeping across the Red Sea are caught on the steep west-facing mountains, that's why all these agricultural terraces were built, by hand, by Yemenis, over many centuries. These mountains rise up to 12,000 feet, or 3,660 meters. Without constant attention and manual-labor upkeep, these ancient walled terraces would erode and collapse during heavy rain floods, and after repeated freeze cycles. Yemenis are taught about of the sacrifice of their ancestors, and their own generation’s responsibility to maintain these almost sacred terrace field, which feed their families and neighbors. If anybody thinks these Yemeni mountain people are short-term thinkers, much less quitters, they are seriously in error.

-
- The Yemeni tribes that inhabit northwest Yemen are closely related to the tribes in the three Saudi-annexed provinces by dialect, and by their adherence to the Zaydi sect of Shia Islam. The unwelcome 1934 new Saudi border cut straight across the formerly continuous Yemeni highland world.

-
-  It’s also important to understand just how big Yemen is: it’s 20% larger than California. Its population is nearly the same as Saudi Arabia’s, at around 36 million.

-
- Almost 3/4 of the total Yemeni population is now under Houthi / Ansar Allah control, and they also hold the capital city, Sana’a. So it’s completely absurd to refer to them as “the Houthi Rebels,” and call the Saudi-paid mercenary militias (who only control the ground under their military vehicles) “the official government of Yemen.”

In addition, only 2/3 of the Saudis are citizens, and 1/3 are foreign-born “residents,” of questionable loyalty or fighting spirit.

Another factor to consider: 4 million Yemeni-Saudis live in the three annexed provinces.

-
- Ansar Allah, aka "The Houthis," are mostly Zaydi Shia Muslims, and these are not quite the same as the Shias of Iran or Iraq. The above map is still useful, though, to understand the religious breakdown of the Arabian Peninsula, the Gulf, and Iran, and why it matters so much in the Saudi-Yemen conflict.

You can see that Iran and part of Iraq are heavily Shia, as are western Yemen and most of the three annexed provinces. But also note the heavy Shia presence along the Saudi Persian Gulf coast, with its vast and vulnerable petroleum infrastructure.
A saying I heard today, I think it’s from Larry Johnson: “The Saudis live in a glass house, and the Yemenis live in a rock house. Who is going to win a rock fight?”

This makes the Saudi royal family extremely paranoid. Not only do they face a war in the south vs. Yemen, but also a war across the gulf with Iran, and an incipient Shia "5th Column" in and among their cash-cow petroleum industries along their Persian Gulf and Red Sea coasts.
I asked Grok about the whole "Houthis or Ansar Allah?" nomenclature debate. Take it for what it's worth.

-
- And here is a meme on this point that I saw and grabbed today. Since “The Houthis” aka Ansar Allah now control 3/4 of the population, the capital, the Red Sea coast, and virtually all of the inhabited arable land, maybe it’s time to just call them: YEMENIS. And that is how I will refer to them going forward. Yemenis. They have earned it.

-
- No matter what you think about the USA-Iran war, or the Saudi-Yemen war, you have to admit that the Yemenis are very brave fighters. Here is a representative video showing one soldier’s courage under fire.
/video/1

Napoleon said: “In war, the morale is to the physical as three to one.” This is why the Saudis and their other paid mercenary militias generally quit when facing the extremely brave and motivated Yemenis.
Their obstinate courage is also why they are now forming a strong leg of Iran’s “Axis of Resistance,” as they call it. Only the Yemenis took on Israel and kept firing missiles at “the Zionist project” while Gaza was being bombed into rubble. And it was the Yemenis who took on the US Navy, and drove it out of the Red Sea during this period from the end of 2023 and into 2025. This gives the Yemenis tremendous and enduring “street cred” across the entire Islamic world, and not only the Shia parts of it.
Here in this clip, Ansar Allah Yemenis are are reviewing some of the recently captured American-build Saudi military equipment. Remember what Napoleon said about “the morale to the physical.” Saudi-paid militia mercenaries are not willing to die in this fight, no matter how well paid or equipped they are.
/video/1
Mountain people everywhere are tough and self-reliant. Hard mountain life makes them this way. Some call the west Yemen highlands "Arabia's Appalachia," but the mountains are closer in height to the Rockies, and they are rain-catching, like the California or Oregon coastal ranges. And all those stone terraces, dug and built by hand by their grandfathers going back a thousand years, gives them a spiritual connection to their land that is hard to duplicate.

Here is a Yemeni fighter declaring he will never quit the fight.
"We were born free! We will live free! We will die free! And we will never become slaves!" The audio is obviously “boosted,” but this message is spreading across the Islamic world, both Shia and Sunni, and it’s not only directed at Saudi Arabia. When he says, “To all the tyrants of the earth,” he is looking at us, and at Israel.
/video/1

Do not underestimate their fighting spirit. And courage is contagious: the Yemenis are now boosting the morale and fighting spirit of both Sunni and Shia Muslims across the world, as an example of how brave people can do battle against the Israeli and American “Axis of Evil” (from their point of view) and their paid stooges across the GCC, and notably in Saudi Arabia.
I’m not here to cheerlead for the Yemenis, but we have to face reality. These guys are fighters, and they are motivating a new generation to continue the battle against the Zionist project and American control of the region and West Asia.

-
- Bracken—Out

And if you want the Kindle or Audible versions, Amazon is your go-to. But these days, Amazon is horrible for authors in the printed realm. Horrible. I barely break even shipping them cases of books to resell. They are trying to force authors to use their in-house  “print on demand” publishing service, but I don’t want them to control so many aspects of my self-publishing business. And the formatting of their POD books is really just lousy.
If you want my printed books, I recommend getting them directly from me, and I’ll even sign them. Amazon won’t. Snail-mail works great, but PayPal is quicker.

reads.title: The Great Decoupling: Why Breaking Up With China Makes Everything You Buy More Expensive.
reads.subtitle: America and China are separating on purpose, each trying to become immune to the other. A more resilient supply chain is also a pricier, less expert one, and the cost gets handed to you at the store.
reads.body:
For about 35+ years, America and China were fused at the hip. America designed things and bought things. China built them. The whole global economy was arranged around that single division of labor, and it worked, because it was built to do one job better than anything before it: deliver the lowest possible price.
Signal, Not Noise! By AJ Signal is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.

- China made it cheap.

- America bought it cheap.
A generation of electronics, cars, and everyday goods stayed affordable because that one connected spine ran through both countries.
Now both are trying to pull apart at the same time. Washington and Beijing are each dismantling the arrangement from their own end, for their own reasons, and the way each one does it tells you where the next 50~ years are heading. I call it the GREAT DECOUPLING.
Two things are worth understanding about it. How it works, and who pays.
America is decoupling on purpose
The American side is deliberate. Tariffs that at their peak ran past 100% on Chinese goods. A hard push to pull chips, advanced technology, defense production, and critical manufacturing out of Chinese hands. And underneath the loud parts, a quieter workhorse doing most of the actual work: The “China + one.”
Subscribe now
Get 7 day free trial
Share
The idea is simple. Big companies keep ‘SOME;’ production in China but move the rest out, to Vietnam, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Mexico and beyond. They are not all walking out the door. They are buying themselves options, spreading the risk so that no single point inside China can hold them hostage “IF” the relationship sours or Beijing decides to squeeze.
It is “insurance more than divorce”, or more precisely, “insurance against the divorce”.

-
- China is decoupling right back
Beijing is doing the same exact thing from its side, and I would argue just as hard. It is racing to make its own chips, mine and refine its own minerals, and build a domestic version of everything it still relies on the West for. Every export control Washington imposes, Beijing answers by standing up the local replacement. The goal is to stop depending on ANY American technology or Western supplier that could be ordered to cut it off.
Subscribe now
Give a gift subscription
So this is not one country leaving and one country left behind. Both are separating, and each is TRYING to make itself immune to the other. That is the shape of it. Two partners who spent 35+ years becoming one system now spending enormous effort to become two.
Here is the part most people miss…
China did not just make things cheaply. That is the surface story, and it is why the decoupling looks easy from a distance, just move the factory somewhere cheaper. The real thing China built is harder to see and far harder to copy.
China concentrated entire industries into specific zones and cities. If your business is phones, there is a region where phone-making lives. Automotive, a different region. Textiles, another. And inside that region, everyone does that one thing. The workers, the component suppliers, the supply chains, the tooling shops, the engineers, all of them, packed together, doing the same specialized work for decades. Even if you needed to change jobs, your experience does not go to a different part of the country, it likely stays in the same city because that is where your specific industry rules supreme. That is experience moving around within your own domain and your own city. Change companies and you are still in the same city, surrounded by the same expertise.
Subscribe now
Get 7 day free trial
Leave a comment
That concentration is the REAL moat those that have not visited China cannot comprehend. It stacks cost, quality, and above all know-how into one place, and it compounds. When every part of an industry sits in the same few square miles, knowledge moves between people faster than it can anywhere scattered. A supplier solves a problem on Monday and the whole cluster knows by Friday. Forty years of that builds something you cannot buy off a shelf or stand up in a hurry. You can ship a factory. You cannot ship the accumulated knowledge of everyone around it.
This is why the “plus one” countries are NOT a clean swap and the multinationals need to account for this. Vietnam, India, and the rest are early in this. They do not yet have the supplier density, the depth of expertise, or in some cases the population to build clusters at that scale. They can take the assembly work. They cannot take the compounded expertise, not yet. On the honest estimate, they are at least 10 to 20+ years away from it.
So the world ends up with a supply chain that is steadier and, at the same time, more expensive and less expert than the one it is replacing. Both things are true at once.
The first effect lands in your wallet
Start with the immediate cost, because it reaches you before anything else does. The old system was engineered for one outcome, the lowest price. Break it and prices rise. A spread-out supply chain is more resilient but less efficient, and less efficient means more expensive. That shows up on electronics, on cars, on the ordinary goods a globalized China kept cheap for 35+ years. Every extra step added to the chain, every factory standing up somewhere new and still climbing its learning curve, keeps costs higher for years. Decoupling pushes prices up, and the bill gets handed to you at the store.
Subscribe now
Give a gift subscription
Get 7 day free trial
That is the first-order effect. The ones that matter more take longer to arrive.
The second effect: a new tier of powers rises
We must keep an eye on where the diverted factories get setup, because those countries are being pulled up the socio-economic ladder. India, Vietnam, Indonesia, Mexico, they are catching plants, jobs, and leverage they never had before. Not because they out-competed anyone, but because they happened to be standing where the supply chain came down when it left China.
A new tier of “middle powers” is forming out of this. Countries that were on the edge of the global economy are being handed a place closer to the center, simply by geography and timing. Over a decade or two, that reshapes who has bargaining power, who industrializes, who matters.
The decoupling is not only splitting America and China. It is promoting a whole set of second-tier states into the game, and they will carry the political weight that comes with industry once they have it.
The third effect I see: the dollar erodes
Here is the slowest and largest consequence, and it works against America’s own aims. The old single spine, everything running through the US-China connection, was also one of the main “architecture” that made the US dollar the center of world trade. One connected system, one dominant currency at its heart; the US dollar.
Break the world economy into more pieces and you get more currencies, more blocs, more ways to move money that never touch Washington hence the emergence of the BRICS++ block where China is the founding member.
A world that no longer runs through a single US-China axis is a world with more room to route and re-route around the US dollar. And this is the trap in America’s own strategy. Pulling the critical industries home may win the security fight, keeping the chips and the defense production out of Chinese hands, and still cost America the monetary dominance that came from sitting at the center of one connected system.
You cannot shatter the global economy into pieces and remain its hub at the same time. Those two goals pull against each other, and Washington is chasing both. Security says fragment the system. Dollar dominance says stay the center of it. It cannot have both, and the decoupling forces the choice whether or not anyone in Washington admits it out loud.

The read
The decoupling was probably always coming after decades of over-reliance on a single country for the world’s manufacturing. The surprise is NOT that it is happening. It is how much it costs, and how the costs stack.

- In the near term, higher prices for ordinary people.

- In the medium term, a new set of middle powers rising because the factories landed on them.

- In the long term, an erosion of the dollar’s centrality that America may bring on itself while trying to protect its security.
You can move the factory. That part is happening now, and you can watch it in the price of things. Moving 35 or so years of concentrated know-how is the part nobody has figured out how to ship, and until someone does, the world gets a supply chain that is safer, dearer, and less skilled all at once.
That is the trade being made, and everyone is paying a piece of it.

reads.title: Iran Is Squeezing CENTCOM From Every Direction at Once, and the Quietest Part May Matter Most: America's Weapons Are Now in Iranian Hands.
reads.subtitle: The Houthis just took a chokepoint. A Saudi pipeline is burning. And under the noise, Iran and its allies are recovering American weapons systems intact, the one prize that outlasts any single battle.
reads.body:
The war across the Middle East gets reported as separate pressures on the United States.

- The Houthis in Yemen.

- The fight over Hormuz.

- The strikes on Saudi oil.

- The standoff with Iran.
Put them on one map and they stop looking separate. Iran and its allies are raising the cost and the exposure of the American position across the whole region at once, on fronts that feed each other.
One of those fronts has barely been covered, and over time it may matter MORE than any single strike. Iran is not only fighting American weapons. It is collecting them.
Take the two visible pressures first, then the one no one is discussing.
Signal, Not Noise! By AJ Signal is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
The Red Sea gate is closing
The Houthis have retaken the port of Mokha on Yemen’s southern Red Sea coast. The location is the whole point. Mokha sits on the approach to Bab al-Mandeb, the roughly twenty-kilometre gate where the Red Sea narrows toward the Gulf of Aden. Holding that coast, plus the western Yemeni shoreline and several islands they have seized, puts a Houthi hand on one of the two chokepoints that carry the world’s energy. H
ormuz is already contested on the far side of the peninsula. Now the Red Sea, the route Saudi Arabia has been using to move the oil it can no longer safely send through the Gulf, is contested too. Squeeze Bab al-Mandeb and you squeeze the kingdom’s last exit.

-
- The squeeze is real, not theoretical. The Petroline, Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline built specifically to reach the Red Sea and skip Hormuz, was hit again this week. Pump stations burning in the satellite images, the line shut down as a precaution. Both Saudi export routes are under pressure at the same time, oil markets feel every strike, and the American strategic reserve keeps draining. This is what Iran’s forward network is built to do. Not one front. Several, timed to compound.
Subscribe now
Give a gift subscription
That is the war you can see. Here is the part that has been kept quiet.
Iran is pulling American weapons off the battlefield
For months now, the Revolutionary Guard (IRGC) and its allies have been recovering American-made weapons and equipment from the fighting. Some of these recoveries are confirmed, photographed, and admitted by the United States itself. That makes them a different kind of loss than a downed jet or a spent missile, and they have not gotten the attention they should.
The clearest case is from September 8. The IRGC Navy pulled an Anduril Dive-LD, an unmanned underwater vehicle, out of the Strait of Hormuz. This is not an Iranian propaganda reel. CENTCOM acknowledged it. Anduril’s own founder confirmed it. The American line is that it was an older model that malfunctioned, sat dead in the water for more than a day, and carried nothing classified. Maybe so. An intact American autonomous underwater system in Iranian hands is still a physical object that can be opened, measured, and studied, whatever its software held or did not hold.

-
- There are other confirmed recoveries next to it. Intact and near-intact GBU-39 small-diameter bombs, Boeing’s precision glide munitions, have been photographed in Iranian possession, at least one with the guidance wings still attached.

-
- And at Mokha, coalition forces pulling out left behind American-built armored vehicles, Oshkosh M-ATVs and other US-pattern MRAPs, which the Houthis filmed and drove away. Those were abandoned in a retreat, not taken off American troops, which matters. But they are American hardware in hostile hands now.
The line between confirmed and claimed is where this analysis lives or dies, so let me hold it. Iran has made bigger claims that do not check out. It says it dug an intact GBU-57 bunker buster out of the ground for reverse engineering. There is no public photograph of an intact one, and Iranian accounts get its weight wrong, which points to a smaller penetrator mislabeled as the big weapon.
Subscribe now
Leave a comment

-
- It has paraded wreckage of MQ-9 Reapers and an F-15E, but wreckage is not a working captured system, and the dozens of Reapers people cite are a loss tally, not a rack of intact prizes. I am not inflating the case, because the confirmed core is bad enough, and the inflated version is the one that lets critics wave the whole thing away. The argument does not need a captured bunker buster. It rests on what we know for certain sits in Iranian hands.

-
- A captured weapon is worse than a destroyed one
A destroyed weapon is gone. A captured one gets taken apart and copied. That is the difference, and it is the part the administration has real reason to worry about.
A recovered system is a live blueprint. Its materials, its design, its guidance, all of it can be studied and reproduced. Iran is unusually ready to do this, because it has spent forty years under sanctions building a domestic arms industry for exactly this purpose, to make what it was denied. Its drone and missile programs already run heavily on reverse-engineered foreign technology. Hand that industry an intact American system and you have handed it a shortcut, years of American research and development, captured off a battlefield at a fraction of what it cost to invent.
Subscribe now
Share
Leave a comment
There is a sharper edge, and it cuts into something rotten in the American system itself. American weapons are priced at absurd multiples of what they cost to build, because the defense industry has learned to bill the government many times over for what it supplies. Iran carries none of that. No shareholders to enrich, no procurement racket, no reason to inflate. When Iran copies a captured American system, it can build its own version far cheaper, and built for mass rather than for the exquisite, low-volume perfection the American original was designed around. The captured weapon teaches Iran two things at once. How to build it, and how to build it at the scale and price the American manufacturer priced itself out of.
The Houthis add another layer. They are not only holding ground. They are learning the same battlefield lessons, the how of the capture, the conditions under which these systems fail or fall. That is intelligence the American manufacturer does not have and cannot easily get, because it never sees its own weapon from the other side. The people who recover a system learn where it is weak in ways the people who built it never will.
Subscribe now
Get 7 day free trial

> What it means for the region, and the next war
Over time, every American system lost in this war becomes a potential Iranian system in the next one, deployed against Iran’s neighbors and against the Central Command units posted across the region. Iran’s forward network is not just bleeding CENTCOM through attrition. It is harvesting American technology off the battlefield and feeding it into an industry built to copy, cheapen, and mass-produce.
That is what makes this phase more dangerous than the strike-by-strike coverage lets on. Missiles run out. Captured knowledge does not. It stays, and it comes back built cheaper and in greater numbers. The Gulf states and the American forces in the region are not only facing the Iranian and Houthi weapons that exist today. They are facing the next generation of them, informed by American designs pulled out of the sand and the seawater.
So the pressure on Central Command runs on three levels. The kinetic one, the strikes and the chokepoints, everyone sees. The economic one, the squeeze on oil and the draining reserve, is slower and structural. The third is the quiet collection and copying of American systems, and its effects will outlast the war itself. Watch what is being recovered, not only what is being fired.
