reads.title: Hasan Piker: smeared by a panicked Democratic Establishment
reads.subtitle: The Democratic Establishment know they’ve lost their base. These smears are driven by panic
reads.body:
- There is a coordinated smear campaign against the leftist streamer Hasan Piker by the Democratic Party establishment over Israel’s US-armed and facilitated genocide against the Palestinian people.
The bottom line about what’s happening here is this: the American people have turned against Israel in revulsion at the genocide and want to stop facilitating its crimes. That opposition is overwhelming among the Democratic rank-and-file. But the Democratic Party establishment remains invested in the alliance with Israel – and they fear being swept aside by pro-Palestinian left-wing candidates in upcoming primaries.
BattleLines with Owen Jones is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
So their response is to smear pro-Palestinian figures – in this case, to try to toxify Hasan Piker and nullify his ability to mobilise grassroots supporters to help progressive candidates win Democratic primaries.
They also clearly want to destroy the chances of progressive candidates like Abdul el-Sayed, who is standing for the Senate in Michigan, even if that destroys the Democrats’ chances of winning the Senate – so they can say: look, if you select progressive candidates, they will lose against the Republicans. The aim is to deter other voters from following that example.
The Democratic Party establishment – like the rest of the pro-Israel faction which dominates the US political elite – knows it has lost the argument. They know they have lost public opinion. They know they have lost their base. So, to stay in control, they are resorting to fear, smear and lies.
Share

## What Hasan Piker actually said
The smear against Hasan Piker which Democratic bigwigs are promoting is that he has threatened Jewish Americans with violence if they don’t stop supporting Israel, and that he is antisemitic. It rests on a total, wilful and deceitful distortion of what he has said.
We’re going to go through what’s going on here. Let’s start by listening to what he said. Here’s the first clip, in which he was responding to an anti-Zionist Jewish follower of his.
What he’s saying here is that US public opinion has dramatically shifted against Israel – and that this has happened despite the efforts of the Western political and media elite. The latest polling, at the end of July, shows that 55% of Americans have an unfavourable view of Israel, with just 31% having a favourable view. That same pollster, back in March 2025, had Americans equally divided – with 43% favourable and 43% unfavourable.
Among Democrats, that unfavourability is overwhelming. But even among Republicans under the age of 30, 58% had unfavourable views of Israel, compared with 29% who had favourable views.
The polling also found that 52% thought the US gave too much military aid to Israel, while another poll by YouGov found that 44% of Americans thought the US shouldn’t send military aid to Israel, compared with just a third who said it should.
The polling has also found that half of registered American voters think Israel has committed genocide, while 35% believe it has not.
Despite the political and media elite being united behind Israel, the American people have decided they’ve seen quite enough mass slaughter and atrocities against innocent people, thank you very much, and they are done with Israel.
Subscribe now
So Hasan Piker is making an argument against conflation. He is arguing that conflating Jewish people with a state whose crimes have repulsed the American people is obviously going to drive antisemitism, and therefore put Jewish people in danger – something he does not want Jewish people to face. He is arguing that this conflation is a threat to Jewish safety.
Indeed, it should be noted that polling also finds that more than six in ten Jewish Americans think Israel has committed war crimes, about four in 10 believe it has committed genocide, rising to 50% among Jewish Americans under 35. Another poll also finds that around half of Jews under 35 want to replace Israel altogether with a binational state with equal rights for all.
So the conflation of Israel and its crimes with Jewish people – promoted by the pro-Israel lobby – is endangering Jewish people based on a lie. Because people who express views about Israel which are common among Jewish Americans are smeared as antisemites.
The point Hasan Piker is making is that Jewish Americans do not prioritise Israel in their voting habits, but they do prioritise antisemitism, quite understandably, and the pro-Israel lobby is trying to manipulate that concern to build support for Israel. He’s arguing specifically for a demarcation between Jewish people and the State of Israel and its crimes.
It’s fundamentally the same point made by Ezra Klein, a mainstream Jewish liberal columnist for the New York Times, who said:

> “Anti-Zionism is rising as a response to what Israel is doing. It will simply not be possible to treat it as a marginal viewpoint that can be shamed or shunned into invisibility. Yes, antisemitism often cloaks itself in anti-Zionism. So don’t do the antisemites’ work for them. If you keep telling people that if they oppose the Jewish state then they must hate the Jewish people, eventually, they will believe you.”
Subscribe now

## Is this really ‘victim blaming’?
Now, obviously, anti-Zionism – opposition to an ethno-nationalism which strips the rights of Palestinians and indeed subjects them to genocide – is not antisemitism. What is absolutely true is that antisemites seeking to recruit people are helped if the argument is routinely made that opposing Israel’s crimes means you hate Jewish people.
The argument here is that this is victim blaming – which is total nonsense.
Look, it’s basic common sense that, say, the September 11 attacks increased Islamophobia. Should they have done? No. Did Islamophobes use the attacks to incite anti-Muslim hatred? Yes. Do we need to aggressively oppose the hateful efforts by Islamophobes to whip up hatred of Muslims because of terrorist attacks like 9/11? Yes, absolutely.
It remains the case that those attacks increased anti-Muslim hatred, and everybody knows that.
The difference is that the 9/11 attacks were not armed and backed by the US government, with a media and political elite vilifying anyone who opposed those attacks as anti-Muslim bigots. Imagine if that was the case!
Let’s listen to this other clip, in which he discusses the pro-Israel Democratic congressional candidate who has refused to endorse Senate candidate Abdul el-Sayed.
In this clip, what Hasan Piker is doing is again opposing the conflation of Jewish people and Israel, and arguing instead for a demarcation between Jewish people and Israel.
Subscribe now

## What about the ISIS comparison?
Some of the contrived anger has arisen because of the comparison between Israel and ISIS.
Let me just pick one quote – there are so many others – from Itamar Ben-Gvir, Israel’s National Security Minister and a key member of the Israeli government. He said:

> “For every tear of an Israeli mother, a thousand Lebanese mothers must weep. All of Lebanon must burn.”"
Is it fair to make a comparison with ISIS there? Yes, it obviously is.
What about the UN independent commission which this year concluded that Israel was deliberately targeting children – up to and including deliberately shooting kids in the head and chest in order to kill them – backed up by testimonies from dozens of US-based medics who served in Gaza?
Or indeed the leading British surgeon, Dr. Nick Maynard, who testified that Israeli soldiers were shooting different parts of the bodies of Palestinian children on different days – one day the head, the next day the chest, the next day the genitalia, and so on.
Does that sound like ISIS to you? I’d say it does.
What about deliberately destroying hospitals?
What about deliberately blowing up ambulances and medical staff, including with double-tap strikes where there’s an attack on civilians, and then the Israeli army waits until medical staff arrive to attack again?
What about systematically attacking mosques and churches?
What about destroying up universities, libraries and archives?
What about destroying ancient monuments?
I could go on.
Don’t want to be compared to ISIS? Then don’t act like ISIS.
Subscribe now

## The Democratic pile-on
Let’s go through some of the coordinated messages from the Democratic Party establishment.
Hakeem Jeffries, the Democratic Minority Leader, posted:

> “The malicious claim that American Jews are inviting violence against themselves is dangerous and antisemitic.
There is zero justification for threats against the safety of our Jewish brothers and sisters at a moment of rising hate.
We will fight the cancer of antisemitism with the fierce urgency of now.”
A deceitful distortion of what Hasan Piker said. Piker opposes these threats and this violence, and he is arguing against the cause of it.
US Senator Cory Booker denounced what he called Hasan Piker’s “dangerous and hateful language”, again claiming that Piker was saying Jewish Americans were responsible for hatred and violence, and arguing he was stoking hatred against our neighbours – the opposite of what Piker was doing.
Congressman Josh Gottheimer insanely claimed Hasan Piker’s comments were “sick, wrong and straight out of the Nazi playbook”.
We could go on – and I’ll explain what the Democratic Party establishment is up to.
But as Pastor Ben Dixon says:

> “There is no question that the Democratic Party Establishment has coordinated more attacks on Hasan Piker than they have coordinated opposition to Donald Trump and his destruction of the Republic.”
Just a fact: this weak, pathetic party Establishment lay back and did nothing while Trump’s Republicans rampaged across an already deeply compromised US democracy. Yet it’s a left-wing streamer opposed to genocide who rouses them from their slumber and makes them go on the offensive.
Indeed, note that Fox News had 224 broadcasts in August mentioning Hasan Piker, compared with 44 broadcasts about the war on Iran. This is a Republican smear campaign which the Democrats have joined in on.
Subscribe now

## What fighting antisemitism actually requires
Dov Waxman, Professor of Israel Studies at UCLA, has some really wise comments. He says:

> “In response to the outrage expressed over Hasan Piker’s recent comments regarding American Jews and antisemitism, which many have interpreted as blaming Jews themselves for provoking antisemitic violence because of their support for Israel, I feel it is necessary to stress some basic points:

- We must unequivocally condemn antisemitic acts against Jews and not make excuses for those who commit them.

- We also need to acknowledge that Israel’s actions fuel much (but not all) of the anger and hatred directed against Jews nowadays.

- Conflating Jews with Israel has been promoted by antisemites, U.S. politicians, the Israeli state and its officials, and by major Jewish organizations and mainstream institutions.

- We should also recognize that while most Jewish Americans do not support the Israeli government’s policies or the Israeli army’s actions in Gaza and the West Bank, most Jews are emotionally attached to Israel and care about it, and it is wrong to require them to sever or disavow their connection to Israel in order to avoid antisemitic discrimination or be safe from antisemitic violence.

- The fact that hatred of Israel can cause hatred of Jews and that Jews are being attacked because they are associated with Israel does not mean that Jews deserve to be hated or targeted because of this association, but it’s not victim-blaming to note that people make this association at least partly because the Jewish state itself and major Jewish groups outside Israel continually emphasize the connection between Jews and Israel and between Judaism and Zionism.”
This is really wise, nuanced stuff.
Antisemitism is a grave evil and it must be fought. Within living memory it caused the Holocaust, the industrialised extermination of six million Jews. And indeed, making Jewish people in the diaspora feel safe itself helps undermine the arguments presented by Israel as some sort of liferaft for Jewish people.
Part and parcel of this must be to demarcate between Israel and Jewish people – and we should emphasise that both antisemites and defenders of Israel are seeking to conflate Jewish people and Israel.
Subscribe now
As Hasan Piker has said:

> “do not let a coordinated republican smear campaign become ‘reality.’ my argument against the dangerous false conflation between zionism and judaism which in turn increases antisemitism is now turned on it’s head. zionism is not judaism. antizionism is not antisemitism.”

## The Democratic establishment has lost its base
What’s really going on here?
Well, the Democratic establishment knows it has lost its base. New polling has just come out on the views of Democratic voters in the first six primary states. Take a look:

-
- Completely overwhelming and decisive. The Democratic Party Establishment has lost its base – and that terrifies them.
So what have they just done? They just appointed Congressman Jared Moskowitz as Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on the Middle East and North Africa. He is one of the most pro-Israel and pro-war members.
It is as deliberate and calculated an “up yours” to the Democratic base as it’s possible to conjure up.
They are doubling down.
Subscribe now

## What Hakeem Jeffries represents
Hakeem Jeffries himself has repeatedly travelled to Israel, including on many trips linked to AIPAC, the main pro-Israel lobby.
He has repeatedly justified Israeli war crimes. In 2014, he told a large pro-Israel rally in New York:

> “When you live in a tough neighborhood Israel should not be made to apologize for its strength”,
adding that:

> “the only thing that neighbors respect in a tough neighborhood is strength.”
He then co-sponsored a House resolution supporting Israel’s military response to Hamas.
He has repeatedly opposed conditioning US military aid to Israel, repeatedly voted to hike Israeli military funding, and voted down attempts to cut aid to Israel during the genocide.
And note how Hakeem Jeffries just privately met up with Jared Kushner, the unelected son-in-law of Donald Trump, to discuss who knows what (we are told it was housing, immigration, the cost of living and supposed areas of cooperation, but we should be sceptical if that was it).
Subscribe now

## The hatred they ignore
Meanwhile, there is constant hatred and bile promoted by the US right – without this pushback from the Democrats.
Take Laura Loomer, a de facto adviser in the court of Donald Trump, who just posted this:

> “I don’t want Muslims in positions of elected office and I don’t want Muslims having financial ties to the GOP.
I don’t like Islam. If I could wave a magic wand, I would round up Muslims and deport them from America.
Most MAGA voters agree with me.
Good luck running for office and trying to convince the MAGA base that we need more Muslims in America.
Good luck.”
This is Nazi-like hatred – calling for rounding up an entire minority – and yet where are the coordinated Democratic attacks?
Subscribe now

## What this is really about
The truth is that the Democratic eEtablishment fears Hasan Piker because they know he can mobilise voters to replace them with progressive candidates, and they are terrified because they know they have lost the Democratic base.
They fear being swept away.
They want people like Abdul el-Sayed to lose in Michigan so that Democratic voters go: well, we’d better not vote to elect people like that, even if we agree with them, because otherwise we’ll let the Republicans win.
The Democrats would prefer to lose to the Republicans than win with the left.
They would prefer to keep facilitating Israel’s genocide and heinous crimes rather than win.
That’s what we are dealing with here.
And if it means destroying US democracy to defend Israel – that’s a price they’re willing to pay .

reads.title: Mark Ruffalo: smeared by Israel’s apologists for speaking the truth
reads.subtitle: There is nothing antisemitic about Ruffalo’s opposition to the Paramount Warner Bros. merger
reads.body:
- Hollywood superstar Mark Ruffalo is being smeared as antisemitic because he opposes Israel’s genocide. What he is saying is supported by most Americans, most people in the West – and most people on earth – and all of that is linked to why he is being smeared.
The Emmy Award-winning actor, known for playing the Hulk in the Marvel Cinematic Universe as well as films such as Spotlight, Foxcatcher and The Kids Are All Right, is being smeared because he opposes the $111bn merger of Paramount Skydance with Warner Bros. Discovery.

## Why Ruffalo opposes the merger
Now, there are lots of reasons he’s opposing the merger. He opposes it on media concentration grounds – this new company will account for over a quarter of wide-release theatrical distribution in the US, and it would mean three distributors account for three quarters of wide-release films, while four would control 86%. California and 11 other states are suing to stop the merger. It also means CBS News and CNN, as well as Paramount Pictures, Warner Bros., HBO and multiple other television networks, would be in the same group.
Help us take on the pro-war, pro-genocide, pro-injustice mainstream media by becoming a subscriber.
He opposes it because it will mean huge job losses, because it will be saddled with around $79bn worth of net debt, and because investment partners include the sovereign wealth funds of dictatorships like Saudi Arabia.
He opposes it because the family who own Paramount – David Ellison and his father Larry Ellison – are close to the Trump regime. Trump has described Larry Ellison as “a friend of mine”, and since they took over CBS News, the channel has shifted its coverage to become more favourable to the Trump administration.
But he has another very strong reason to oppose it – and that is because Paramount Skydance is run by a family who are not just ideologically vehemently pro-Israel, but who have actual profound links to Israel.
Oracle’s relationship with Israel is longstanding to say the least. Its technology has been supplied across the Israeli state, including to military, government and police. That relationship formed the context for a clip circulated by Ruffalo on Instagram – footage of Oracle executive vice-chair Safra Catz, who also sits on Paramount’s board, discussing technology Oracle offered Israel after 7 October.
Share
On his Instagram story, Ruffalo shared a video of Safra Catz, an Israeli who serves as former Oracle CEO and now as executive vice-chair – and who is also a director on the board of Paramount since its merger with Skydance Media.
Amongst other things, in the video she boasts of Oracle offering “really profoundly scary technology” to Israel as it committed genocide from October 2023 onwards. A state which a consensus of genocide scholars, NGOs like Amnesty International and Médecins Sans Frontières, and a UN independent commission say is committing genocide – and here she is, boasting of offering up “really profoundly scary technology” to support what she would claim is a military offensive, but is a genocide.
Subscribe now
Ruffalo then posted the following:

> “This is the company that Larry Ellison is using to fund his son David’s Warner Bros acquisition.
These ‘really profoundly scary technologies’ will most likely be merged into one of the largest media conglomerates in the world and one day used on you. Look how she revels in what we now have come to see as a genocide, which was built on an apartheid system of oppression powered by Oracle.
There is an old saying. ‘The way you do one thing is the way you do everything.’
From one of the biggest tech companies in the world. Powering some of the most destructive and inhuman forces in the world. Why has Trump pushed this illegal merger through?
Larry Ellison will own most of ‘Para Bros’. Larry is a classic Oligarch. They are crushing workers and consolidating the wealth of the world for their own power and concentrated dominance.
We have a chance to stop this. There are 12 state Attorneys General suing to block this merger. It will be catastrophic for our film industry.
There will be a loss of 4500 direct film making jobs and the loss of another 10k ancillary jobs. Merger like this are almost always bad for workers, consumers, and the industry they tend to dominate. It’s a classic antitrust case.
It will hike up the cost of cable and flatten out competition. This means less choice for our audiences. It also concentrates an enormous amount of creative control to companies that say and do things like this strange woman from Oracle.”
Paramount then released a statement which included the following:

> “We are, as always, troubled when antisemitic tropes are invoked in purported service of a business dispute. Words like ‘genocide’ and ‘apartheid,’ applied to a corporate transaction, aren’t just wrong – they’re a bridge too far, and they cheapen the very real suffering those words are meant to describe. This doesn’t deserve a response in kind – and to be clear, we don’t tolerate prejudice of any kind, against anyone.”
Subscribe now

## Where is the antisemitism?
This is a lie. There was nothing antisemitic here – we’ll come on to that more.
Now two so-called “prominent Jewish advocacy groups”, as Variety put it, have accused Ruffalo of spreading “antisemitic tropes”. That is the Simon Wiesenthal Center and something called the Creative Community for Peace.
The CEO of the Simon Wiesenthal Center said:

> “Words matter, and so does the willingness to draw a line when legitimate debate gives way to antisemitic tropes.
“We commend Paramount for speaking clearly and refusing to allow prejudice to masquerade as political or corporate criticism. At a time when antisemitism is too often minimized, rationalized, or repackaged in more socially acceptable language, this kind of moral clarity matters.”
The cheek of these people using “moral clarity” to smear opponents of an ongoing genocide.
Subscribe now

## What the Simon Wiesenthal Center calls antisemitism
Want to hear more about what the Simon Wiesenthal Center thinks is antisemitic?
In 2016, they had their list of the Worst Global Anti-Semitic/Anti-Israel Incidents. Guess what was at number one? The UN’s treatment of Israel, with particular emphasis on the Obama administration abstaining on a UN Security Council resolution condemning illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank.
That was above the white supremacist neo-Nazi Richard Spencer, who attended a gathering featuring Nazi salutes, where Spencer questioned whether Jews were even people.
And in 2011 they issued a statement opposing Israel returning to its pre-1967 borders – that is, before the illegal occupation of Palestinian territory – with a press release with the headline “Israel Should Reject a Return to 1967 ‘Auschwitz’ Borders”. Let’s not mince our words here. These people are absurd extremists as well as apologists for terrible crimes.
Subscribe now

## The Ellisons and Israel
Let’s just go through the facts about the Ellisons and their relationship with Israel.
In 2014 Larry Ellison gave $10m to Friends of the IDF. In 2017, he gave another $16.6m.
That’s what we know publicly.
In 2024, a Jerusalem Post article wrote about David Ellison taking over Paramount, saying it was a “groundbreaking strategic move reshaping the US media market”. They quote a source familiar with the details, who says:

> “This is the next generation of global Jewish leadership. These two young men love Israel, are connected to their Judaism, have Zionist values, and it’s very encouraging to see that in such successful families, the values are passed on to the younger generations. Both quietly donate quite a bit to the State of Israel and the IDF. It is positive news for the Jewish world that Korff and Ellison are the next generation of global Jewish leadership, connected to Israel and holding Zionist values.”
And what gives that source credence is that at the bottom of the article it says: “This article was written in cooperation with SkyDance.”
Was it indeed.
In 2014, Larry Ellison told Israel’s Channel 10: “We love our country of Israel and we’ll do everything we can to support the country of Israel.”
Larry Ellison’s first wife described him as “an ardent Zionist” and, according to New York Magazine, “remembered him taking a week off work to watch coverage of the Six-Day War in 1967.” It also noted that Larry Ellison is close to Benjamin Netanyahu, who it says vacationed on his Hawaiian island in 2021.
It further goes on to say:

> “David once joined Larry on a trip to Israel and posted a photo to Instagram from a dinner with the prime minister. ‘I am very grateful for everything he has done and continues to do for the nation of Israel! #bibinetanyahu,’ David wrote. After October 7, David declared that ‘Skydance stands with Israel,’ and the Ellisons’ support for the country goes part of the way to explaining the hiring of Weiss.”
According to Israeli newspaper Haaretz, Larry Ellison even offered Netanyahu membership on the board of Oracle in 2021.
As Drop Site News reported, in 2015 Israel’s then ambassador to the UN, Ron Prosor, asked Ellison whether Marco Rubio had “passed your scrutiny” and whether they had discussed Israel. Ellison replied that the meeting went well and that “Marco will be a great friend for Israel.” Ellison subsequently hosted a Rubio fundraiser and put $5m into a super PAC supporting him.
And as for Safra Catz, the subject of the Ruffalo video, she wrote the following in an email to former Israeli prime minister Ehud Barak in 2015:

> “We have all been horrified by the growth of the BDS movement in college campuses and have concluded that we have to fight this battle before the kids even get to college. We believe that we have to embed the love and respect for Israel in the American culture. That means getting the message to the American people in a way they can consume it.”
Need I go on?
These are unbelievably rich pro-Israel activists with direct, extensive links to Israel and to Netanyahu himself. They are going to wield massive power over US media and entertainment - indeed they already do. That is a fact, and it is not antisemitic to say this. It is not an attack on Jewish people to state the facts about these specific very wealthy and very powerful individuals.
Subscribe now

## Ruffalo hits back
Now Ruffalo fired back with the following statement, which is worth reading in full:

-
- It so far has 161,000 reposts, 856,000 likes and has been seen nearly 30 million times.
Subscribe now

## The attempt to equate Israel with Jewish people
So in that context, what about this post by Jonathan Greenblatt, who heads the Anti-Defamation League, which routinely equates opposition to Israel’s crimes with antisemitism:

-
- “Sickening”? What qualifies as “sickening” in anything Ruffalo says? Let’s be clear about what’s sickening: Israel wiping Gaza from the earth, slaughtering about 1 in 20 of its inhabitants by direct violence, and destroying its hospitals, schools, mosques, churches and universities.
Note how Greenblat doesn’t even say Israel, he says “the Jewish state” in order to promote the agenda of equating Israel with Jewish people. There is no antisemitic rhetoric in what Ruffalo said at all at all, and neither are there baseless claims about Israel’s monstrous crimes.
What is antisemitic is equating Jewish people with the crimes of Israel. The polling finds that 61% of Jewish Americans think Israel has committed war crimes, while 39% think it has committed genocide – rising to 50% among younger Jewish Americans.
Read what Hannah Einbinder - an Emmy-award winning Jewish American actor - had to say:

-
- The truth is Ruffalo is being smeared because he opposes the genocide, backing a ceasefire way back in October 2023.
Subscribe now

## Then came another smear
Here’s this example from Hadley Freeman, a columnist at The Times. She posted a picture of Mark Ruffalo wearing the Artists4Ceasefire badge, and wrote:

-
- What on earth is she talking about?
Back in March 2024, even pro-Israel propagandist website IsraellyCool wrote a post entitled: “A Plea to My Fellow Israel Advocates: Leave The Fake News Sharing to Our Adversaries”.
It then wrote:

> “While I think these celebrities are absolutely wrong in calling for a ceasefire, the claim that the red pin symbol derives from the Ramallah lynching is not based in fact.
“Artists4Ceasefire explain the symbol as such:
“The Artists4Ceasefire enamel pin is composed of a red background to symbolize the urgency of the call to save lives. The orange hand conveys the beautiful community of people from all backgrounds that have come together in support of centering our shared humanity. The heart being cradled in the center of the hand is an invitation for us to lead with our hearts, always, to lead with love. When we lead with love, we understand that all of our fellow beings deserve to be loved and protected.
“True, the pin design is reminiscent of the bloodied hands, and pointing that out as an irony is absolutely valid and useful. But to state as fact something that is based on resemblance alone – and does not seem logical – is an own goal.”
When I corrected Hadley Freeman’s outrageous smear, she blocked me on X and posted: “Wow, an OJ pile on. What is this, 2019?”
In other words, she accused me of being a bully after I corrected her for smearing Mark Ruffalo for opposing genocide.
She has since deleted her original tweet, but with no correction.
Subscribe now

## The new McCarthyism
The truth is: this is just the latest example of the biggest attack on free speech since McCarthyism.
Across the Western world, people have been smeared, deplatformed, sacked, arrested, violently assaulted by the state, imprisoned and deported for opposing Israel’s genocide.
Yet public opinion has decisively shifted against Israel. These two facts are linked. The strategy is straightforward: use fear to prevent public opinion from being acted on.
But you can only turn the world upside down for so long.
Help us take on the pro-war, pro-genocide, pro-injustice mainstream media by becoming a subscriber.

reads.title: Canada Is Right, The USA Cannot Be Trusted
reads.subtitle: Others Must Act Like
reads.body:
Hi All,
First an announcement. I will be doing an emergency Substack Live on Canada-US relations with Bob Rae tonight at 1800 UK time/1300 EST. I can think of no one better with whom to discuss the Canadian position at this moment. Here is a link so that you can attend.
A few people have asked me to write something about the US-Canada dispute (which is about far more than trade, it is about Canada’s right to exist as a sovereign state). On the one hand I actually was worried because it strikes me as such a destructive and self-harming move by the US Government that all I would end up doing is string together a series of superlatives about how profoundly stupid this all is. That being said, it is happening and it is more important than people realize. As such, it could be useful to have a piece on what we are seeing and divide it into three sections.
Canada Is Right
The US Cannot (and Should Not) Be Trusted By Any State
Other States Must Act Like Canada
The upshot of all of this is that what Canada is doing is exactly how all states should deal with the USA in its present state (and probably for a while afterwards). The Canadian response contrasts to a year and a half of kowtowing and appeasement of an evil and stupid USA by others, particularly American allies. That latter policy has failed and made things worse. The only positive of what we are seeing now is that, knowing how weak the USA actually is—Canada might win in the end.
We can only hope so.
Phillips’s Newsletter is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.

## Canada Is Right
If there was one line that summarized why Canada was right to reject the trade deal with the Trump administration that the latter was trying to foist on it, it was this by Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney.
“We’ve recognized from the start that America has changed. We recognize that sometimes, its signature is written in pencil.”
The “sometimes” is actually too kind.
Canada is faced with a USA that is now fundamentally dishonest and rapacious. Moreover, it is faced with a US government that denies its ultimate right to exist and speaks openly (and regularly) about how Canada should be annexed into the USA. Just to reinforce this latter point, Natalie Harp tweeted about Canada as a state just yesterday.

-
- I actually asked an AI how many times since his inauguration Trump has spoken of making Canada a US state, and it responded: “No one keeps an official tally, and reporters describe it as too frequent to count.”
That being said, even a cursory examination will show that it has happened almost monthly since the start of Trump’s second term. Moreover the threats were regularly tied in with ominous talk of hitting Canada with crippling tariffs if it did not join the USA. Here are just some examples from the first six months of his second presidency:

- 1 Feb 2025 — Trump says Canada should become the 51st state because of  “Much lower taxes, and far better military protection.”

- Feb–Mar 2025 — Trump repeated the “Governor Trudeau” jibes and claimed that the US-Canada border is an “artificial line.”

- 11 Mar 2025 — Trump threatened Canada with steel and aluminium tariffs unless it becomes the “cherished Fifty First State.”

- Apr 2025 — asked by TIME whether he was joking, Trump replied: “Actually, no, I’m not.”

- 28 Apr 2025 — Canadian election-day, Trump urged Canadians to “elect the man” who could make Canada “the cherished 51st” with zero tariffs.

- Mar/Apr 2025 — Trump raised Canada joining the USA directly with Carney on their first phone call (Carney later confirmed this).

- 6 May 2025 — In the Oval Office, after Carney said Canada “is not for sale”, Trump replies: “Never say never.”

- June 2025 — Trump on Fox News: “Frankly, Canada should be the 51st state, it really should.”

The negotiations between Canada and the USA can only be seen in that light. The US included such onerous demands on Canada that it can only be seen as an attempt to destroy Canada’s independence and force the country into the USA. These were not trade negotiations in the normal sense; they were attempts to interfere deeply in Canadian internal affairs and basically transfer much of Canada’s ability to govern itself, to Washington DC. There are a number of lists that are circulating that supposedly show these demands, but none are of the quality that I believe that they can be taken as truth. However one thing is pretty clear: the US was actually asking to restrict Canadian sovereignty in these talks.
Add this all together and it is clear how right Canada is in not making a deal with the USA at this time. The Canadians understand (indeed they understood far earlier than other powers) that the USA has changed fundamentally and no deal agreed with the USA is actually a deal—it is simply a short term truce with the Trump administration. The US has a clear goal, the absorption of Canada, and as such all negotiations must be seen in this light.
I am sorry for all these lists, but you need to see how repetitive, threatening and unreliable the US has been in its dealings with Canada to understand this. I can say, in my recent trips, that too many Americans have internalized Trump’s psychopathology. That means that they quickly overlook when he acts horribly and latch onto the moments of quiet. That was really the case over Greenland. When I was in America for a long time this April, many Americans I spoke too looked at the Greenland crisis as a short-term event that passed in January 2026, not understanding that it had had a fundamental and long-term impact on how European states see the USA. It was not over quickly, as the Americans seemed to think.
Anyway, here is a list with the different tariff threats bolded, from only a six month period (April-October 2025).

- April 2025—Automotive Sector Tariffs: Coinciding with the April 2 “Liberation Day” rollouts, the US enacted a threatened 25% tariff on Canadian automobiles and auto parts entering the US market, prompting counter-tariffs from Ottawa on non-CUSMA-compliant vehicles.

- June 2025—Steel and Aluminum Escalation: Trump escalated Section 232 national security metal tariffs, threatening and enacting a doubling of duties on Canadian steel and aluminum from 25% to 50%.

- June 2025—Digital Services Tax Retaliation Threat: Trump threatened to terminate bilateral trade negotiations and impose sweeping retaliatory tariffs against Canada if it implemented its planned Digital Services Tax (DST), leading Canada to withdraw the legislation to preserve talks.

- July-August 2025—General Non-CUSMA Tariff Hike to 35%: Following warnings that Ottawa was not making sufficient concessions, Trump signed an executive order increasing the baseline emergency tariff on non-CUSMA-compliant Canadian goods from 25% to 35%, while threatening a 40% transshipment penalty on goods routed through Canada to evade US duties.

- October 2025—Provincial Advertising Surcharge Threat: In response to a US-broadcast advertising campaign sponsored by the Ontario government opposing American protectionism, Trump threatened an additional 10% punitive tariff and briefly suspended negotiations until the ad campaign was pulled.
Written in pencil indeed.
Canada was being asked to commit suicide by the USA, and had no alternative but to reject that. And the Canadian government is right on the fundamentals. Any deal on the terms being offered would only have been followed up with greater demands later, demands that have one ending point: the ending of Canada as a sovereign nation.
Canada is right
Share

## The US Cannot (and Should Not) Be Trusted By Any State
What the Canadians have discovered is that the USA cannot be trusted. This needs some discussion. All states lie and deceive. That is nothing new. Indeed, one element of successful diplomacy is the effective and well-placed strategic lie. However, if your entire policy is to lie, all the time and with malice, it makes a mockery of international relations.

reads.title: Weekend Update #199: Ukraine’s Campaign Against Russian Oil Infrastructure Should Be The Focus
reads.subtitle: The Trump Con Comes To Its Natural Conclusion, More Time For Putin: Fedorov Calls For Ukrainian Elections
reads.body:
Hi All,
I am starting this Weekend Update with a little pre-announcement. Next week will be my 200th weekend update—which is something that rather boggles the mind. As always it will be free, that will never change. However, I was thinking that if you wanted to make a donation to Come Back Alive to mark the moment, that this would be an excellent thing. I was talking with the people from CBA and they have put together this link just for people wanting to make such a donation to mark the 200th Weekend Update.
Come Back Alive: Weekend Update #200 Donation.
The area of CBA being supported in this case will be one of the overlooked areas of the charity, and that is its running costs. CBA usually raises money for its special projects, Dronefall, UGVs, the various training academies, etc. However, what is often missed is the support for the administration of the charity. If you do want to give to mark the 200th WU, I would be delighted. Any amount, however small, will be most welcome.
Phillips’s Newsletter is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.

There will also be a Substack Live with leading voice from CBA not long after Weekend Update #200, and that person will be taking questions from the audience. Please do join us.
Speaking of Substack Lives, as I was so overwhelmed with questions in the AMA session (and then failed to answer them all before going on vacation), I will hold a Substack Live session to take questions this Friday (time to be announced). I will take questions from paying subscribers and do as many as I can. It is the least I could do after the AMA debacle!
OK, let’s get to the update. On Friday I sent out this piece on airpower that caused a little stir. People have called it the anti-Wildberries campaign, which I suppose is partly right. However, the key thing was that it called for focus in airpower and argued that signalling (showing capabilities) is usually a failure and that the best way to use airpower is to deconstruct strategic systems which underpin warfighting.
The article made the point that Ukraine needed to focus continually on Russia’s fuel system (refineries, pipelines, shipping) and that campaigns against Wildberries and the like often have much less strategic effect than understood (in that they do not damage warfighting potential). This week there were a number of examples and arguments about just how vulnerable Russia’s fuel system happens to be and it makes sense to lead on that.

-
- The Russian Novokuibyshevskyi oil refinery, burning after an attack from just a day ago.Otherwise, the last piece of the Trump con that started in early July came apart this week, when it was reported that Trump had actually blocked Starlink from helping Ukraine in its campaign to attack Russian communications. Now, as it was a con, this was always going to happen, and it finally was confirmed. What that means, of course, is that the real winner from all this, Vladimir Putin, got more time. In the end, however, there was one glimmer of hope—Ukraine attacked what they wanted to regardless, and might have had success.
Lastly a brief update on the Fedorov situation. He rather controversially called for Ukrainian elections this week—a sign that he knows he is not coming back under Zelensky. It was controversial.
Share

## Ukraine’s Campaign Against Russian Oil Infrastructure Should Be The Focus
On August 21/22 the Ukrainians hit the Russian Novokuibyshevskyi oil refinery in Samara Oblast. This facility is located about 1000 miles from Ukraine. This attack came just one day after the Ukrainians attacked another major refinery in Perm, which is also located about 1000 miles from Ukraine.
It is an indication of a recent uptick and return to refinery attacks, which is sometimes overlooked in the discussion of the Wildberries campaign, etc.
However, as this week showed, not so much in these attacks but in some other data that has been emerging, the campaign on Russia’s oil infrastructure is beginning to have strategic effect. If Ukraine can keep it up, expand it, and hit the same targets multiple times (either preventing repair or degrading quick repairs) Russia’s oil system could head towards failure.
Almost two and a half years ago (yikes, has it been so long?) I summarized both the advantages and challenges of such a campaign against Russian fuel, showing that the key thing was not flashy one off attacks, but repeated attacks to stop repairs and reconstitution.
Here was a summary from that piece.
In other words, don’t get fooled by dramatic pictures. An oil production system can be repaired and slack in the system can be made up for what is temporarily lost in other areas. That’s why I harp on stocks above. Ukraine has to keep this up for a while and attack (and re-attack) numerous facilities for this to work. It is not easy.
Now, the issue Ukraine has faced is from that point it has not consistently and repeatedly hit the same refineries to put them out of action for good. It has ramped up the campaign and then ramped down the campaign, hit new refineries but then, frustratingly, seemed to forget about other refineries that it had earlier hit.
Finally in the last few months, the Ukrainians have started doing what needs to be done. Here is a chart from Bloomberg data that I included in the Friday piece.

-
- Now the attack rate is still not ideal. There was a severe and regrettable decline in attacks on refineries for two months in the Spring of 2026, but the focus on the whole oil infrastructure system is now clearer and the refineries, pipelines, and port attacks are starting to cause a buckling of the system.
When it comes to the refineries, as I tried to say a few years ago, the repeat attacks are finally eating away at Russia’s ability to repair these facilities. Here is a chart I put together of attacks on Russia’s largest 11 refineries this year. I have checked the data, but some of it comes solely from Ukrainian sources (which have been reliable, but I wanted to point that out).

-
- CDU is the central distillation unit—the cracking tank—and if you want to know more about the importance of hitting certain vital parts of a refinery, this piece laid that out almost two years ago, but could be a helpful refresher.
What seems to be happening, finally, is that Russia’s ability to keep repairing these facilities is losing its integrity. Mikhail Khodorkovsky, who ran the largest of Russia’s oil companies before Putin forced him out, put together this fascinating thread on what might be going on in Russia’s fuel system and the problems with repair. In a nutshell, the Russians are trying to get by with constant, short term repairs, or patching. However that can only get them so far, and at some point the system will start to fail. When that happens, the results will be pretty dramatic. Here is most of the thread.

-
- This recent pick up in attacks is once again leading to a Russian rationing crisis for fuel. Here is how that has progressed over the last few months looking at numbers of Russian regions with rationing of some sort.

-
- Here is the Meduza article with the most recent update and examples of how this situation is spreading.
Now this is hitting Russian income and that could get much worse. With refinery coming offline, Russia has had to switch to exporting crude (it must keep all the refined fuels for its own consumption) and even having to purchase refined fuels from the world market and import them into Russia.
So it is exporting less profitable fuel and having to spend desperately needed capital importing fuel from the outside. Now, Trump’s War with Iran has provided a cushion for Putin by keeping the prices for crude very high, meaning that states like India and China are buying whatever Russia can sell. However if the refining campaign can be joined by an equally effective Port campaign (remember, the USA is putting pressure on Ukraine to keep oil flowing out of Russian ports) then even this will not work—and Russia’s financial crisis will hit a death spiral. It will have to import expensive refined fuels and be able to ship out much less crude.
This is why this campaign is so important. It is not because it affects Russian morale, or causes inconvenience, it is because ultimately it is the best way to take away the one thing all war machines need—money. Russia without the ability to raise money by exporting fuel is not only not a great power, it is not a medium economic power. It is an economic basket case.
That is why this fuel system should be the focus.
Note—that does not mean the only thing attacked, just always the highest priority. After that I would put communications, armaments production and strategic transport. However going through all this would require another piece.
Share

## The Trump Con Comes To Its Natural Conclusion, More Time For Putin
Guess what? After all that waiting it turns out that Trump decided not to help Ukraine by pushing Elon Musk to let the Ukrainians have Starlink access to attack strategic targets in Russia. The FT had a story on that development this week, which has been summarized in other outlets like this.
This was the second part of the Trump con that has gone on this summer.
The first part, which fell apart a few weeks ago, was that he was going to grant Ukraine a license to build Patriot interceptors. This was all part of the extremely misleading reporting that saturated the press in late July, that Trump was “warming” towards Ukraine, that Trump was so impressed by Ukrainian resolve that he was going to help them, that he was, finally, going to hammer Putin.
Of course none of it was ever true, and the press has moved on after embarrassing itself by writing the same, wrong, stories on the subject. However, here we are, almost two months after the con started and absolutely nothing has changed. No Starlink help for Ukraine, no Patriot licenses, no new large supply of Patriot interceptors—and no prospect of Ukraine getting any of this.
Now this con was brutally effective for Putin. The Ukrainians actually believed there was a real possibility of Trump giving them both Starlink access and Patriot interceptors and a license. They worked for a long time preparing their pitch, put together plans in case they were successful, and invested a good deal of emotional and political energy into their efforts.
And here we are almost two months later and it did not happen, but it should be clear by now that it was never going to happen. They were just, as they have been for the last 19 months, being strung along.
And the beneficiary is the Russians. All this means is we have had two more months of blue smoke and mirrors, with people wondering if Trump might help the Ukrainians, and in the meantime Russia can bombard an almost defenseless Ukraine. This week, for instance, it was reported that Ukraine had “run dry” of Patriot Interceptors.
The effects of being defenseless to Russian (and North Korean) ballistic missiles, which is what this means, is now crystal clear and getting worse by the week. Ukrainian civilian casualties are trending steadily upwards as the Russians can launch mass attacks knowing some of their missiles will definitely get through and other systems can therefore deal with overwhelmed Ukrainian air defenses. This was how Ukraine’s foreign minister summarized the situation for July 2026.
In July alone, Russia killed at least 437 civilians and injured 2,610 across Ukraine — the highest monthly civilian toll since May 2022. 17 children were killed and another 166 injured, the highest monthly number of child casualties since April 2022.
Having more time to do this is Putin’s key objective—which is why the con is so devastating. Most importantly for the Russians, Putin wants to have all the winter of 2026-2027 to bombard a defenseless Ukraine—to make last winter’s terrible bombardment with its heat and power outages, seem mild in comparison. This is now being admitted by Ukrainians. This week, Serhii Kyslytsia, First Deputy Head of Zelensky’s Presidential Office was quoted as saying.
"Putin has no desire whatsoever to sit down at the negotiating table now, and after winter begins and until it ends, that is, at least until mid-March, he will have even less motivation. Because he believes that Ukrainians are not strong enough as a nation to survive this winter."
This is why it is vital to call what we are and have always seen as a Trump “con”. It is why, for months, I have trying to communicate that this is all about leaving Ukraine as exposed and vulnerable as possible in the upcoming winter. Now, the Ukrainians are admitting that publicly itself. And that is why I wrote two days after the Patriot license con was announced that all that was really happening was that Ukraine was being set up to have the crap kicked out of it this winter. Here is a quote from that piece.
The fact that Russia seems to be upping its strike rate with three attacks on Kyiv in six days, just as it is clear that Ukraine is running out of Patriots interceptors, shows how the Russians are aware of the help Trump has and will continue to provide for them. For at least a year, if not longer, they can do a great deal of damage with their ballistic missiles knowing that the Ukrainians have few options to shoot them down. That is a massive strategic gift that the USA has given to Russia. Trump has provided Putin at least one more whole winter, and possibly two or three (the Japanese after many years of licensing are only making 30 Patriot PAC-3 interceptors, the ones Ukraine needs, annually), to attack what he wants.
In other words, it is not harmless optimism to act like Trump might help Ukraine, it is falling for a deadly, pro-Putin maneuver that is and will increasingly lead to Ukrainian suffering.
And it delays Ukraine doing what it should and restrains Europeans from doing what they could. We have had one example this week. One of the reasons the Ukrainians were desperate to get Trump to give them Starlink access because they wanted to attack a new Russian sattellite that is about to go into operations and could give the Russians much greater accuracy within Ukraine (where they do not have Starlink).  They believed that they needed Starlink to do this effectively.
Actually, they might have been wrong on this. A week ago, probably understanding that US aid was not going to be forthcoming, the Ukrainians attacked and seem to have heavily damaged the facility being prepared to deploy this new Russian system.

-
- The Russian Space Center in Samara, Attacked By Ukraine A Week AgoThe Ukrainians must stop investing any hope and effort in getting Trump to support them. They must stop falling for the con, and the western press should at least stop pretending the con is not happening, to help them make that choice.
Share

## Fedorov Calls For Ukrainian Elections
For now the situation with Mykhailo Fedorov, the one time and excellent Ukrainian defense minister, seems to have reached a new equilibrium. The Ukrainian parliament (Rada) has approved Yevhenii Khmara as his replacement. So legally we have a successor and for now Zelensky seems determined to keep Fedorov away from power.  That seems unlikely to change for a while.
Fedorov is obviously frustrated and this week, while his replacement was being confirmed, made an audacious, and probably misconceived political gambit. He called, in a Youtube video, for a new Ukrainian election.
While I can understand his frustration, it was, from what I am hearing from Ukrainians I trust, a major mistake. An election is not going to happen now, not least because Ukraine cannot protect itself from Russian missiles, which would make any campaign a possible death trap. Moreover, Ukrainians do not want an election until and unless there is a lengthy stop in the fighting that will allow for a real campaign. Even some of Fedorov’s supporters were surprised, therefore, that he made this move.
So two things can be true. Fedorov can still be an excellent defense minister (and Ukraine would benefit from having him in post) and it can still be a major mistake of his to call for elections.
The one upshot of this is that, for now, the issue is settled. He is not coming back.
Have a good rest of the weekend everyone.
Thanks for reading Phillips’s Newsletter! This post is public so feel free to share it.
