reads.subtitle: Drop Site Daily: August 21, 2026
reads.body:
- Residents carry containers while queuing for potable water from a tanker, amid recurring shortages and power outages, in Matanzas, Cuba, on August 6, 2026. Photo by AFP via Getty Images.Friday, August 21, 2026 – Fifteen-year-old boy dies after being shot in the head by Israeli soldiers in Gaza. Israeli forces and settlers kill two Palestinians, wound several others in occupied West Bank attacks. Drop Site reports on detained Palestinian journalist. Hamas is “fully committed” to Board of Peace roadmap, official says. Qatar, Turkey, and Egypt condemn Israeli attacks on Gaza. European leaders condemn Israeli settlement expansion. Turkey seeks Interpol red notice for Netanyahu over Global Sumud Flotilla attack. Three Palestinian parties in Israel revive Joint List ahead of October Knesset election. U.S. threatens countries trading with Iran with “economic oblivion.” China registers opposition to U.S. economic campaign against Iran. Oil traffic through Hormuz remains constrained. Iranian crude oil offers to Chinese buyers decline. Israeli army continues attacks in Lebanon despite “ceasefire” agreement. Explosions heard over Tyre as Prime Minister Nawaf Salam tells army its deployment restores state “sovereignty, authority and prestige.” U.S. issues sanctions on Hezbollah. Progressive Aisha Wahab wins California special election, dealing blow to AIPAC-backed opponent. Emails reveal ICE quietly coordinated with Iran on deportation flights. Transgender migrants in ICE detention losing rights, medical care, New York Times finds. Department of Homeland Security spied on at least five Midwest churches amid anti-ICE activist probe, court records show. Texas Gov. Greg Abbott targets Muslim washing stations at airports. Missouri judge allows Trump-backed congressional map for November election. Research finds over 150 Polymarket wallets likely traded on inside U.S. military information. Private prison giant GEO Group donated $1.4 million to pro-Trump PAC after landing major ICE contracts. Ebola virus outbreak in DRC “growing exponentially.” U.S. imposes new Cuba sanctions, detains Americans returning from island. Former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan sent back to prison hours after hospital visit. Hundreds protest against Tunisian President Kais Saied. Human Rights Watch: Russian paramilitaries “summarily killed” nine Mali civilians, including four children. Ukraine hits Russian oil and power sites in overnight drone barrage, blacking out much of Crimea. RSF attacks kill six, displace over 1,000 in Sudan’s North Kordofan. U.S. deportees arrive in Liberia. Syria weighs joining security pact with Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi Arabia. Hong Kong Tiananmen vigil organizers convicted under national security law. Judge rules Palestine Action did not violate UK terrorism laws.
This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday – Friday

## Palestine

- 15-year-old boy dies after being shot in the head by Israel in Gaza: A 15-year-old Palestinian boy died on Thursday after being shot by Israeli troops in Beit Lahia, northern Gaza. Footage appears to show him shot in the head.

- Israeli forces and settlers kill two Palestinians, wound several others in occupied West Bank attacks:

- Hebron: A 17-year-old Palestinian boy was killed after being shot in the chest by armed Israeli settlers during an attack on homes in Khirbet Hamroush, northeast of Hebron, WAFA reported. A 70-year-old man was also shot and wounded, and settlers burned down a home. In southern Hebron, settlers attacked homes near Al-Dhahiriya and Al-Samu, injuring five Palestinians, stealing sheep and attacking a Palestinian Red Crescent ambulance, preventing it from reaching the wounded. Israeli forces later arrested four Palestinians in Shaab Al-Butum, including a father and son, and three others during a raid on Beit Ummar.

- Jenin: Israeli forces shot and killed Fathi Hazem, a 58-year-old retired police colonel in the Palestinian National Security Forces, during a raid on his home in central Jenin and withheld his body. An eyewitness told AFP, “They shot him seven times in front of his 10-year-old son. They dragged him down the stairs and took him with them.” Two of Hazem’s other sons were killed by the Israeli military in 2022. In Zababdeh, south of Jenin, Israeli forces shot a 14-year-old boy in the chest and back during a raid. Israeli forces also hung Israeli flags along several points of the Jenin–Nablus road.

- Nablus: Israeli settlers attacked the Bula Al-Hawa area, east of Nablus, beating a Palestinian.

- Drop Site reports on detained Palestinian journalist: After more than two years in Israeli detention, the first photo of Palestinian journalist Mohammed Arab emerged on Monday. Israeli forces seized Arab from Gaza’s Al-Shifa Medical Complex on March 18, 2024.

- “They are calling on us using the quadcopters. Pray for me, and take care of the children,” Arab told his wife Wafaa Abu Al-Laban in their final conversation.

- “Mohammed’s health is very, very poor,” Abu Al-Laban told Drop Site’s Abdel Qader Sabbah. Arab was subjected to severe abuse at Sde Teiman and forced to remain on his knees for prolonged periods, causing a slipped disc and serious back problems. His eyesight also deteriorated after his glasses were taken away, his lawyer said.

- After more than two years in detention, Arab told his lawyer that seeing his own face had become a dream. “I just want to know what I look like,” he said. A petition had to be filed to obtain underwear and a mirror for him.

- Watch Abdel Qader Sabbah’s video report on Mohamed Arab for Drop Site here.

- Hamas is “fully committed” to Board of Peace roadmap, official says: Basem Naim, a senior Hamas official, told CNN on Thursday that the group remains fully committed to the “agreed version” of the “Board of Peace” roadmap for Gaza, noting that the group believes that the roadmap satisfactorily handles the decommissioning of its weapons, the future of its tunnels, and implementation timelines.

- President Donald Trump’s envoy Nickolay Mladenov had pledged to secure Israel’s approval for the deal, Naim said, but Israel has since rejected the deal and carried out massacres in Gaza in a deliberate attempt to derail it.

- Naim also told CNN that Board of Peace mediators and Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner are asking Hamas to be “sensitive” to Benjamin Netanyahu’s political position ahead of Israel’s upcoming election over the already-agreed Gaza roadmap. “As a Palestinian, I am not in a position to pay the price from the bodies and blood and the lives of our people in order to secure the victory of Netanyahu’s election,” Naim noted to CNN in response.

- Qatar, Turkey, and Egypt condemn Israeli attacks on Gaza: Qatar, Egypt, and Turkey “strongly condemned” recent Israeli attacks on Gaza that have killed civilians, including women and children, in a joint statement Wednesday.

- The statement said the intensification of Israeli attacks “undermines regional and international efforts at a critical juncture,” as work continues to implement the plan to end the war, including the Board of Peace’s meeting with Israeli officials. They stressed that Israel must “fully comply with all its obligations under the ceasefire agreement” and refrain from actions that could escalate tensions.

- European leaders condemn Israeli settlement expansion: The leaders of the UK, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway and Canada condemned Israel’s decision to issue construction tenders for the E1 settlement project in the occupied West Bank in a joint statement on Thursday.

- The statement urges Israel to “retract these plans immediately” and halt settlement expansion.

- It also warns businesses not to bid on the tenders, citing possible “legal and reputational consequences” and the risk of involvement in “serious breaches of international law.”

- Turkey seeks Interpol red notice for Netanyahu over Global Sumud Flotilla attack: Turkey asked Interpol to issue a red notice for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over the Israeli attack on activists aboard the Global Sumud Flotilla carrying humanitarian aid to Gaza, Justice Minister Akin Gürlek said Friday via Anadolu Agency. Gürlek said proceedings are continuing before an Istanbul court against 35 defendants over the attack in international waters and the detention of activists.

- Arrest warrants were issued for Netanyahu and Israeli official Afek Moskovitch on July 14 on charges including genocide, crimes against humanity, torture, aggravated deprivation of liberty and hijacking, prompting the Justice Ministry to request Interpol red notices.

- Three Palestinian parties in Israel revive Joint List ahead of October Knesset election: Three Palestinian parties in Israel, Hadash, Balad, and Ta’al, announced a reconstituted Joint List on Wednesday ahead of the October 27 Knesset election.

- The list will be led by Hadash’s Yousef Jabareen, followed by Ta’al’s Ahmad Tibi and Balad’s Sami Abu Shehadeh, with the parties targeting at least 10 seats and competing against the United Arab List led by Mansour Abbas.

- Balad deputy secretary-general Yousef Tatur said the party made concessions to reach the agreement given “the gravity of the current moment,” citing Israel’s genocide in Gaza, West Bank displacement, and attacks in Jerusalem, and called on Palestinian voters with Israeli citizenship who are eligible to vote to help “turn unity into a real force on the ground.”

## Iran

- U.S. threatens countries trading with Iran with “economic oblivion”: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Thursday that Washington would impose the “toughest sanctions in history” on Iran following Trump’s declaration of “economic warfare.”

- “The economic pressure means that we are going to all of our allies, and this is going to be the greatest coordinated economic isolation in the history of the world,” Bessent told CNBC, noting that all countries will now be judged as “either with us or against” the U.S. based on their economic relationship with Iran.

- “If you insist on doing business with them, either transferring money or buying their oil, they are doing seaborne ship transfers, then the US Treasury and the U.S. government, they will put its full might and force toward enforcing against you,” Bessent told CNBC.

- Separately, Bessent noted his confusion at rising oil prices, saying that the U.S. had “asymmetric information” and he was “not sure why oil has popped up on this.”

- Vice President JD Vance said Thursday that the war with Iran had entered “a new phase where the most effective tool we have is the economic pressure we can impose on them.” “It will be a delicate dance,” he added, because Iran “will try to put economic pressure on us.”

- Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf called for a plan to overcome what he described as “cruel sanctions” following the U.S. Treasury announcement. Speaking during a visit to Iraq, Ghalibaf said Iran and other Muslim countries possess significant resources and raw materials that their “enemies are coming to plunder,” and urged Baghdad to cooperate with Tehran in confronting the sanctions.

- China registers opposition to U.S. economic campaign against Iran: Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Lin Jian said on Friday that the newest round of U.S. economic pressure would “not help to resolve” the conflict in the Middle East.

- Lin called on all sides to address tensions through political and diplomatic means.

- China has repeatedly rejected unilateral U.S. sanctions, arguing that measures not authorized by the UN Security Council lack standing in international law.

- Oil traffic through Hormuz remains constrained: Kpler recorded 10.73 million barrels of west-to-east liquid tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz from August 14–20, an average of just 1.53 million barrels per day, a sharp contrast from the 10 million barrels per day figure that two U.S. officials gave Axios.

- Only 14 outbound tankers were observed during the entire week, with no recorded traffic on August 14 or 17, according to the maritime tracking firm.

- Kpler cautions that its figures may change as more vessel-position data becomes available, including from ships traveling with their tracking systems switched off. But the currently observed traffic is nowhere near the scale Washington described.

- Iranian crude oil offers to Chinese buyers decline: Offers of Iranian crude to Chinese buyers have fallen this week, Reuters reported on Friday, while prices have jumped.

- The number of planned deliveries for September and October declined from July and August, and barrels shipped earlier have already been sold.

- Crude oil, which is usually sold at a lower price, is now being sold at premiums, Reuters reported.

## Lebanon

- Israeli army continues attacks in Lebanon despite “ceasefire” agreement: Israeli forces set off a “massive explosion,” conducted in two stages, in the area between the towns of Arnoun and Kfar Tebnit, in the Nabatieh district in southern Lebanon, the Lebanese National News Agency reported on Friday.

- In Tyre (Sour), Israeli attacks were reported in the Mansouri-Majdal Zoun area, according to the NNA, with the Israeli military firing artillery shells on Mansouri.

- Israeli soldiers also fired on Khiam, where Israeli forces had blown up a house. Israeli warplanes also struck the outskirts of Baraashit, in the Bint Jbeil district, targeting a house, early Friday morning.

- Israeli forces bombarded the strategic Ali Taher hill in southern Lebanon for more than five hours overnight, with artillery fire beginning after 11 p.m. and continuing until around 5 a.m., L’Orient Today reported.

- Explosions heard over Tyre as PM Salam tells army its deployment restores state “sovereignty, authority and prestige”: Explosions were heard over the southern Lebanese city of Tyre (Sour) on Friday as Prime Minister Nawaf Salam delivered a speech at the Benoit Barakat Barracks, Lebanon’s National News Agency reported. Speaking as Israeli attacks on Lebanon continue, Salam said restoring sovereignty requires “one strong army” and bringing all of southern Lebanon under the authority of the state. He said the Lebanese state and its constitutional institutions must regain the “decision of war and peace,” describing the army’s deployment in the south as the restoration of state “sovereignty, authority and prestige.”

- U.S. issues sanctions on Hezbollah: The U.S. Treasury Department sanctioned 10 people it says form a network smuggling cash to Hezbollah, and redesignated Hezbollah itself as operating “under the command” of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Quds Force (IRGC-QF), OFAC announced Thursday.

- The Treasury Department accused the network of using couriers on commercial flights between Lebanon, Turkey, the UAE, and Iran to move “up to hundreds of millions of dollars,” giving Hezbollah a channel outside the banking system to obtain foreign currency and evade sanctions.

- A State Department official said the redesignation is meant to show Hezbollah is “not a stand-alone operation” but acts for Iran.

- Hezbollah responded to the sanctions on Friday morning, rejecting its characterization as “under the command” of the IRGC, adding it did not need anyone to certify its Lebanese identity or patriotism, and describing its relationship with Iran as a “close and fraternal” relationship.

- It described the move as part of longstanding U.S. policies aimed at targeting Hezbollah through political, financial, and security pressure, which it said was intended to “protect the security of the Israeli enemy,” and said the sanctions would “not deter” its fight against Israel.

## U.S. News

- Progressive Aisha Wahab wins California special election, dealing blow to AIPAC-backed opponent: State Senator Aisha Wahab defeated transit official Melissa Hernandez in the special election to fill former Representative Eric Swalwell’s House seat, despite Hernandez’s backing from the American Israel Public Affairs Committee’s super PAC, United Democracy Project, which spent roughly $2.5 million in the race.

- Wahab, who opposes unconditional aid to Israel and has characterized Israel’s conduct in Gaza as a “genocide,” will represent the district for the remainder of the year.

- Emails reveal ICE quietly coordinated with Iran on deportation flights: Newly released emails obtained by the National Iranian American Council show U.S. immigration officials worked with Iranian government representatives to deport more than 100 Iranians on three flights between September 2025 and January 2026, with Iranian officials influencing which individuals were included on deportation manifests and ICE at times heeding last-minute requests from the Iranian Embassy, according to CBS News.

- The coordination continued even during the June 2025 U.S.-Israel war with Iran. Then-acting ICE Director Todd Lyons called Iranian repatriation a “priority” days after President Donald Trump warned Tehran residents to evacuate, and an ICE official described the deportations as a “White House priority” despite Iran’s closed airspace.

- A separate lawsuit filed by Iranian asylum seekers in July alleges ICE illegally shared confidential information with Iranian officials while the migrants were in detention.

- Trans migrants in ICE detention losing rights, medical care, NYT finds: The federal government has halted specialized care for transgender detainees at more than 10 immigration detention centers and deleted an Obama-era policy assuring the basic rights of transgender people in immigration custody, according to a Thursday report from The New York Times.

- Camila Toro de Paula, a 25-year-old transgender Venezuelan asylum seeker who has spent 11 months in a men’s facility in Jena, Louisiana,  described being assaulted, denied hormone treatment, and held in solitary confinement without consistent water access to the Times.

- Another transgender asylum seeker, Wilmar Quintero, who left her native Venezuela after being tortured by police officers for her transgender identity, described being sexually assaulted while detained in Michigan before she was deported in April.

- DHS spied on at least five Midwest churches amid anti-ICE activist probe, court records show: Court filings that emerged last week reveal DHS agents surveilled five churches in Minnesota and Michigan as part of an investigation into activists opposing ICE known as “Operation Puppet Master.”

- Undercover agents attended events at First Universalist Church of Minneapolis and University Baptist Church, with one undercover agent attending a Mixed Martial Arts class at University Baptist Church in May with a hidden audio recorder, and another agent collecting license plate information near St. John the Evangelist Episcopal Church in St. Paul during an April activist meeting.

- The revelations raise questions about whether DHS violated a February court injunction barring warrantless enforcement actions at churches.

- Texas Gov. Abbott targets Muslim washing stations at airports: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott sent a letter Friday to the heads of Houston and Dallas-Fort Worth airports alleging that their Muslim wudu washing stations constituted “religious discrimination.” Abbott, has consistently pursued anti-Muslim policies, asked the U.S. Department of Transportation to investigate and warned his office is “reviewing all grants” to entities involved, according to The Washington Post.

- Missouri judge allows Trump-backed congressional map for November election: Cole County Circuit Judge Daniel Green ruled Wednesday that Missouri’s new Republican-friendly U.S. House districts can be used in November, rejecting a bid by the group People Not Politicians to put the map to a statewide referendum.

- The redistricting, prompted by President Donald Trump’s push for Republican-led states to redraw boundaries ahead of the midterms, targets Democratic Rep. Emanuel Cleaver by splitting Kansas City among Republican-held districts and extending his 5th District into rural GOP territory, with about 59% of the district’s voters newly assigned under the plan.

- People Not Politicians executive director Richard von Glahn said the group plans to appeal to the Missouri Supreme Court.

- Missouri’s fight joins roughly a dozen lawsuits nationally over redistricting efforts that could net Republicans up to 16 additional House seats across eight states.

- Research finds over 150 Polymarket wallets likely traded on inside U.S. military information: More than 150 wallets on Polymarket International appear to have traded on insider U.S. military information, collectively earning $8 million with a 97.2% win rate on defense-related bets, according to research from the nonprofit Anti-Corruption Data Collective.

- ACDC also found that bets from these accounts appear to attract copycat wagers from larger traders and automated bots, including $200,000 and $100,000 copycat bets placed hours before June 2025 U.S. strikes on Iran.

- Private prison giant GEO Group donated $1.4 million to pro-Trump PAC after landing major ICE contracts: GEO Group’s reentry services division contributed $1.4 million to MAGA Inc., a super PAC supporting President Donald Trump, in July, according to Federal Election Commission records reviewed by The Lever, just weeks after the company secured two five-year Department of Homeland Security contracts to operate ICE detention facilities in Colorado and North Carolina worth a combined estimated $165 million in annual revenue.

- The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment recently sued GEO Group, forcing the company to allow state inspectors to investigate a tuberculosis outbreak at one of its facilities.

- More on the GEO Group’s political activities is available from The Lever here.
📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill?  Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com

## Other International News

- Ebola virus outbreak in DRC “growing exponentially”: The Ebola virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is “growing exponentially,” the UN warned on Friday. Julien Harneis, the UN’s Senior Ebola Coordinator, said in a statement that more than 2,500 people had died in the last three months, with over half of all deaths occurring in just the last 20 days. “The epidemic is spreading to an area that is bigger than France. And the outbreak is growing faster and wider than the Ebola response,” Harneis said. He also stressed the “brutal” conditions facing healthcare workers with 160 healthcare workers contracting Ebola, with 43 dying.

- U.S. imposes new Cuba sanctions, detains Americans returning from island: The Treasury and State departments announced new sanctions Thursday against nine Cuban state-owned mining, metal, and construction companies, and on the leadership of the Cuban Institute of Friendship with the Peoples, which Secretary of State Marco Rubio accused of sponsoring “a vast subversive network in the United States aimed at identifying, cultivating, and radicalizing” Americans, according to the Associated Press.

- The move follows an operation at the Miami airport last weekend in which several Americans returning from Cuba after attending events marking Fidel Castro’s 100th birthday were briefly detained and had electronic devices seized for inspection.

- Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez said that the U.S. imposed the sanctions with the “deliberate aim of harming” the country’s economy ”to prevent the provision of basic services to the population.” The measures add to an oil blockade the U.S. imposed earlier this year following the removal of Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, which has resulted in regular blackouts and medical shortages on the island.

- Imran Khan sent back to prison hours after hospital visit: Former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan was briefly hospitalized, declared medically fit, and returned to prison within hours early Friday, a move his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party said violated a Supreme Court order requiring him to remain under medical supervision until at least mid-September.

- Khan’s sister, Uzma Khan, said he told her he was being “repeatedly” tortured in prison, and party officials accused authorities of “contempt of the Supreme Court” after Khan was examined at a state-run hospital, contrary to a court order mandating that he be treated at a private facility.

- Khan has been imprisoned since August 2023 on charges he has characterized as “politically motivated.” PTI officials have announced a nationwide march, planned to take place on September 27, in response to his medical deterioration.

- Separately, Zulfikar Bukhari, a top aide to Khan, told Reuters on Thursday that the former PM would not confront army chief Asim Munir if freed, marking a significant shift in rhetoric from a party whose supporters have long rallied against the military leader they blame for Khan’s 2023 imprisonment.

- Hundreds protest against Tunisian President Kais Saied: Hundreds of protesters marched in Tunis Thursday calling for President Kais Saied’s ouster and rejecting what they called “one-man rule” and “a slide towards dictatorship,” urging the release of jailed opposition figures, activists, and journalists, Al Jazeera reported.

- The demonstration follows a similar protest on July 25 marking the anniversary of Saied’s 2021 dismissal of the government and suspension of parliament.

- Saied, a 68-year-old former constitutional lawyer elected in 2019 on an anti-corruption platform, has faced international criticism for consolidating control over the judiciary and overseeing mass trials of political opponents.

- The country has been racked by mounting economic pressure, with inflation at 5.2%, according to the World Bank. Protests have also emerged in response to widespread water and power cuts, and the environmental problems that accompanied wildfires that hit the country earlier this summer.

- HRW: Russian paramilitaries “summarily killed” nine Mali civilians, including four children: Human Rights Watch said Thursday that Russia’s Africa Corps summarily killed nine civilians, including four children, in Mali’s central Mopti region in the presence of Malian soldiers earlier last month, alleging the paramilitary group also beat dozens of people and burned at least eight homes.

- HRW said more than 100 Africa Corps fighters rounded up at least 80 men and boys in Bombori village on July 10, beating them while interrogating them about alleged ties to armed groups, before shooting six who tried to escape and executing three others in custody, one allegedly by beheading.

- The killings come amid Mali’s ongoing civil war against armed groups linked to al-Qaeda and ISIL, with Russia’s Africa Corps having become the country’s main military partner since Bamako’s relations with Western nations, particularly its former colonizer France, deteriorated following the military’s 2021 seizure of power.

- Ukraine hits Russian oil and power sites in overnight drone barrage, blacking out much of Crimea: Ukraine struck a wave of Russian energy targets overnight into Thursday, Aug. 20, in one of its heaviest long-range drone campaigns of the war, hitting oil refineries, a Black Sea export terminal, and a substation feeding occupied Crimea, according to Ukraine’s General Staff. Ukrainian drones struck a substation in Krasnodar Krai, which provides Russian-occupied Crimea with much of its power, leading to a blackout in the area overnight. Drones also struck an export terminal at Volna and a refinery in Tatarstan.

- RSF attacks kill six, displace over 1,000 in Sudan’s North Kordofan: Rapid Support Forces fighters raided the villages of Um Dareisa and Al-Shaqla in Sudan’s North Kordofan state Wednesday, killing six civilians and forcing more than 1,000 people to flee on foot to the state capital El Obeid, Sudan Tribune

reads.title: The Israeli Siege of Palestinian Families in Qusra Is Part of an Escalating Tactic
reads.subtitle: Israeli settlers and soldiers are increasingly targeting Palestinians in Area B of the occupied West Bank to force them from their homes.
reads.body:
Drop Site is a reader-funded, independent news outlet. Without your support, we can’t operate. Please consider becoming a paid subscriber or making a 501(c)(3) tax-deductible donation today.
Subscribe now

-
- Israeli soldiers and settlers have been besieging three Palestinian families in their homes in the village of Qusra in the occupied West Bank since August 9. Photo on August 14, 2026 by Issam Rimawi/Anadolu via Getty Images.RAMALLAH, Occupied West Bank—For the 12th consecutive day, three Palestinian families, comprising 10 people, including two young children, have been trapped inside their homes in the occupied West Bank, besieged and terrorized by dozens of armed Israelis—both settlers and soldiers. The family members have been stuck in separate homes, unable to shelter together or attend to their basic needs, with food supplies running dangerously low and without access to cooking gas or a fridge.
While the siege on the three families has garnered international media attention and statements of condemnation, the attack is not the first of its kind, but rather a more prominent example of a growing tactic by Israeli settlers and soldiers working in tandem to dispossess Palestinians from their homes in the West Bank. The attacks are increasingly focused on Palestinian communities in Area B, a designation under the Oslo Accords where the Palestinian Authority is nominally in charge of civil administration while Israel retains security control.
The latest Israeli siege targeted a small cluster of Palestinian homes that sit atop a hill on the edge of the village of Qusra, in the southern part of the Nablus governorate in the northern West Bank.
On the morning of August 9, armed settlers blocked off the only road leading to the homes and erected a colonial outpost directly in front of the door of one of the houses. They began pelting the homes with rocks and trying to break inside on a regular basis.
Israeli occupation forces eventually arrived on the scene and removed the outpost, but the settlers were able to erect it again, a pattern that repeated several times. And despite brief clashes with Israeli forces, the settlers were allowed to remain and continued to roam the area freely.
The settlers also cut off access to water and electricity and for more than a week prevented anyone—including emergency workers or ambulances—from reaching the families trapped inside. Qusra municipality employees were eventually allowed to repair the water and electricity lines after being initially assaulted by settlers and detained by Israeli forces.
Israeli troops have also exacerbated the situation by occupying two of the Palestinian homes they claim to be protecting.
On August 14, soldiers forced Yousef and Ruqayya Hassan and their two daughters, four-year-old Kinda and two-year-old Hour, from their home and into their neighbor’s unfinished villa, which belongs to Loui Abu Ridi, a U.S. citizen. Still unfinished, Abu Ridi’s home lacked basic furniture, including beds.
“It feels like there was a death in the family. We’re all distressed, angry and in a state of sadness,” Ruqayya told Drop Site in a phone interview.
Israeli troops occupied another neighboring home that was still under construction and belonged to Abou Ridi’s brother, Raed. The soldiers also erected a tent around twelve meters away, according to the mayor of Qusra, Abdelatheem Wadi.
“It’s the armed settlers on one hand and the military on the other,” Wadi told Drop Site, characterizing the trapped families in Qusra as being under a “double siege.”
Meanwhile, Ruqayya’s daughters fell ill and started exhibiting flu-like symptoms, with a fluctuating fever and a heavy cough. On the afternoon of August 12, Ruqayya and both her daughters were allowed to temporarily evacuate from the area in an ambulance to a medical clinic for treatment. It was when she and her daughters returned to the besieged area two days later that they found Israeli soldiers occupying their home and were ordered to move into Abu Ridi’s.
Another home belongs to Ruqayya’s brother-in-law, Rizq Hassan, who is trapped inside along with his 61-year-old mother and sister. The Israeli military has separated the families and prevented them from seeing each other.
“My daughters keep asking me why their teta (grandmother) is right next door and yet they can’t be with her. They are very distressed. How on earth can I explain what’s happening to them?” Ruqayya, adding that the psychological and physical toll was already visible in her eldest daughter. “Kinda has started urinating involuntarily. Even during the day, when she’s awake, she wets herself,” she said.

## “Complete Siege”
The fact that Abou Ridi, a U.S. citizen, was the owner of one of the homes may have helped spark statements of condemnation, including from staunchly pro-Israel U.S. officials like Ambassador Mike Huckabee, who called the settlers “Israeli terrorists” and their actions “criminal,” though Washington did nothing to intervene. Abou Ridi traveled from Ohio back to Palestine on August 17 to join his brother Qusai and his nephew who were staying in his home along with Ruqayya, her husband, and two daughters.
Those staying in Abou Ridi’s home eventually received supplies of food, water, and medicine from a UNICEF team on August 17, as well as personal care supplies for Ruqayya and her daughters. Those in Rizq Hassan’s home, which is under less of a spotlight, were not as fortunate.
“My brother-in-law’s home is under complete siege. They’re not allowed to leave the front door. They don’t have gas, or a fridge—they’re living on bread and a few canned items,” said Ruqayya. “No one is talking about them.”
Wadi, the mayor, said they are being abused by soldiers. “The aid brought in by UNICEF to Rizq Hassan’s home was left by soldiers in the yard for 24 hours in the sun, before the family was allowed to receive it, and half of it was already ruined,” Wadi told Drop Site. “There is media attention only on Loui’s home.”
The military and settler siege expanded beyond the three homes on August 13, when hundreds of Israeli occupation soldiers stormed Qusra and imposed a curfew across the entire village. Soldiers took over at least eight homes and forced their families out. According to Wadi, they severely vandalized the houses, damaging furniture and belongings.
The soldiers withdrew days later from the eight homes and the rest of the village, but they declared the area of the three besieged homes a closed military zone. Wadi estimates at least 50 to 60 soldiers remain stationed in and around the area of the besieged homes.
While the military claimed this order would be over by Tuesday evening, it remains in place, according to the residents.

-
- Israeli security forces and settlers gather outside the besieged Palestinian houses in the village of Qusra, in the occupied West Bank on August 17, 2026. Photo by Jaafar ASHTIYEH / AFP via Getty Images.

## “The New Reality”
Palestinians in the occupied West Bank have been coming under a steadily escalating assault for the past three years. Israeli settler attacks backed by Israeli soldiers and the state have fully or partially displaced 107 communities since January 2023, alongside unprecedented settlement expansion, according to a new report by Human Rights Watch. The Israeli military expelled another 32,000 Palestinians from their homes in the Jenin, Tulkarem, and Nur Shams camps in January 2025.
The besieged families in Qusra have been under assault since January, when settlers first took over a nearby building that was under-construction and began launching daily attacks on the residents.
Their homes lie in Area B of the occupied West Bank. While settler attacks and the forcible transfer of Palestinians in recent years have largely targeted villages and Bedouin communities in Area C—which comprises roughly 60% of the West Bank and includes almost all the agricultural land—Israeli settler violence and theft of land is now increasingly spreading into Palestinian communities located in Area B.
Last month, a Palestinian family of eight living in the nearby village of Jalud, were forced from their home after a similar 10-day settler and soldier siege. The concentrated attack began three months prior, when settlers erected a colonial outpost near the Al-Tubassi family and began targeting them on a daily basis.
“During the final month, the settlers occupied a house under construction on the road to the Al-Tubassi family home, and in the last 10 days they cut off the water, electricity and no one could reach them any more,” Bashar Qaryouti, a medic and activist in the area, told Drop Site. “In the last four days the family had no food, nothing left, and on the final day they were held at gunpoint by the settlers and forced to leave.”
In a statement last week, the UN Human Rights Office condemned the attacks on Qusra. “These criminal actions by the settlers, supported or acquiesced to by Israel, the Occupying Power, are making life unbearable for these Palestinian families, and are clearly aimed at forcing them to leave their homes and land. Time is running out for these three families before they are forcibly displaced,” the UN Human Rights Office said. “The International Court of Justice is clear that all Israeli settlements are illegal and that Israel is obligated to cease all settlement activities, evacuate all settlers, including those terrorizing Qusra and Jalud, and bring to an end its unlawful presence in the West Bank.”
Analysts also warn that the recurrence of the siege tactic in Qusra is ominous and points to a wider pattern unfolding across the occupied West Bank.
“It began with Bedouin Palestinians in the remote areas, then it moved to the small villages at the edges of the governorates, and now they are in large villages, with the active participation of the military, which also supplies the weapons and trains them,” Ramallah-based political analyst Nihad Abu Ghosh told Drop Site.
In addition to the tens of thousands of Palestinians forcibly displaced over the past three years in the West Bank, over 1,000 Palestinians have also been killed, nearly a quarter of them children.
“These are fascist, Jewish-Zionist militias who are carrying out pogroms and killings in the occupied West Bank,” continued Abu Ghosh. “Both the government and the settlers are in a race against time. They consider the few remaining months or days of this government’s tenure to be an exceptional opportunity to change the reality on the ground. That is why they are intensifying their attacks until they reach a point where, in their assessment, it will be difficult to reverse what they have done.”
Conditions for Palestinians in the occupied West Bank deteriorated even further last month after a large-scale settler attack on the village of Tel, southwest of Nablus city, on July 24, during which four Palestinians and two Israeli settlers were killed.
Since the incident in Tel, settlers and soldiers have carried out daily, round-the-clock attacks, including mass shootings, physical assaults, arson, and land theft. Settlers have also erected at least 15 new colonial outposts on Palestinian land across the West Bank, with the vocal backing of top Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who announced a series of steps that included “accelerating the legalization of farm outposts and establishment of new ones.”
Back in Qusra, residents are terrified.
“I keep thinking about what happened to the Al-Tubassi family and praying that we can outlast this,” said Ruqayya.
Wadi, the Qusra mayor, is equally concerned. “We fear that this siege will become the new reality in the occupied West Bank, that Qusra will be another precedent for all the villages,” Wadi said. He also recounted that his older brother and nephew were murdered by armed settlers on October 12, 2023, during a funeral for four other Palestinians killed in the village also by settlers the prior day.
Some warn that the unrelenting settler-colonial violence may be reaching a tipping point. “The distance between the Palestinian people in the West Bank and massacres, is a question of when—not if,” said Abu Ghosh. “When the knife reaches the throats of Palestinians, they will have no choice but to resist with whatever means are available to them.”

reads.title: U.S. national debt tops $40 trillion; Russian strikes kill 16 in Ukraine; Ecuador’s intelligence chief killed in Kenya helicopter crash
reads.subtitle: Drop Site Daily: August 20, 2026
reads.body:
- People walk past damaged cars amid debris in a residential area hit by Russian strikes on August 20, 2026 in Kyiv, Ukraine. Photo by Ihor Kuznietsov/Global Images Ukraine via Getty Images.Thursday, August 20, 2026 – Fifty Bodies recovered in Gaza City. Report: 94% of households in Gaza need shelter aid. Human Rights Watch: Israeli settler violence has displaced 107 West Bank communities since 2023. Israel opens bidding for 1,234 units within settlement project, cutting northern West Bank from south. Israeli settlers injure nine Palestinians as attacks continue across occupied West Bank. World Central Kitchen condemns Israeli decision to close probe into killing of its workers in Gaza. President Donald Trump calls for “economic D-Day against Iran”; Iran calls it diversion from U.S. debt crisis. U.S. officials make dubious claims about Hormuz traffic. Iraq asks Iran for eased oil exporting rules. Ansarallah claims “comprehensive blockade” of Saudi tankers. Israel continues ceasefire violations with shelling and demolitions across southern Lebanon. Lebanese Parliament speaker “guarantees” U.S. that Lebanese Army can assert control over south if Israel withdraws. UNIFIL hands over Khardali-Litani position to Lebanese army ahead of mission’s end. U.S. national debt tops $40 trillion for first time. Trump pushes crypto industry's Clarity Act with ethics concerns looming. Los Angeles prosecutor reduces felony charges against officer who recorded colleagues’ bigoted remarks. Democratic-aligned “VoteVets” official also runs credit card industry lobbying front group. Florida Democratic Senate nominee Angie Nixon calls Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu a “war criminal.” Syrian FM says Israel had “no justification” for bombing air base earlier this week. Ecuador's intelligence chief and five Americans killed in Kenya helicopter crash. Sudan’s Rapid Support Forces see additional defections, Sudanese army claims. Russian missile strikes kill 16 amid Ukrainian interceptor shortage. Poland arrests Ukrainian man over alleged Russia-linked assassination plot. North Korea tests short-range ballistic missiles after U.S.-South Korea drills are scaled back.
This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday – Friday

## Palestine

- Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, 10 Palestinians were killed and 25 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.

- The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,417 killed, with 174,360 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,283 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,248, while 813 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble.

- Fifty Bodies recovered in Gaza City: Gaza Civil Defense crews recovered 50 bodies from beneath the rubble of the Al-Sawafiri, Al-Batniji, Karam, Harz, and Al-Af family homes in Gaza City after three days of work, the Palestine Information Center reported on Thursday.

- The Civil Defense agency said its teams have inspected eight completely destroyed homes where around 170 Palestinians are believed to remain buried, as recovery efforts continue while Israel obstructs the entry of equipment into the strip.

- Report: 94% of households in Gaza need shelter aid: An estimated 1.98 million Palestinians in Gaza, or 94% of the population, need shelter and basic household assistance, according to a new report by the Shelter Cluster, led by the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC).

- The report found that nearly two-thirds of households live in tents or makeshift shelters, structures that are not designed for long-term accommodation. More than half of households in tents had already used the same tent for over a year, while more than half of tents and makeshift shelters assessed were in poor or very poor condition.

- “A shelter is not adequate simply because it has four walls or a roof,” Jehan Salim, National Shelter Cluster Coordinator, said in a statement. “Ten months after the October 2025 ceasefire, most families have lived more than a year in shelters that were never designed for long-term accommodation. The materials needed to repair homes, restore basic services and provide improved shelters are still not entering Gaza at anything close to the scale required.”

- HRW: Israeli settler violence has displaced 107 West Bank communities since 2023: Israeli settler attacks have fully or partially displaced 107 Palestinian communities, comprising some 5,900 people, across the occupied West Bank since January 2023, Human Rights Watch (HRW) said in a new report. The Israeli military expelled another 32,000 Palestinians from their homes in the Jenin, Tulkarem, and Nur Shams camps in January 2025. HRW said Israeli authorities are “arming, funding, and granting impunity” to settlers responsible for the attacks, which increasingly target Palestinians’ homes, land, livestock and access to water. The group cited OCHA figures showing an average of 6.6 settler attacks resulting in casualties or property damage per day in 2026—the highest rate it has recorded—and said at least 15 Palestinians, including two children, had been killed by settlers as of July 24.

- “The Israeli government and the settlers share the same goal of maximum land and minimum Palestinians,” HRW said.

- Israel opens bidding for 1,234 units within settlement project cutting northern West Bank from south: Israel issued a tender for the construction of 1,234 housing units in the E1 area east of Jerusalem, advancing a settlement project that would disrupt Palestinian territorial contiguity between Ramallah, East Jerusalem and Bethlehem, The Times of Israel reported. The units are part of roughly 3,400 homes approved last August, when Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said the project would “practically erase the two-state delusion.”

- The UN Secretary-General expressed “deep alarm” over the move, with his spokesperson warning that E1 would effectively “sever the connection between the northern and southern West Bank” and pose an “existential threat” to a two-state solution.

- The UK issued an unusually sharp response, summoning Israel’s chargé d’affaires and demanding the government immediately retract the tender and halt settlement expansion. Britain called the move “unacceptable and destructive” and said it “will not stand back and accept the destruction of the Two-State Solution.” The government also said it would announce a “comprehensive set of measures” in the coming weeks, including sanctions targeting those involved in illegal settlement expansion.

- Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar rejected the UK’s condemnation, claiming Jewish people have a right to live “throughout the Land of Israel,” and invoked the Balfour Declaration—a 1917 British imperial declaration backing the establishment of a Jewish national home in historic Palestine—to defend settlement in the occupied territory.

- Israeli settlers injure nine Palestinians as attacks continue across occupied West Bank:

- Ramallah: Five Palestinians were injured Thursday in a settler attack on a vehicle between Al-Mughayyir and Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah, WAFA reported. Settlers attacked the vehicle, causing it to overturn, before assaulting those inside. Israeli authorities returned the body of a 17-year-old Palestinian boy, from Sinjil, after withholding it since he was killed by Israeli forces on March 17.

- Tubas: A Palestinian man was injured after settlers attacked him while he was working in the Al-Buqaia plain in the northern Jordan Valley.

- Hebron: Israeli forces transported several mobile homes to the newly established “Doron” settlement outpost on Mount Tarousa, west of Hebron. Israeli forces began excavation and land-clearing work there in June after armed settlers, under army protection, erected a tent and declared the establishment of the new settlement. Doron is among 19 new settlements approved by the Israeli government last year.

- Nablus: Settlers continued for a 12th consecutive day to besiege several homes in Qusra, south of Nablus, under Israeli army protection. Israeli forces raided Nablus city, Salem, Bazariya, Madama and Einabus, assaulting three Palestinians and detaining 10 others.

- World Central Kitchen condemns Israeli decision to close probe into killing of its workers in Gaza: World Central Kitchen (WCK) condemned the Israeli military’s decision to close investigations into the April 2024 strikes that killed seven of its workers. The army said Wednesday it reviewed 150 incidents of troop conduct in Gaza and only made decisions on five cases. It also closed investigations into two separate incidents that killed four Doctors Without Borders (MSF) employees in 2023 and 2024. At least 550 aid workers have been killed by Israel in Gaza since October 2023, almost all of them Palestinians.

- WCK said there was “never any excuse or justification” for the successive Israeli strikes on its clearly marked vehicles and accused the military investigation of muddying the events and shifting blame for the Israeli military’s conduct. The organization renewed its demand for an independent investigation, saying the Israeli military “cannot credibly investigate its own conduct.”

- Australia also condemned the decision, saying it was “outraged” that Israel would not pursue criminal proceedings over the killing of Australian WCK worker Zomi Frankcom and her six colleagues, with Foreign Minister Penny Wong announcing that Israel’s ambassador would be called in.

- Israeli human rights group B’Tselem called Israel’s rare internal investigations a “sham” that amount to a “a legal Iron Dome to protect Israeli soldiers from potential international legal consequences.”

- Netanyahu’s rival threatens strikes on Iran as candidates compete over who would wage more war: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett said Wednesday that, if he led the Israeli government, he would strike Iran in response to any attack by Hezbollah, claiming he would overhaul Israel’s security doctrine in the role.

- Bennett, one of Benjamin Netanyahu’s main political rivals ahead of Israel’s October election, served as prime minister from 2021 to 2022.

## Iran

- Trump calls for “economic D-Day against Iran”; Iran calls it diversion from U.S. debt crisis: President Donald Trump claimed he was about to undertake what he called “the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country” against Iran on Wednesday, vowing “economic warfare and isolation on an unprecedented scale,” in a post on his Truth Social platform.

- Trump threatened that “any country that allows its financial institutions, businesses, airports, or government entities to provide any type of lifeline to Iran will itself face tremendous economic consequences.” He cited as examples of support “oil smuggling, swap lines, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries, [and] front companies.”

- The warning indicates that Trump will impose additional sanctions on states and firms that keep trading with Tehran. As of Wednesday, no specific measures had been published by the Treasury Department, whose last Iran sanctions were announced on August 7.

- Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed Trump’s campaign against Iran as a diversion from America’s own crisis of “unprecedented debt” and surging interest costs. “Doubling down on failed policies will only bring further defeat—and enmity of Iranians,” Araghchi wrote in a post on X Thursday, sharing CNN and New York Times reports on the U.S. national debt surpassing a record $40 trillion and rising borrowing costs, adding that U.S. “economic terrorism threatens global economy and sovereignty worldwide.”

- U.S. officials make dubious claims about Hormuz traffic: Two U.S. officials told Axios on Wednesday that the U.S. military has been running a corridor through the Strait of Hormuz for weeks, moving about 10 million barrels of oil a day, roughly half pre-war volume, out of the Gulf via a southern channel off Oman.

- President Trump has said that “a tremendous amount of oil” is now leaving the strait and that the U.S. is not negotiating with Iran.

- Several energy analysts have questioned the 10 million figure, with Gregory Brew of Eurasia Group saying available data doesn’t corroborate it, and estimating flows at “at least 5-6 million bpd.” Rory Johnston suggested flows nearer to 5 million bpd, calling the 10 million figure a “stretch.”

- Iraq asks Iran for eased oil exporting rules: Iraq has asked Iran to grant its oil exports “special consideration” through the Strait of Hormuz, as disruptions to Gulf shipping continue to constrain Iraqi crude, Al-Monitor and the Iraqi News Agency reported on Wednesday.

- Iraqi Parliament Speaker Haibat Al-Halbousi made the request in talks with his Iranian counterpart Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf in Baghdad on Wednesday, saying Iraq was among the countries most affected by the regional crisis.

- Ghalibaf, who said Tuesday the strait would stay closed until the U.S. lifts its blockade, was in Iraq as part of a three-day visit to the country.

## Yemen

- Ansarallah claims “comprehensive blockade” of Saudi tankers: A spokesperson for Yemen’s Ansarallah claimed on Wednesday that the group had imposed a “comprehensive blockade” on Saudi ships, as part of its “siege for siege policy, ” arguing that its military strength had allowed it to more effectively deter Saudi attacks.

- The spokesman said the group had targeted eight Saudi oil tankers since its blockade began, five in the Red Sea and three in the Gulf of Aden and Arabian Sea, and turned back 48 others.

- In response to Saudi strikes on Sanaa airport and Hodeidah port, and airspace violations over Saada and Hajjah, the spokesman said the group carried out nine operations against Yanbu, Najran, Jizan, Abha, and Eastern Province oil facilities, and 14 more targeting Saudi forces at sites including Marib and al-Makha.

## Lebanon

- Israel continues ceasefire violations with shelling and demolitions across southern Lebanon: Israel continued its attacks across southern Lebanon on Thursday, carrying out a large explosion near Zawtar Al-Sharqieh in Nabatieh governorate, while renewed Israeli shelling struck Houla and the area between Talloussa and Markaba, also in Nabatieh governorate, according to Lebanon’s National News Agency (NNA).

- Heavy Israeli artillery fire targeted Wadi Al-Salouqi, Wadi Al-Hujeir and valleys around Qabrikha and Touline, spanning Nabatieh and Bint Jbeil districts. In Tyre (Sour) governorate, Israeli forces carried out an explosion in the town of Mansouri.

- On Wednesday, Israeli forces carried out a wave of attacks and demolitions, striking Mansouri from the air, shelling Srebbine and blowing up homes in Zawtar Sharqieh, Tallouseh, Bani Hayyan, Houla and Khiam. In Mansouri, Israeli forces demolished and burned homes before renewed airstrikes later in the day.

- Parliament speaker “guarantees” U.S. that Lebanese Army can assert control over south if Israel withdraws: Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri said on Wednesday that the situation in southern Lebanon has become “unbearable” and is comparable to Gaza in the scale of Israel’s destruction, killings, and attacks on homes and heritage, L’Orient Today reported.

- Speaking to a delegation from the American Task Force on Lebanon (ATFL), Berri said the U.S. and President Trump were uniquely positioned to force Israel to end the war and withdraw to the international border.

- If Israel withdraws, Berri, Hezbollah’s chief political ally, said he would “guarantee the immediate deployment of the Lebanese Army” throughout the area south of the Litani River, with the army becoming the sole armed force responsible for security there.

- Separately on Wednesday, French President Emmanuel Macron invited the Lebanese government to a September 17 preparatory meeting in Paris ahead of an international conference aimed at supporting the Lebanese Army and Internal Security Forces. The conference, originally expected in March, was postponed following the outbreak of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran and Israel’s escalation of its war on Lebanon.

- UNIFIL hands over Khardali-Litani position to Lebanese army ahead of mission’s end: The United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL), the UN peacekeeping mission deployed in southern Lebanon since 1978, handed over its position near the Lebanese army post in the Khardali-Litani area to the army’s 7th Brigade, NNA reported. The transfer is part of a plan to hand a number of UNIFIL positions to the Lebanese army ahead of the mission’s scheduled termination at the end of this year.

## U.S. News

- U.S. national debt tops $40 trillion for first time: America’s gross national debt surpassed a record $40 trillion Wednesday, with the country on track to borrow more than $2 trillion this year alone amid spending on the Iran war and 2025 tax cuts. Rising interest payments now account for about half the country’s annual borrowing.

- Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who set a goal of cutting the deficit to 3% of GDP by 2028, acknowledged that the deficit is moving in the wrong direction this year.

- His department unexpectedly announced on Wednesday that it would “at least double” its long-dated debt buybacks, from $2 billion to at least $4 billion per operation, after yields on long-term government bonds surged to their highest levels in nearly two decades.

- The move, targeting 10- to 30-year debt, sent the 30-year yield down nearly 10 basis points and pushed the dollar sharply lower.

- Trump pushes crypto industry’s Clarity Act with ethics concerns looming: President Donald Trump called on Congress to pass the Clarity Act, a bill establishing federal regulatory rules for digital assets, at a White House event Wednesday attended by executives from Coinbase, Ripple, and other crypto companies.

- The bill would split crypto regulatory authority between the SEC and CFTC, impose anti-money-laundering rules, and ban senior officials, including the president, from creating digital assets while in office.

- Trump held this meeting and advocated for this legislation amid concerns about his personal ties to the industry, having taken in more than $1.4 billion from cryptocurrency-related ventures in 2025. The Trump family’s crypto business has expanded under his second term as well, with Trump’s World Liberty Financial company and personal meme coins having netted the family hundreds of millions of dollars each.

- LA prosecutor reduces felony charges against officer who recorded colleagues’ bigoted remarks: Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman said Wednesday he would reduce felony charges against LAPD officer Daniel Flores, who secretly recorded 16 colleagues making racist, sexist, and homophobic remarks, to misdemeanor charges.

- Hochman, who was heavily criticized for his charging decision, maintained the recordings themselves violated California’s two-party consent eavesdropping law, though he called the comments themselves “abhorrent.”

- Flores, who taped co-workers 122 times over about a year before filing a complaint with the police commission in January 2025, will now be eligible for judicial diversion that could leave him with no criminal record if he avoids breaking the law for a year.

- Democratic-aligned “VoteVets” official also runs credit card industry lobbying front group: Peter Kauffmann, vice chair of the Democratic-aligned veterans group VoteVets and treasurer of its philanthropic arm, also serves as chief spokesperson for the Small Business Payments Alliance, a group funded by the credit card industry that fights to protect swipe fees charged by Visa and Mastercard, according to new reporting from The American Prospect.

- The Small Business Payments Alliance, a project of the credit-card-industry-funded Electronic Payment Coalition, has spent millions lobbying against the Credit Card Competition Act, and a report from Demand Progress found many of its member businesses have received funding directly from Mastercard, JPMorgan Chase, and Capital One.

- VoteVets’s political action committee has separately raised more than $20 million this year from billionaire donors to intervene in Democratic primaries favoring moderate, veteran-affiliated candidates over progressives, including $10 million spent boosting Iowa state Rep. Josh Turek over progressive Zach Wahls. Read the full report here.

- Florida Democratic Senate nominee Nixon calls Netanyahu a “war criminal”: Angie Nixon, who won Tuesday’s Democratic Senate primary in Florida, called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a “war criminal”  during on “Morning Joe” on Wednesday, saying he “needs to answer for his [crimes]” and that she opposes “sending any money or weapons to Israel at this moment.”

- “Right now, here in our state, in our country, we have veterans that are living unhoused on the streets,” Nixon said. “We have teachers that are calling my state office monthly because they can’t afford to live in the state of Florida anymore.”

- Analysis of Nixon’s victory published by the Washington Post on Wednesday found that she depended on a new coalition, performing strongest in counties that were younger, poorer, less college-educated and had larger Black populations. Nixon won the least college-educated and Blackest counties by roughly 30 points, carried counties with median household incomes below $65,000 by 20 points, and dominated areas with the largest shares of young adults.
📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill?  Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com

## Other International News

- Ecuador’s intelligence chief and five Americans killed in Kenya helicopter crash: The director general of Ecuador’s intelligence agency (CIES), Michele Sensi-Contugi, was among seven dead as a result of a helicopter crash in central Kenya, officials said on Wednesday.

- The U.S. State Department confirmed five Americans were among the dead, including a Telemundo executive and a Miami restauranteur.

- The aircraft, carrying guests from the luxury tour operator &Beyond, crashed in the foothills of Mount Ololokwe in Samburu County. The cause of the crash remains under investigation.

- Sensi-Contugi, 42, appointed to lead Ecuador’s National Intelligence Center in 2024, was a close associate of right-wing President Daniel Noboa, a key U.S. partner in Washington’s militarized anti-cartel push.

- He and the CIES “served as architects of the political lawfare, police state, and brutal crackdown against journalists, indigenous members of the 2025 General Strike… and leftwing figures,” Drop Site contributor Camila Lourdes Galarza writes.

- Russian missile strikes kill 16 amid Ukrainian interceptor shortage: Russia launched a large-scale missile attack on Kyiv and the surrounding region, firing dozens of cruise, ballistic and hypersonic missiles alongside 168 drones, killing at least 16 people and wounding more than 40. Ukrainian officials said 30 residential buildings, a school, children’s hospital, and kindergarten were damaged, while some 90,000 households temporarily lost power.

- Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine’s dwindling stock of Patriot interceptors had not been replenished and accused allies of responding inadequately.

- A separate wave of attacks also struck infrastructure in Odessa, where repeated Russian attacks on ports and shipping have sharply disrupted Ukrainian agricultural exports.

- Poland arrests Ukrainian man over alleged Russia-linked assassination plot: Polish authorities arrested a Ukrainian man accused of trying to assassinate a representative of Ukraine’s arms industry in Irpin, near Kyiv, on behalf of Russian intelligence. Investigators said the suspect planted an improvised explosive device beneath the target’s car that was meant to be detonated remotely by cell phone but failed because of a malfunction.

- The suspect fled to Poland after the failed attack and was arrested in Warsaw, where he faces charges including attempted murder with explosives and could receive life imprisonment.

- RSF sees additional defections, army claims: Sudan’s army said 315 fighters from the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces defected on Wednesday, led by Brig. Gen. Musa Khamiseen, as they crossed from North Darfur into Northern State before traveling under military intelligence escort to Omdurman, according to Sudan Tribune.

- Khamiseen’s reception by the army has drawn criticism from some of its Darfuri allies, who accuse him of involvement in summary executions and civilian killings during the RSF siege and capture of El Fasher last year.

- One fighter who was present during the siege accused Khamiseen of participating in killings near the earthen barricade erected to prevent civilians from fleeing and said he was filmed alongside Al-Fateh Abu Lulu, an RSF commander notorious for recording himself carrying out summary executions.

- North Korea tests short-range ballistic missiles after U.S.-South Korea drills are scaled back: North Korea launched roughly 10 short-range ballistic missiles from the Pyongyang area toward its eastern waters, prompting South Korea’s national security council to hold an emergency meeting and call on Pyongyang to stop launches they say are prohibited by U.N. Security Council resolutions.

- The test came a day after the U.S. and South Korea announced they were reducing the size of the 11-day Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises after President Donald Trump ordered the Pentagon to “substantially reduce” the drills in an apparent attempt to revive diplomacy with Kim Jong Un.

- Syrian FM says Israel had “no justification” for bombing air base earlier this week: Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani told Axios on Wednesday that Israel had no justification for bombing the Abu al-Duhur airbase, saying Damascus had explicitly informed Israel that no Turkish base or permanent Turkish troop deployment was planned there.

- Israel dropped at least eight bombs on the site on Tuesday, damaging newly rebuilt runways and hangars.

- Al-Shaibani said the base was largely empty and being rehabilitated for Syria’s air force, though Turkish officers had previously visited the site as part of broader military cooperation between the countries.

- Drop Site dispatch from Cuba: Amid a total oil blockade imposed by the U.S.—resulting in nationwide blackouts, medicine shortages, and disruptions to hospital operations—Cuba is transitioning away from fossil fuels toward renewable energy. Over 2,500 photovoltaic parks have been inaugurated across the country, a 96% increase over those built this time last year. Drop Site contributor Sasi Alejandre reports from Cuba, breaking down the country’s push toward an energy revolution; watch the video here.

reads.title: Options Basics for Beginners: Long Calls and Long Puts
reads.subtitle: What Options Are, and How They Work
reads.body:
Options are a bit more complicated and can seem daunting compared to “Ye Olde Buy Shares and Holde™”, but the goal of this article is to showcase the power that options can have with active investing.
While they are a bit tricky to understand, the basic functions are quite similar to how shares work, except there’s a few other variables at play.
An options contract represents 100 shares of stock, no matter what price the contract is. The upside to options is that you can control a theoretical 100 shares of stock for much cheaper, with a very high exponential profit zone. The downside is that you have a fairly high probability of the investment going to 0.
The distinction between these contracts is represented with two forms: Calls and Puts.
Of these two forms, they are broken into long calls and short calls, along with long puts and short puts. There are two different styles of options, American and European, with the only distinction being that you can only exercise (buy or sell the shares) European options on the expiration date, whereas you can exercise American style options whenever. Most companies and ETFs on the U.S. exchanges utilize American style options, save for a few.
For this article, we’re going to focus on American style options primarily.
Before we get into it further, we’ll take a look at the makeup of an option contract as it appears on the Unusual Whales Flow page, and how it would read in most places you see it.
A quick breakdown of a long call in the flow.
This position would read: VET 17.5C 12/18/2026.
Let’s break this position down to explain each part:
The first part, VET, is the stock “ticker”, an identifying abbreviation, for the company Vermillion Energy. This just tells you what company or stock the contract is for. (For example, the “ticker” for the S&P 500 ETF Trust is SPY).
The second part, 17.5C, actually has two pieces of information. The 17.5 refers to the “strike”, or the price the stock price must reach for this contract to be “in the money”.
The C indicates that this contract is a “Call”. We’ll get into how calls can be traded “long” and “short”, and what those terms mean, a little later.
The last part of this contract, 12/18/2026, is the expiration date of the contract. This is exactly what it sounds like; the last date this contract can be transacted or exist.
At the expiration date of a contract (in this case, December 18th, 2026), there are 3 potential circumstances that can happen for a call contract.

- The contract expires in the money, which means the underlying share price’s value is greater than the strike price, or VET > $17.50. This gives you the option to exercise the contract and purchase 100 shares of Vermillion Energy at $17.5 a share. We’ll talk more on exercising later.

- You can also sell the contract beforehand, and collect money from the sale. Depending on certain circumstances, which we will get to later, this may either be a gain or a loss. This option is the most common for retail traders like us.

- VET shares might be less than $17.50, which means the contract expires worthless, and is then worth $0. Why does it expire worthless? It simply does not make sense to purchase the shares for more than they are worth. If the stock is not $17.50 or higher, this contract would expire worthless on the expiration date.
Now let’s break down the basic of basics by taking a look at Long Calls and Long Puts outright.

## Long Calls
Long calls, also known as calls bought to open, are the most similar to buying stock in a company. When the stock goes up, your call should go up in value, too. Long calls have a theoretical infinite upside, so the higher the stock price rises, the more profit can be made on Long calls. That’s what the VET example above outlines.

Below is a Profit and Loss diagram (PnL) for a long call bought at strike A.

-
- A long call gives the investor the right, but not the obligation, to buy 100 shares/units of the underlying stock/asset at a fixed price, on or before the expiration date of the contract.
What this technical phrase means is that you can exercise the option to purchase 100 shares at any time, even on the expiration date, but you do not have to.

## Long Puts
Long puts (puts bought to open) are most similar to shorting stock in a company. When the stock goes down, your put theoretically should go up in value. Long puts have a limited theoretical max gain, as the underlying stock cannot go below $0 per share. However, long puts have the same loss potential of long calls, which is the total value of your initial investment.
Below is a PnL Diagram for a long put purchased at strike A.

-
- A long put gives the investor the right, but not the obligation, to sell 100 shares/units of the underlying stock/asset at a fixed price, on or before the expiration date of the contract.
Much like long calls, you also have the option to sell 100 shares at any time, including the expiration date, but you do not have to.
A quick breakdown of a long put in the flow.
This position would read: CCL 24P 09/04/2026.
Let’s break this position down just as we did the Long Call example above, with a little more context.
Just like the Long Call example, the 24P refers to the “strike” (in this case, $24 for CCL). We can see under the “Bid-Ask” column that the lowest price someone is willing to sell the contract for (the “Ask”) is $0.22, and the highest amount someone is willing to pay for a contract (the “Bid”) is $0.19. Under the “Spot” column (or, the price at which the contract transacted), we see this order of 1,000 contracts for CCL 24P 09/04/2026 transacted at the Ask price of $0.22.
This indicates a higher likelihood that the contracts were Bought (but not, I repeat: not a guarantee they were bought). Another important point to note is that the Size of that order (1,000 contracts) is greater than the Open Interest of the contract (113 contracts) combined with the total volume that same day (9 contracts). This confirms that this position is a newly opened position, because it’s not possible to “close” contracts that don’t exist, and the size of that order is much larger than any existing positions in the contract.
What are the uses?
Both of these descriptions look quite similar, and they are. One makes money when a stock goes up (long call), and the other makes money when a stock goes down (long put).
“But what is a fixed price?”
The fixed price in those descriptions is known as the strike price from earlier
“So how are these prices determined?”
American style options are typically priced by something called a binomial tree, while European options are priced with a model known as Black-Scholes-Merton. These prices are represented per share of the contract, so an options contract that is valued at $1.00 on your brokerage platform is one dollar per share x 100, for the 100 shares the contract controls for a total value of $100. This price is known as the premium.
An example:
For the sake of simplicity, let’s say you have “Generic Manufacturing Corp (GMFC)”, and it’s trading at $100 a share. You see some options flow hit the tape, and you believe that there will be an increased industry demand for GMFC’s main product in the next 3 months. You, as an investor, decide to buy a long call with the strike of $105 for $500 in premium ($5.00 per share x 100 shares) with an expiration in 6 months.
After 3 months, let’s say GMFC is trading at $120, and you are still holding the $105 call. The value of your contract has gone from $5.00 per share to $15.00 per share, for a total of ($15.00-5.00) = $10 x 100 = $1000 in profit.
You’ve made a profit, but you ask yourself “how does this work?”
The value of your long call has theoretically increased by $1000, and you’re presented with a few different options.

- Sell the long call for a total profit of $1000.

- Exercise the long call, and buy 100 shares of GMFC for 105 a share.

- Continue to hold the long call in hopes the stock continues to go up.
Let’s go over each of these scenarios.

## Option A
You decide to take your profits, and sell the option for $1500. You receive $1000 in profit from this, since you initially paid $500 for the long call 3 months prior. You are no longer invested in $GMFC, and you can use the money to buy yourself a pizza

## Option B
Let’s say you have 3 months remaining on the contract, and $GMFC is trading at $110 per share. Your contract would be worth $1000, or $10.00 per share.
If you choose Option B, you can exercise the contract. This means you can act out the right to buy the 100 shares the contract represents, at $105 per share. The value of such an ordeal would be $10500 that you would pay to obtain the shares. That same amount in shares is worth $11000 if you were to sell, but there’s a catch with it.
The total profit from the option, should you choose to exercise, is calculated as follows:
(Share price x 100) - (Strike price x 100) - (price paid for the contract)
In this case, it would be:
$11000 - $10500 - $500 = 0.
So should you choose to exercise, your total profit would be $0.
If $GMFC is trading at $140 a share, your profit would be:
$14000 - $10500 - $500 = $3000.

## Option C
If you choose option C, you would do nothing different. You would continue to hold your long call in the hope manufacturing demand continues to increase, and your contract’s premium continues to gain in value.
In two more months, you would have a month remaining on the contract.
If GMFC is trading at $140 per share, your long call would now be worth $35 per share, or $3500 for the contract. This gives you a profit on the trade of $3000 should you choose to then pursue Option A, and sell the contract. If you notice, this is equivalent to how much you could exercise the option for and then sell the shares.
GMFC could also go down, based on bad news, a poor earnings report, the manufacturing demand decreasing, or a market-wide drawdown. Say you didn’t pursue Option A, and now $GMFC is trading at $110 per share. The value of your contract would then be back at $5.00 per share, or $500.
“But how did the stock go up and I haven’t made money on the position?”
This is due to an effect known as time decay, or time value (often represented by the Greek “Theta”). Time value is represented by how much excess money an investor is willing to pay in hopes that $GMFC’s share price, and in turn, the option’s value, increases before the contract expires in 1 month.
Regardless, you’re back to break even, your options contract is worth $500 after 5 months, and you can look at the options discussed above again and reposition for your next decision.
This is more or less how an options trade unfolds. There are a lot of risks surrounding options, but that doesn’t necessarily mean that they’re scary and should be avoided.
In a future article, we’ll talk more about the risks, along with short calls, short puts, and some other terminology. Trading is all about managing risk, and options are very much a mechanism for doing that.
