-
- Crime scene of prosecutor Alexandra Bravo’s and her sister, Olinda Bravo’s assassination. Photo provided to Drop Site News by Radio Pichincha.Para leer esta historia en español, haga clic aquí.
QUITO, Ecuador—Alexandra Bravo, the prosecutor assigned to investigate U.S. strikes on three Ecuadorian boats and the 36 survivors’ subsequent accounts of torture and kidnapping, was shot dead in the coastal city of Manta last month. According to police, on June 14 a hitman aboard a black motorcycle opened fire on Bravo as she and her sister were leaving a café at about 11 a.m.  Bravo’s sister, who jumped to protect her, was also killed in the attack.
Upon arriving at the crime scene, officers say they found five 9mm shell casings and Bravo’s injured driver, but no sign of the police detail that had been assigned to protect her. The Police Directorate, which operates entirely under the executive branch, has launched a probe to determine if there’d been an internal security breach.
Bravo is the 26th member of Ecuador’s justice system to be assassinated since 2020 and the second individual investigating state crimes murdered that week. Besides her usual caseload of homicide and organized crime, Bravo had been working the Fiorella, Negra Francisca, and Don Maca cases—a series of drone attacks on civilian fishing ships exposed by Drop Site in April. Two of the boat’s crews returned home and reported being abducted, blindfolded, and starved for eight days by American gunmen in U.S. military uniforms aboard a U.S.-flagged patrol ship, before being abandoned in El Salvador. The UN Committee on Enforced Disappearances endorsed the calls for an investigation, demanding that the U.S. provide information on the whereabouts of the eight still-missing men and any involvement in the matter by April 27. To date, the United States has not responded.
Under Ecuador’s right-wing president Daniel Noboa—a Miami-born billionaire often characterized as a “U.S.-backed dictator”—the country has become a central testing ground for Operation Southern Spear, Washington’s extrajudicial bombing campaign purporting to target “narco-terrorists,” which has killed 221 people to date. There is no evidence that many of the victims, including those in Bravo’s investigation, had engaged in drug trafficking.
“I can’t make any assertion regarding it being a political assassination, but evidently, when a prosecutor is killed it’s because of the investigation they’re conducting,” Fernando Bastias, a renowned human rights attorney with Ecuador’s CDH and member of the Geneva-based World Organization Against Torture, told Drop Site, “That’s something we’ve learned from our experience in Ecuador.”
A source inside the Manta police department, who knew Bravo personally, told Drop Site that the Ecuadorian prosecutor was under pressure from her superiors at the Attorney General’s office to treat the U.S. attacks as exclusively “cases of disappearance.” The source, who asked for anonymity out of fear of retaliation, said Bravo was told to close all lines of inquiry after 36 of the 44 missing men were found—despite arriving with severe injuries, including 70% vision loss and feet torn to flesh and bone, which medical experts found consistent with their accounts of explosions and torture.
A senior researcher with Human Rights Watch who interviewed Bravo as part of her investigation into the three vessels, similarly recalled Bravo facing “internal challenges within the institution itself to advance the investigation.” The researcher said the prosecutor repeatedly sought cooperation from other branches responsible for the ship’s rescue, including the Manta Port Captaincy, but “none responded to her requests for information.” During the Negra Francisca bombing, Darwin Pico-Flores, an eyewitness aboard a nearby boat, told Drop Site he called the Manta Port Captaincy to request emergency assistance. Nobody came. In April, as part of its first investigation into the incident, Drop Site called the port seeking comment. Officials hung up after learning the call was from journalists.
As of their last meeting on May 8, the researcher told Drop Site, Bravo “was still in the initial stages of inquiry and investigation.” Bastias said Bravo “was investigating a country [United States] that has been positioned in the media as an ally against crime. That investigation has not advanced at all, and that stems from an intention to avoid getting into trouble or problems with anyone.”
The source inside the Manta Police Department said that, given this lack of cooperation from partner agencies, Bravo had asked for advice on how to pursue new sources for evidence.
In the days leading up to her death, Bravo was relocated to the Attorney General’s office in Montecristi, a neighboring municipality. Her caseload changed after the transfer and she was no longer in charge of investigating the three boat attacks. Drop Site attempted to reach Bravo’s replacement for comment but he had been explicitly instructed not to speak to the press. After weeks of attempts to reach the Attorney General’s office for comment, they told Drop Site the investigation was sealed and they could not comment on why Bravo was relocated.
Inside Ecuador’s U.S.-backed military regime, the Attorney General’s office has become an increasingly opaque and politicized institution. “It’s already a major obstacle for prosecutors to investigate local state agents. Now imagine international state agents,” Bastias said. “The Executive Branch has implemented a series of legal frameworks that leave these foreign state agents immune from prosecution,” he added, referring to the diplomatic immunity granted to all U.S. military and Department of Defense personnel through President Noboa’s 22 martial law decrees.
The Pentagon, Coast Guard, and U.S. Southern Command have all denied any knowledge or responsibility of the boat incidents. After Drop Site published photo evidence of the Negra Francisca bombing, U.S. lawmakers questioned U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth during a congressional hearing. On June 13, the day before Bravo’s murder, Reps. Joaquin Castro (D-Texas) and Bill Keating (D-Mass.) published a letter to Hegseth, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Head of the U.S. Coast Guard, Kevin Lunday, demanding a full audit of U.S. government involvement in the attacks. Despite the deadline of July 10, none of the agencies have issued a public response. Keating’s press secretary Lauren McDermott told Drop Site that his office had received a reply from Rubio’s office, but none from the Department of War or Coast Guard. She did not disclose the contents of the response.
The survivors who returned home, and the families of those who didn’t, still have not received any answers, telling Drop Site “authorities shut the door in our face.” Maria, the wife of one of the fishermen, tells Drop Site her mother-in-law died awaiting her son’s return, saying she was struggling with severe depression and stopped in the weeks leading up to her death.
Despite both governments’ efforts to stonewall the investigation, evidence continues to emerge supporting the fishermen’s accounts of abduction, airstrikes, and torture. Drop Site obtained exclusive video of U.S. Coast Guard activity in the vicinity of the Negra Francisca bombing, open-source intelligence that corroborates the Negra Francisca’s testimonies, and police interviews with eyewitnesses that confirm the U.S. involvement alleged by survivors and documented by Drop Site. With the help of Airwars OSINT analyst and former U.S. Marine Corps member Tomi McCluskey, Drop Site accessed additional NASA thermal imagery consistent with the Negra Francisca bombing and vessel tracking data placing U.S. Coast Guard activity along the route the fishermen say they were taken after the strike.
Video obtained by Drop Site showing alleged Coast Guard activity near the Negra Francisca strike.

## Political Lawfare Under Ecuador’s U.S.-Backed Military Regime
Noboa, who governs by military curfews and mass starvation of political prisoners, has gone to great lengths to become Trump’s strongest partner in South America. Since taking office, he brushed aside Ecuador’s constitutional ban on U.S. military presence—ratified by 60% of voters as recently as November 2025—which was originally introduced almost 20 years ago precisely due to a history of U.S. military sinking boats off the coast of Manta. Additionally, his administration authorized the first FBI office on Ecuadorian soil, assisted a U.S. Embassy effort to falsely frame members of Colombia’s left-wing government ahead of elections, and collaborated with the U.S. in the bombing of innocent civilian farmworkers along the Colombian-Ecuadorian border—all in the name of combatting drug trafficking.
Notably, boats from Noboa’s family shipping corporation were caught trafficking ₤26 million of cocaine—a detail that has not deterred the State Department from naming him a key partner in Trump’s War on Drugs. Last month, The Guardian reported that a whistleblower who was investigating Noboa’s ties to drug trafficking was murdered.
Still, Noboa remains a member in good standing of Trump’s Shield of the Americas. The Americas Counter Cartel Coalition, as the Shield is also known, functions as both a military and a highly political alliance, having openly intervened to prop up U.S. interests in Bolivia as President Rodrigo Paz faced off with anti-austery protests.
A local prosecutor charging U.S. forces with extrajudicial bombings and torture of Ecuadorian civilians would undermine the alliance and damage Ecuador-U.S. relations.
Other government officials investigating U.S.-Ecuadorian criminal collusion received death threats. Mónica Palacios, a National Assembly lawmaker representing Ecuadorians living in the United States, who announced plans to bring the Fiorella boat case before the United Nations, faced months of political lawfare after exposing a U.S.-Ecuadorian government embezzlement scandal. Last Friday, Palacios said she received death threats against herself and her one-year-old son, along with footage of the outside of her New York home. She directly blamed President Noboa, saying the threats were retaliation for her investigation into U.S.-Ecuadorian corruption.
“There is a direct persecution of judges and prosecutors who, within the scope of their duties, make decisions that are not entirely aligned with what the Executive Branch wants and end up being sanctioned,” Bastias, the human rights attorney, said. “On the other hand, there is also the risk stemming from the context of criminality.” Regardless, he asserted, Bravo’s death “has a lot to do with what the state does or does not do, because so far there haven’t been any effective security mechanisms for the justice system’s civil servants. The responsibility lies in having failed to ensure protection.”

-
- Alexandra Bravo, prosecutor for Ecuador’s Attorney General’s Office, during an interview with Radio San Mateo. Photo provided to Drop Site News by Radio San Mateo.Diego Vintimilla Jarrín, formerly a lawmaker with Ecuador’s National Assembly and now a spokesperson for Ecuador’s Communist Party, similarly told Drop Site, “Noboa’s government is the most anti-sovereign agenda we have had since the start of democracy. I have no proof of who murdered the prosecutor but the fact that she was investigating certain elements and that they later ceased to seem important also says a lot about the underlying issues.”

## New Evidence Implicating U.S. Emerges

## The Negra Francisca
The U.S. maintains it never interacted with any of the three boats. A spokesperson for the U.S. Coast Guard told The Guardian that the agency’s only involvement in the events was deploying the USCGC Bertholf on a search-and-rescue mission after receiving a MAYDAY alert that the Negra Francisca was on fire, and ultimately found nothing.
But tracking data of the Bertholf’s movements, provided exclusively to Drop Site by McCluskey, places the cutter near the Negra Francisca around the time of the bombing before turning off its signal—only to reappear off the shore of Costa Rica the same dates the Negra Francisca crew were taken into Central American waters and transferred to El Salvador’s Naval Command, with mangled limbs and major burn injuries from the attack. Hernán Flores, captain of the Negra Francisca, told Drop Site that Salvadoran officers specifically informed him that “U.S. personnel had called to coordinate the handoff.”
The Coast Guard denied that it coordinated the handoff. “The Coast Guard did not play any role in the transfer of fishermen from the Negra Francisca Duarte II,” said a spokesperson.

-
- The USCGC Bertholf operating in Costa Rican waters on the same dates (times converted from UTC) that the Negra Francisca crew members were brought to Central America and received by El Salvador’s Navy/Coast Guard. Photo from Global Fishing Watch, provided by OSINT analyst Tomi McCluskey.The USCGC Bertholf departed the Galápagos military base at 4 p.m. on March 16 and stopped transmitting its location shortly afterwards. A day later, the Negra Francisca was bombed 170 miles away—a distance typically covered by boat in 3 to 10 hours. Drop Site asked the U.S. Coast Guard to account for the cutter’s activity after its signal went dark. The Coast Guard responded it “does not disclose cutter movements during law enforcement missions for operational security.”
At 1:02 p.m. on March 17, NASA FIRMS registered a thermal anomaly consistent with an explosive fire, corroborating the time and location where Negra Francisca fishermen told Drop Site their ship was set ablaze by multi-drone strikes. The crew say they were then seized at gunpoint by English-speaking men with blond hair dressed in khaki fatigues with American flag patches stitched onto their sleeves—their descriptions match the uniforms pictured in U.S. Southern Command press releases. Aboard the U.S.-flagged patrol ship, the gunmen allegedly held them hostage, sank their bombed boat, placed hoods over their heads, beat some of the fishermen, and withheld food for eight days as they transported them to Central America.

-
- OSINT provided to Drop Site by Tomi McCluskey document the USCGC Bertholf’s movements near the Negra Francisca around the time of the bombing (times converted from UTC).
-
- OSINT provided to Drop Site by Tomi McCluskey documenting the USCGC Bertholf’s movements near the Negra Francisca around the time of the bombing (times converted from UTC).The USCGC Bertholf’s signal resurfaced in Costa Rican waters on March 22 near the Golfito Port, approximately 450 nautical miles from El Salvador’s waters. It turned off its transponder and did not reactivate it until March 24, 24 hours after El Salvador’s Coast Guard publicly announced having had the Negra Francisca fishermen in their custody.
As part of our first investigation, Drop Site reached out to 11 government personnel in El Salvador. All of them refused to go on the record, citing a media gag order.
There is precedent for the Bertholf transferring victims of U.S. airstrikes to Central American authorities, with Costa Rican outlets reporting it delivered the remains of two deceased and one injured survivor to Costa Rica’s Port of Golfito around the same time. Costa Rica’s nautical inspector Wilber Urroz Guido said he had no information on the cutter’s movements but that it was authorized to act under a memorandum of understanding between the U.S. and Costa Rica—similar to agreements the U.S. maintains with Ecuador and El Salvador.
Eyewitness testimony also casts doubt on the U.S. Coast Guard’s version of events. Video footage shared exclusively with Drop Site by Darwin Flores-Pico, an eyewitness to the attack and nephew of the Negra Francisca’s captain, shows a U.S. Coast Guard cutter patrolling the waters where the bombing occurred.
Video obtained by Drop Site showing alleged Coast Guard activity near the Negra Francisca strike.
Darwin said he was fishing nearby on March 17, aboard his boat the Solavil, when he spotted smoke rising in the distance around 2 p.m. While making repeated attempts to reach the Negra Francisca’s crew by radio, he spotted an American aircraft circling above. It wasn’t until hours later that he learned by radio signal that the Negra Francisca was in flames and rushed to make his way to the scene, finding the vessel consumed by fire and no sign of survivors.
He recovered two scorched emergency skiffs, took photo evidence of the fire, then called the Port of Manta to ask for help. Nobody came.
Darwin decided to begin his journey back to the port to get emergency assistance and, as he was leaving the scene of the fire, red and green lights descended upon the Negra Francisca. Fearing for his safety, he steered his boat away from the site.

-
- The Negra Francisca burning, photographed and shared with Drop Site by Darwin Pico-Flores.The following afternoon, Darwin told Drop Site his boat was boarded by the U.S. Coast Guard, which detained and questioned the crew for nearly 12 hours via a Spanish translator with a Puerto Rican accent. He said Coast Guard personnel confirmed the red and green lights were from their patrol and acknowledged reaching the site of the Negra Francisca the previous night, but refused to elaborate on anything they’d found.
Instead, they questioned the fishermen about whether they’d seen anything and why Darwin had salvaged the skiffs. After telling the Coast Guard officials that the Negra Francisca was his uncle’s boat, Darwin says they abruptly stopped questioning him and began communicating by radio in English with colleagues aboard the nearby cutter shown in the video. “Since we were the only people who saw everything, we were afraid they might do something to us,” Darwin said. He felt the U.S. Coast Guard showed little interest in helping him locate his family and instead seemed more focused on “making sure we weren’t witnesses to anything.”
McCluskey says the multi-drone tactic—described by all three boats—reflects a U.S. doctrine. He argues it’s unlikely that other regional powers, from neighboring countries to organized crime groups, would have the budget or access for such technology. There is no known precedent of cartels using “eye-in-the-sky” surveillance drones deep in maritime territory, though the Coast Guard has also denied operating armed drones in Ecuadorian waters.
Furthermore, the decision to keep the survivors alive, albeit involving testimonies of torture, and the efforts and expenses to transport them, is far more reflective of a Department of Defense protocol—-designed to avoid international legal ramifications—than any organized crime group would typically care to practice. “If it was cartels, you would’ve never found them,” McCluskey said. “There would be no survivors to talk to, there would be no stories.”

## The Fiorella
The Fiorella was struck off the coast of the Galápagos on January 20; all eight fishermen aboard remain missing. The day before the vessel vanished, the captain’s wife received a call from her husband on an emergency line, warning that U.S. aircraft were orbiting overhead.
Drop Site obtained police interview transcripts from two eyewitnesses, Christian Flores and Dimas Ignacio Álvarez, who corroborated seeing the Fiorella engulfed in smoke and surrounded by American assets. The two men were members of the Fiorella crew but had been out setting a long line on a nearby raft for several hours when the vessel went up in smoke.
In their police statements, Flores and Álvarez described two U.S. aircraft flying over the Fiorella on January 18; multiple grey American drones and a U.S.-flagged patrol ship circling the vessel on January 19; and, on January 20—the day their crewmates disappeared—the large U.S.-flagged patrol ship near the smoke. From a distance, they could not make out the personnel aboard the ship, but their accounts echo those of the Negra Francisca crew, who said they were taken hostage by armed Americans aboard a U.S.-flagged patrol vessel. The witnesses’ descriptions also match aircraft and equipment featured in public posts by U.S. Southern Command.
After spotting the smoke, the two fishermen said they heard their crewmates calling the captain over the radio in distress. They were never seen again.
The attorney representing the two survivors of the Fiorella, Juan Avila, told Drop Site that the slain prosecutor, Alexandra Bravo, was in fact his niece.
The Coast Guard told Drop Site it “has no record of involvement with La Fiorella.”

## Bravo Is No Anomaly
The absence of an assigned police detail when Bravo was murdered bears similarities to the 2023 assassination of frontrunner presidential candidate Fernando Villavicencio. A congressional commission determined that Villavicencio’s police detail was insufficient, that he had been unconventionally escorted through an exposed street-level exit contrary to standard protocol, and that the armored vehicle designated to protect Villavicencio on the campaign trail had been left by his security team in another city that day. These breaches made him particularly vulnerable when assailants approached and shot him on the sidewalk as he was leaving a meeting with other government officials.
Villavicencio’s death cleared the way for now-President Daniel Noboa’s campaign—which had been polling at 3%—to surge to victory. In an interview with Señal Colombia, National Assembly legislator and member of Villavicencio’s party, Gisella Molina, who was with him and injured during the assassination, suggested government officials had prior knowledge of the plot.
During the 2024 murder investigation, Drop Site published private messages from then–Attorney General Diana Salazar revealing a plot to implicate former democratic socialist President Correa’s party in Villavicencio’s assassination, amid close collaboration with the U.S. ambassador.
The state later concluded that the Los Lobos cartel carried out Villavicencio’s murder and alleged that former members of Correa’s party were the masterminds. Prosecutors assert that Los Lobos killed Villavicencio for exposing their criminal network. While Villavicencio campaigned on eradicating the cartel economy, Ecuador under Noboa—accused of offering organized crime bosses immunity in exchange for electoral support—has risen as the top distribution hub for 70% of the world’s cocaine.
Immediately following Bravo’s death, the Attorney General issued a public statement attributing her murder to retaliation against prosecutors combating organized crime. When asked why authorities had linked the killing to organized crime and whether investigators had uncovered any information about Bravo’s missing police protection detail, the Attorney General’s office told Drop Site the investigation is under seal and declined to comment.
Though the attorney general has yet to present evidence to support their claim, Bravo lamented to the Human Rights Watch that “danger was always present” in her work. “She said that being a prosecutor in a context of organized crime was complex and risky, but she did not provide any further details,” the researcher told Drop Site. Manta sits at the epicenter of Ecuador’s organized crime crisis, as the small South American country becomes the most violent nation in the Western Hemisphere.
Bravo was also responsible for looking into the unsolved 2024 disappearance of the Patricia Lynn ship and its 21 crew members.
Bravo is the second person associated with the Patricia Lynn case to be assassinated. The first was the mother-in-law of one of the disappeared fishermen who became the spokesperson for the victims’ families and organized marches demanding answers for their missing relatives. María Chóez was fatally shot by two armed assailants while operating her street food stand in downtown Manta.
The Human Rights Watch researcher says the sinking of the Patricia Lynn boat in Ecuadorian waters, “served as a precedent in all these ship-related matters.”
“If Ecuador had a framework of trust in its institutions, one might think [Bravo’s murder] was an ordinary crime,” Vintimilla Jarrin, the former lawmaker, said. “But given the systematic violence against judges, prosecutors, and lawyers, there isn’t much room to give them the benefit of the doubt. Twenty-six murdered members of the justice system is a shocking number. And of course, this entire crisis has been fostered by an agenda driven directly by government authorities; the ones who benefit from organized crime are the large power groups.”

reads.title: How to Short Earnings Volatility With Unusual Whales API
reads.subtitle: Shorting Earnings Volatility With Defined Risk
reads.body:
Hey all! Nicholas from the Unusual Whales team, here!
In this issue, we’re bringing to you a banger write-up by our own Dan Wagner covering the potential of the Unusual Whales Earnings Vol Scan Skill. The general concept revolves around shorting earnings volatility in a risk-defined way.

-
- While myriad options strategies exist, this concept lies in utilizing calendar spreads, versus the popular short straddle. Using an AI Assistant alongside the Unusual Whales API and Earnings Vol Scan Skill, Dan outlines how this risk-defined strategy works, and walks us through how to set it up in just a few short, easy-to-follow steps, so check it out below!

## Shorting Earnings Volatility With Defined Risk: How to Use the Unusual Whales Earnings Vol Scan Skill

## TL;DR
Options that span an earnings date systematically price in bigger move than what is usually realized, and sellers of that event risk get paid the difference. This is known as the earnings variance risk premium, and this Skill hands your AI assistant a ready-to-run scanner that finds calendar spread setups to capture that risk premium with a defined, known-in-advance max loss. Copy the prompt below then paste it to your AI assistant to learn the method and generate trade ideas in a single session or review the Skill yourself here:
https://unusualwhales.com/skills/uw-earnings-vol-scan-skill.md

## A Prompt to Get You Started

> The Unusual Whales team created this Skill to identify interesting opportunities to short earnings volatility in a risk-defined way: “https://unusualwhales.com/skills/uw-earnings-vol-scan-skill.md”. The Skill file is long (2000+ lines), so make sure you access the entire file! Read the Skill (store a local copy if possible) then interactively work through these steps with me: (1) provide a short summary explaining why this strategy might have a durable edge, (2) concisely explain the filtering techniques it uses with as little jargon as possible, then (3) stand up and run the scanner the Skill provides, confirm its selftest passes, then review the returned trade ideas with me.

## Capturing the Earnings Variance Risk Premium
Earnings announcements are known catalysts on a known date as management releases new information to the market.
Since these announcements typically occur during illiquid post-market or pre-market sessions, the price of the underlying stock has a lot of potential to “gap” or “jump”. Options expiring right after the report price in an expected move, and on average the move that realizes is smaller than the move that was implied. This difference is the earnings variance risk premium, which is what the Skill is designed to harvest.
The earnings variance risk premium is not a fringe idea.
It is widely documented in professional options literature:

- Positional Option Trading (2020) by Euan Sinclair (Chapter 5, “Finding Trades with Positive Expected Value”)

- Trading Volatility (2014) by Colin Bennett (Chapter 6 Section 4, “Trading Earnings Announcements / Jumps”)

- The Volatility Edge in Options Trading (2008) by Jeff Augen (Chapter 7, “Trading the Earnings Cycle”)

## Why the Risk Premium Exists: Options as Insurance
A long option acts like portfolio insurance, and insurance pricing must make sellers money on average (or else no one would sell insurance):

- Long the stock? Buy Puts to cap your downside risk at the strike price minus the contract price.

- Short the stock? Buy Calls to cap your upside risk at the strike price minus the contract price.
Options are priced right most of the time; I have (somewhat jokingly but not really) heard the options market referred to as “the smart guy Olympics”.
But around earnings, market participants looking for protection bid up the price of options, and sellers willing to take that risk are paid the average difference between the expected move and the realized move.

## Structure: calendar spreads vs. short straddles
The obvious way to capture any variance risk premium (earnings or not) is with a short straddle; selling both the at-the-money Call and the at-the-money Put.

-
- Selling straddles works, but the risk is theoretically undefined as a large price gap can cause a catastrophic loss. (You can learn more about the short straddle structure here: https://unusualwhales.com/option-strategies/short-straddle.)
This Skill uses a long calendar spread as well, which comes with tradeoffs:

- Positive: long calendar spreads (sell the front expiry, buy the back expiry) have a max loss of the debit paid to enter the trade

- Negative: long calendar spreads are not a perfect bet on implied volatility, they are a bet that the elevated implied move does not materialize and that the term structure normalizes after the report
Remember that “defined risk” is not “low risk”; if the stock price moves sharply away from your strike, you will lose money.

## A Real Setup: CHWY in June 2026
CHWY reported earnings before the open on June 10, 2026. Late on June 9 the stock sat at 20.58, and the market was pricing a large one-day move of roughly 13%. Obviously that “fear” was concentrated in the closest expiry, which was June 12, 2026.
Here is the term-structure inversion the scanner hunts, in one real quote:

- Sell the 06/12/2026 22.5 Call: implied vol at 168%, collect 0.56

- Buy the 07/17/2026 22.5 Call: implied vol near 69%, pay 1.16

- Net debit per calendar spread: 0.60 ($60 before transaction and exchange fees), which is the max loss
What actually happened is the whole argument for this structure.
The CHWY price fell after earnings and moved away from the strike, the direction this position least wanted. However, the collapse in the short-dated Call’s premium was significant enough that the full structure could be closed for 0.62, marginally above the entry cost and enough to cover the round-trip transaction costs for a scratch. The maximum loss would hurt, but it will never be more than the cost of the position (plus fees).
Two practical notes on the strike choice. First, astute readers are likely asking, “Why the 22.5 strike instead of the 20 strike, which was closer to (but below) the spot price at the time?” The answer lies in real-world execution.
The 22.5 strike had significantly tighter bid-ask spreads, which is important for a two-leg structure that has to cross the spread 4 times over its life. Market quality can matter more than centering the strikes perfectly, especially in names with fewer strikes and lower volume.
Second, the tradeoff created by the 22.5 strike choice. Shifting strikes further above the spot price introduces a bullish directional lean. Selecting the at-the-money strike does a better job isolating the volatility target of this trade since vega is highest at-the-money.

## Run It
The Skill calls the Unusual Whales API, so you need API access to run step 3 of the prompt.
If you have not subscribed yet, you can start with an API trial subscription here:
https://unusualwhales.com/pricing?product=api
As of July 19 2026, the first 7 days of trial subscriptions are free, and you can cancel anytime during that window without paying a cent.
You will need to register a credit card to start the trial subscription, and if you do not cancel before the trial ends, it will convert into the paid trial plan at $50 per week.
Make sure you have your API key ready, since the Skill needs it to successfully fetch data from the Unusual Whales API.
Send the prompt to your AI assistant, ask questions at each step, and you will walk away with two things: (1) a working understanding of the earnings variance risk premium and (2) a trade idea generator running on your own key.

## Credit Where Credit is Due
The filter thresholds in this Skill were derived from a backtest published on the Volatility Vibes YouTube channel here:
The presenter packs a lot of valuable insight into a 19 minute video, and it is well worth a view.
As with any single published backtest, validate the logic against your own assessment and data before committing capital to any strategy.
Educational content, not investment advice. The scanner surfaces ideas to research, not recommendations. Options carry risk, including the loss of the full premium paid.
NOTE: This post is not financial advice. The stock market is risky, and any trade or investment is expected to have some, or total, loss. Please do research before any trade. Do not use this information for investment decisions. Check terms on site for full terms. Agree to terms before considering this information.

reads.title: Israel‘s Secret Sales Pitch to Provide Surveillance Drones to the UAE
reads.subtitle: Internal emails and documents reveal how Israel’s Elbit Systems worked to supply the UAE with drones and other weapons.
reads.body:
As a reader-funded independent news outlet, we operate free from the influence of governments, advertisers, and corporate backers. This is essential to our mission: to report on what matters most, beholden only to the truth. In that spirit, we made a commitment to ensure that our journalism is free for everyone, not locked behind a paywall. But that means we rely on the voluntary support of our community of readers. Please consider making a tax-deductible donation to support our work today.
Subscribe now

-
- An Elbit Hermes 900 unmanned aerial vehicle is seen at Israel’s Palmachim Air Force Base, on July 5, 2023. Photo by Jack Guez / AFP via Getty Images.On May 12, U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee publicly disclosed a significant development in the military relationship between Israel and the United Arab Emirates amid the war in Iran.
“Israel just sent [the UAE] Iron Dome batteries and personnel to help operate them,” Huckabee said at an event in Tel Aviv. Huckabee described the deployment as a fruit of the Abraham Accords, calling the Israeli-Emirati relationship “extraordinary.”
The deployment—as Iranian missiles and drones targeted the region in response to a joint U.S.-Israeli attack—marked the first publicly acknowledged presence of Israeli military personnel and air-defense equipment inside a Gulf monarchy. But the integration of Israeli weapons into the UAE’s defenses did not begin with the Iran war.
An archive drawn from the email account of Vered Haimovich, a former Israeli military officer who became vice president of Elbit Systems’ UAV Systems Business Unit in January 2021, shows how the arms company worked in the aftermath of the Abraham Accords to create a channel for the sale of drones and aerial surveillance equipment to Abu Dhabi.
The email archive includes internal documents from Elbit and its Emirati subsidiary, as well as documents identified as request lists from the UAE military to Elbit in the context of negotiating weapons deals. Drop Site conducted cryptographic verification on the email address signatures and also verified non-public contact information for parties referenced in the documents.
The email archive was published by Distributed Denial of Secrets and released by Handala, an online hacking group presumed to be tied to the Iranian Ministry of Intelligence. The archive consists of personal messages, newsletters, and advertisements from Haimovich’s Gmail account. But it also contains a smaller collection of Elbit correspondence that executives from the company sent to her personal account—along with Elbit documents Haimovich forwarded to her own Gmail account from her Elbit address.
The Elbit emails, dating from late 2021 through early 2023, include a detailed April 2022 proposal from Elbit Systems Emirates subsidiary to provide a suite of Hermes 900 drones with supporting equipment and logistical support to Abu Dhabi. The proposal lays out the terms of a deal that would see the Israeli defense manufacturer provide the UAE two Hermes 900 systems comprising six aircraft, SkEye wide-area surveillance sensors, ground-control equipment, training, and logistical support.
The proposal identifies Elbit Systems Ltd. as the seller and says the package was intended to meet an “Urgent Operational Requirement” of the UAE. The initial package offered six aircraft and supporting systems for $154 million with additional upgrades that would raise its total value to approximately $225 million.

-
- From an Elbit Systems Emirates proposal for a Hermes 900 drone system included in the Gmail account of Vered Haimovich, vice president of Elbit Systems’ UAV Systems Business Unit.Other documents also point to a broader Emirati interest in airborne intelligence and electronic-warfare capabilities provided by Israeli firms. One photographed document, labeled “Confidential” and titled “Airborne SIGINT Wish List,” describes itself as a UAE Armed Forces request for two manned and two unmanned signals-intelligence aircraft. The request sought systems capable of intercepting cellular and satellite communications and conducting electronic attacks involving cyber operations, lasers, and high-power microwave technology.
Neither Elbit nor the Emirati government has publicly confirmed that the UAE has acquired or currently operates Hermes drones, and the documents available in the archive do not include a final purchase order or delivery record, although internal correspondence repeatedly described the Emirati requirements at the time as urgent and stated that an agreement could close within weeks.
Despite public proclamations of the close relationship between the two countries by both Emirati and Israeli officials, specific details of their defense relationship have remained largely hidden from the public.
In 2025, it was reported that the UAE’s Edge Group was in talks with Elbit to purchase the Hermes 900 in a deal that would include “transfer of technology and localized production,” from Tel Aviv to Abu Dhabi, marking a rare public acknowledgement of an opaque defense relationship that has slowly been coming out of the shadows since the signing of the Abraham Accords in 2020.
Reached for comment, Elbit Systems stated that it “does not comment on business matters relating to its customers,” but added, “the materials presented do not accurately reflect the company’s business activities.” The company did not respond to follow-up questions.
The Emirati embassy and Ministry of Defense did not respond to a request for comment.

## “We need to move quickly”
On November 14, 2021, Elbit publicly announced that it had established Elbit Systems Emirates as a subsidiary that would pursue “long-term cooperation” with the UAE Armed Forces, customize systems for Emirati requirements, and lead technology transfers to the country.
At the time, both countries were still basking in the glow of the recently signed Abraham Accords, which had helped set the stage for a more overt partnership.
“The Abraham Accords provide a sound basis for business collaborations in the region,” Elbit executive Ran Kril said in the company’s announcement. Five days earlier, internal correspondence from Haimovich’s inbox indicated that Elbit had already received preliminary policy authorization to pursue a Hermes 900 sale to the UAE in a restricted configuration.
A November 9 email, written by Elbit executive Michael Edelstein, summarized a meeting the previous day between Elbit CEO Bezhalel Machlis and the head of the Israeli Defense Ministry’s Defense Export Controls Agency. Under the heading “United Arab Emirates,” Edelstein wrote that the official had given permission to proceed with a “900” drone in an imaging-only configuration. The UAE was also described as an important prospective customer for Israeli arms, though development of the relationship would depend on political conditions. “The potential is considerable, but for internal and external strategic reasons, progress will not be comprehensive immediately,” Edelstein wrote.
The email also mentioned a list of candidates for weapons exports to other Gulf Arab states, including Saudi Arabia, for whom a C-130 aircraft upgrade is noted in the email as “approved to proceed,” along with artillery equipment for the Saudi military.
The Israeli Defense Export Controls Agency, the email continued, had approved the sales to Riyadh so long as the artillery equipment did not match planned IDF military upgrades, and despite concerns that “development of relations is progressing slowly” with Saudi Arabia, which is not a signatory to the Abraham Accords and does not maintain official relations with Israel.
Qatar is also listed in the email as approved for the sale of an aircraft protection countermeasure system known as DIRCM, as well as additional signals intelligence equipment to Bahrain.
The Qatari, Saudi, and Bahraini embassies did not respond to requests for comment.
The same email also addresses the possibility of receiving future export authorization for the sale of offensive weapons for the UAE. The first was Elbit’s MPR 2000, a 2,000-pound air-dropped penetrator bomb designed to break through reinforced concrete before exploding. The second was the SkyStriker—known in Hebrew as “Shrakrak”—an Elbit loitering munition, or explosive attack drone, designed to circle over an area before diving into a target.
“Pay attention to the 900,” Elbit executive Yoram Shmuely wrote when forwarding the summary to Haimovich. “We need to move quickly.”
Drop Site is reader-supported. Consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
The drone effort formed part of a broader opening that was rapidly producing publicly announced defense partnerships between Abu Dhabi and Tel Aviv. Four days after Elbit announced its Emirati subsidiary, the UAE’s EDGE Group and Israel Aerospace Industries signed a memorandum of understanding to jointly design a series of 17-meter unmanned surface vessels. The proposed vessels would support intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance; border patrol; mine detection and sweeping; submarine detection and anti-submarine warfare; and maritime-security operations, according to the companies’ announcement.
On January 3, 2022, Elbit announced its first publicly disclosed contract through the Emirati subsidiary: a five-year, approximately $53 million agreement to supply directed infrared countermeasures and electronic-warfare self-protection systems for the UAE Air Force’s Airbus A330 tanker transport aircraft.
But that public contract was narrower than the drone and intelligence package Elbit was developing privately.
The UAE’s security situation changed dramatically later that month. On January 17, Yemen’s Ansarallah movement claimed a missile-and-drone attack on Abu Dhabi. Explosions engulfed three fuel tankers near an Abu Dhabi National Oil Company storage facility, killing three people and wounding six; a separate fire broke out at an extension of Abu Dhabi International Airport. A week later, the UAE said its defenses had intercepted and destroyed two Houthi ballistic missiles targeting Abu Dhabi.
By March, internal correspondence described the Emirati project as urgent, and an Elbit planning memorandum said the system was intended to detect missile and drone launches from beyond the UAE’s borders.
“They want the SkEye with the 900,” Hagi Topolansky, then an Elbit senior vice president responsible for UAVs and strategic affairs and a former deputy commander of the Israeli Air Force, wrote in a March 8 email. The passage appeared under “Arig,” a designation that other documents connect to the UAE. Topolansky relayed an unnamed official’s assessment that the transaction would close “within a few weeks,” adding that the official was highly optimistic and that the customer was “under pressure.”
In a separate line, Topolansky wrote that an unidentified customer “really wants” a laser system and that discussions were progressing well. The email did not identify the customer, the laser product, or its price.
On March 13, emails show that Elbit executive Amir Bettesh circulated a planning memorandum to push forward a deal. The memorandum described an initial proposal for five complete Hermes 900 systems for the UAE—three aircraft per system, or 15 aircraft in total. Each system would include electro-optical sensors with laser target designators, daytime and nighttime SkEye systems, self-protection and electronic-warfare equipment, along with ground equipment and training, noting that a “significant discount” had been applied to the proposed sale at customer request.
According to the memorandum, the systems were intended to maintain surveillance beyond the customer’s borders and detect missile and drone launches into the country, but could also be used domestically for “homeland security” missions. The deal was portrayed in the document as queuing up a much larger line of business, stating that “in the next phase the customer intends to procure 15 systems in total—an additional 10 systems beyond the urgent operational requirement (UOR) described above—which will incorporate a broader range of mission payloads.”
The memorandum stated that the technical specifications, statement of work, financial offer, draft contract, and executive summary had already been delivered to the customer and were “ready for signature.”

## Wish List
While the documents in Haimovich’s correspondence show that Elbit was pursuing a substantial Hermes 900 sale to the UAE in 2022 and record detailed Emirati operational requirements they do not confirm whether Abu Dhabi executed the sale at the time or received delivery of the systems.
Other correspondence contained in the archive indicate that talks were proceeding for the provision of Israeli-made UAVs and a much broader range of aerial surveillance and electronic warfare equipment to the Emirates.
On February 28, 2023, two short emails were sent from Haimovich’s personal Gmail account to her Elbit address. The subjects of the emails were listed as “Johan 1” and “Johan 2” and the underlying documents include metadata indicating that they were created in July 2022. The attachment in the email “Johan 1” is a photographed document marked confidential and titled “Airborne SIGINT Wish List.” The document describes itself as a UAE Armed Forces request to acquire two manned and two unmanned signals-intelligence aircraft. It asked that delivery of the initial aircraft, intelligence systems, and supporting equipment begin within 42 months of a contract’s initiation.

-
- An “Airborne SIGINT Wish List” included in the Gmail account of Vered Haimovich, vice president of Elbit Systems’ UAV Systems Business Unit.The requested aircraft referenced in the document would combine communications intelligence, electronic intelligence, imagery intelligence, electronic attack, cyber-surveillance, and artificial-intelligence capabilities. The electronic-attack requirement included “cyber/laser/HPM attack.” A separate technical document defines “HPM” as high-power microwave.
The document attached to “Johan 2” appears to be a detailed vendor response to the wish list in the first email. The document is marked as unclassified as standalone but classified secret when viewed in conjunction with other information and is labelled as “Commercial in Confidence”—a classification often used to refer to commercially sensitive material. The document proposes possible configurations for large and small manned aircraft and unmanned aircraft, as well as cellular and satellite-communications interception and electronic warfare capabilities.

-
- A “request for information” included in the Gmail account of Vered Haimovich, vice president of Elbit Systems’ UAV Systems Business Unit.The correspondence continues with emails—including “Johan 3” and “Johan 4”—containing password-protected draft files whose contents are not visible in the hacked email archive.

## “More relevant and stronger”
The internal Elbit proposals and correspondence concerning the UAE and the sale of Hermes 900 systems and other aerial surveillance tools to Abu Dhabi emerged amid a rapidly expanding Israeli-Emirati military relationship that had evolved after the Abraham Accords from diplomatic normalization into increasingly open defense cooperation.
By September 2022, Reuters reported that Israel had agreed to sell the UAE a SPYDER air-defense system, citing sources familiar with the agreement. Neither government publicly confirmed the details at the time. In 2023, Israel’s Ministry of Defense inaugurated its first national pavilion at the IDEX arms exhibition in Abu Dhabi with more than 30 Israeli companies displaying air-defense systems, drones, artificial intelligence, electro-optics, and cyber technology.
In November 2025, Elbit announced an eight-year, $2.3 billion contract for an unnamed international customer. One month later, Calcalist reported, citing the French publication Intelligence Online, that the customer was the UAE.
The Iron Dome deployment during the 2026 Iran war represents yet another evolution in a relationship that has continued to blossom despite the genocide in Gaza and a regional war triggered by Israel and the U.S., bringing Israeli equipment and personnel to operate inside the Emirates during an active conflict.
Despite keeping many details of its defense cooperation with Israel secret, the UAE has become more vocal about its attachment to Tel Aviv, describing its relationship as one based on shared values and interests.
“Everything that the UAE does with Israel is formal, above board,” said Emirati presidential advisor Anwar Gargash in an interview this May. “We don’t have to find secret channels to do that, and I feel that that relationship is going to be even stronger, and the Israeli relationship is more relevant and stronger.”

reads.title: Israel Firebombed a Family Home Where Children Were Sleeping in Latest Killing Spree
reads.subtitle: As the world focuses on the renewed U.S. war with Iran, Israel has killed nearly 60 Palestinians over the past week and moved to occupy close to 70 percent of Gaza.
reads.body:
Drop Site is a reader-funded, independent news outlet. Without your support, we can’t operate. Please consider becoming a paid subscriber or making a 501(c)(3) tax-deductible donation today.
Subscribe now

-
- The Al-Masri family home in Gaza City after it was bombed by the Israeli military, killing a couple and their four children as they slept on July 21, 2026. Gaza City. Screenshot of video by Abdel Qader Sabbah.Story by Abdel Qader Sabbah, Mohamed Ahmed, Sharif Abdel Kouddous, and Jawa Ahmad
GAZA CITY—The charred shell of the Al-Masri family home in the Sabra neighborhood of Gaza City was still smoldering on Tuesday afternoon, hours after the Israel military bombed it, killing Firas and Salsabeel al-Masri and their four children—Faryal, Salma, Amira and Naim—as they slept.
The airstrike came without warning in the middle of the night, destroying the upper floor of the simple two-story structure and setting it ablaze. “We were asleep in the middle of the night, at around 2 a.m. or so, when we heard a huge explosion,” Abu Youssef Al-Masri, the children’s grandfather, told Drop Site as he stood in front of the partially collapsed home. “We realized the house had been struck. The house collapsed and caught fire.”
The fire spared nothing inside, family belongings burnt to ash lay among broken cinder blocks, the walls that remained standing blackened with soot.
“The house burned completely. It was my brother’s home—he, his wife, and their four children. Burned until it was charred. My brother’s entire family has been erased,” Mohammed Al-Masri, the brother of Firas, said. “They burned before our eyes and we couldn’t do anything.” He spoke standing at the graveyard where the family of six were buried on Tuesday afternoon.
The bodies were carried by relatives wrapped in white shrouds through the rubble-strewn cemetery to be laid to rest. Abu Youssef stood in the middle of the shallow graves and placed the small body of his granddaughter, Amira, next to her mother as Israeli drones buzzed incessantly overhead. “The whole world is watching us,” Mohammed said. “There is no ceasefire in effect, the war hasn’t stopped, and no one cares about us.”

## Relatives bury Firas and Salsabeel al-Masri and their four children after they were killed in an Israeli airstrike on their home in Gaza City on July 21, 2026. Video by Abdel Qader Sabbah.

The attack on Tuesday came amid a particularly brutal and escalated Israeli assault across Gaza over the past several days as the world’s attention has been distracted by the renewed U.S. war with Iran. Daily airstrikes, shelling, quadcopter attacks, and shootings have targeted residential buildings, tent encampments, civilian vehicles, a funeral procession, a police station, and a hospital-turned-shelter, killing dozens of Palestinians across the enclave over the past week alone. At the same time, Israeli ground troops have been pushing further into Gaza, steadily extending the “yellow line” westward, taking more land, and driving the Palestinian population onto an ever-shrinking territory.
“It’s not simply that the resumption of the war in Iran provides cover, it’s also the fact that the war has largely been a failure from an Israeli perspective, and the Israeli state will look to compensate for this failure elsewhere before a new regional balance takes shape,” Nasser Abourahme, a professor of Middle Eastern and North African Studies at Bowdoin College, told Drop Site. “It’s most important to remember that the genocide itself has both stalled and never stopped. For all the horrific and unprecedented destruction and death, Israel hasn’t yet achieved any of its core aims: the ethnic cleansing of the Strip, the disarming of the resistance factions, or the resettlement of the Strip.”
The latest killing spree has brought the Palestinian death toll in Gaza since a so-called ceasefire went into effect in October 2025 to 1,180—including over 250 children—with 127 being killed in the first three weeks of July. Over 3,800 have been injured. The total recorded death toll since Israel launched its genocidal assault in October 2023 is now over 73,300 killed, with nearly 174,000 injured, according to Gaza’s health ministry.
On Monday, an Israeli airstrike slammed into the Al-Yemen Al-Saeed Hospital building in the Jabaliya refugee camp, killing at least four people and wounding several more. Like many hospitals in Gaza, the facility entirely ceased functioning during the war and is instead being used primarily as a shelter for displaced Palestinians.
“I went out to visit my friend near Al-Yemen Al-Saeed and suddenly there was a very large explosion, two consecutive explosions,” Youssef Akasha, an eyewitness who was just meters away from the attack, told Drop Site as he stood outside Shifa Hospital in Gaza City where the dead and wounded were being brought. Bloodied children were carried out of ambulances while bodies wrapped in blankets were put on gurneys. “The children were having fun, playing football, and suddenly they started screaming. We went directly to Al-Yemen Al-Saeed…we found the place destroyed and children were lying on the ground, women screaming, and men running to rescue the wounded.”
One of the worst attacks came on Friday, when Israel bombed a funeral procession outside the Ahmed Yassin Mosque in the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza, killing at least eight mourners as they gathered to bury a man killed just hours earlier. Bodies lay strewn on the blood-soaked ground. One man was blown in half, his legs torn off his body as crowds of people screaming on the street tried to rescue the wounded. At Al-Awda hospital, injured children lay wide-eyed and silent on hospital beds as doctors rushed to treat them. One man knelt and embraced a bloodied corpse lying on a gurney, unable to let go.
“It was a very big attack and there was a large number of martyrs,” Medhat Saleh, an eyewitness who was wounded in his right arm, told Drop Site. “We couldn’t have imagined they would bomb a funeral of this size. Many children, women, and men…A massacre in every sense of the word. The people were piled on top of each other, torn apart.” He continued, “It’s gotten much, much worse. In recent days, this has become a daily occurrence.”
The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Thameen Al-Kheetan, made note of the escalated Israel assault in a statement on Tuesday. “The Israeli military has intensified its attacks in Gaza in recent days, killing and injuring dozens of Palestinians—children, women and men…Nine months after the announcement of a ceasefire, still, nowhere is safe for Palestinians in Gaza,” Kheetan said, noting that the UN had documented 57 Palestinians killed between July 13 and July 20 alone. “Meanwhile, the Palestinian population in Gaza remains trapped in an ever-shrinking area, with the ‘yellow line’ constantly being moved westwards by the Israeli occupying power, presenting a continuous threat to life as the Israeli military appears to routinely fire on Palestinians for mere presence in the vicinity of that line…The violations, the suffering and the misery that continue to be imposed on the Palestinians in Gaza cannot be ignored.”
As part of the October 2025 agreement, Israeli troops withdrew to the “yellow line,” a boundary running roughly parallel to the coastline and cutting off large swathes of north and south Gaza, that gave Israel control of 53% of the enclave. The move was supposed to mark the beginning of an eventual phased withdrawal back to a “buffer zone” at the border with Israel. Yet over the past nine months, the Israeli military has instead steadily pushed further westward in areas along the yellow line, taking more Palestinian land and placing yellow concrete blocks in some places to indicate their new line of control, which is now estimated to encompass closer to 70% of Gaza, according to Israeli military officials.
“The escalation of the killing, the expansion of the so-called yellow line in new land grabs, and the agitation of politicians and the settler movement for renewed Jewish settlement in Gaza all point to the fact that Israel’s endgame remains the ethnic cleansing of Gaza and its full conquest one way or another,” Abourahme said. “At the end of the day, the so-called ceasefire didn’t stop the genocide, it only modulated its tempo and intensity.”
For the past several days, Israeli ground troops have launched a sustained attack on areas near the Zeitoun neighborhood in Gaza City, including aerial bombing, shooting, and shelling attacks, razing land with bulldozers, and issuing displacement orders to force residents to flee their homes and shelters and drive them eastward.
“Today, they moved the yellow line here. The day before, they bombed the area, so we left. We spent one more night at home, then we had to leave,” Umm Salem Dawla, a resident displaced from the area, told Drop Site. “We gathered our belongings and left them at the camp. I keep saying I’ll go and sit by the cemetery. What can I tell you? What kind of life is this?”
On Wednesday, the troops pulled back and residents in the area found yellow concrete blocks placed at the Dawlah junction on Salah al-Din street—the main north-south thoroughfare running the length of the enclave.

## The Israeli military forced residents to flee from the Zeitoun neighborhood in Gaza City and placed yellow blocks on Salah al-Din street on July 22, 2026. Video by Abdel Qader Sabbah.

“The Israelis started shelling the area, tanks started firing at us and at our home so we fled because the situation was extremely difficult…the tanks are always visible in the street, firing at our homes, and the quadcopters are constantly overhead. They don’t leave us alone. Twenty four hours a day there is shelling and gunfire,” Assem Dawla, another displaced resident of Zeitoun, said. “As you can see, we’re now taking out our belongings and leaving because the occupation has advanced the yellow line to Salah al-Din street. There is no longer any possibility of life here. Life in Zeitoun has been wiped out. There is no hope left and no way to live here anymore.”
The Israeli military’s encroachment to the Dawlah junction in effect prevents Palestinians in this area of Gaza City from accessing Salah al-Din road and the rest of the enclave further south.
“My fear is that all of Gaza will end up inside the occupation’s new boundaries. Netanyahu is now talking about taking 67% to 70% of the Gaza Strip, but I believe he wants to control all of it. There won’t be anywhere left for us. We’ll all be living under the control and domination of the Israeli army,” Dawla said. “The war is not over. We’re still living in a state of fear, greater even than when the war was ongoing.”
Sami Vanderlip edited the videos for this report.
